Moses smeared some of its blood on Aaron's right earlobe, some on his right thumb, and some on the big toe of his right foot. 24Moses did the same thing for Aaron's sons, before splattering the rest of the blood against the four sides of the altar. 25He took the animal's fat tail, the fat on its insides, and the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and the right hind leg. 26Then he took from a basket some of each of the three kinds of bread that had been made without yeast and had been dedicated to the Lord.
27Moses placed the bread on top of the meat and gave it all to Aaron and his sons, who lifted it up to show that it was dedicated to the Lord. 28After this, Moses placed it on the fires of the altar and sent it up in smoke with a smell that pleased the Lord. This was part of the ordination ceremony. 29Moses lifted up the choice ribs of the ram to show that they were dedicated to the Lord. This was the part that the Lord had said Moses could have.
30Finally, Moses sprinkled the priestly clothes of Aaron and his sons with some of the oil for ordination and with some of the blood from the altar. So Aaron and his sons, together with their priestly clothes, were dedicated to the Lord.
31Moses said to Aaron and his sons:
The Lord told me that you must boil this meat at the entrance to the sacred tent and eat it there with the bread. 32Burn what is left over 33and stay near the entrance to the sacred tent until the ordination ceremony ends seven days from now. 34We have obeyed the Lord in everything that has been done today, so that your sins may be forgiven. 35The Lord has told me that you must stay near the entrance to the tent for seven days and nights, or else you will die.
36Aaron and his sons obeyed everything that the Lord had told Moses they must do.
translation_text:
Mose hyɛ Aaron ne ne mma asɔfoɔ
(Eksodɔs 29.1-37)
1 Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 2Fa Aaron ne ne mma ka ne ho, ɛne ntadeɛ no ne sra ngo no, ne bɔne ho afɔdeɛ nantwinini no ne adwennini mmienu no ne apiti kɛntɛn no. 3Na ma asafo no nyinaa mmɔ dwa, ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano. 4Na Mose yɛɛ sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ no no, na ɔmaa asafo no bɔɔ dwa, ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano. 5Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ asafo no sɛ: Yei ne adeɛ a AWURADE ahyɛ sɛ wɔnyɛ. 6Na Mose de Aaron ne ne mma no bae, na ɔde nsuo hohoroo wɔn ho; 7na ɔde atadeɛ yuu no hyɛɛ no, na ɔde aboomu no bɔɔ n’asene, na ɔde batakari no hyɛɛ no, na ɔde asɔfotadeɛ no hyɛɛ no, na ɔde asɔfotadeɛ no nkyekyeremu no bɔɔ no abɔsoɔ; 8 na ɔde adaaboɔ no hyehyɛɛ no, na ɔde Urim ne Tumim no hyɛɛ adaaboɔ no mu; 9 na ɔde abotitene no bɔɔ ne ti, na ɔde sikaterɛ no, kronkronyɛ ahyehyɛdeɛ no, fam abotitene no anim sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no. 10 Na Mose faa sra ngo no de sraa tenabea no ne deɛ ɛwɔ mu nyinaa, na ɔyɛɛ no kronkron; 11na ɔde bi petee afɔrebukyia no so mprɛnson, na ɔsraa afɔrebukyia no ne ɛho nnoɔma nyinaa ne kuduo no ne ntaaseɛ no ngo de yɛɛ no kronkron. 12Na ɔhwiee sra ngo no bi guu Aaron atifi sraa no ngo de yɛɛ no kronkron. 13Na Mose de Aaron mma no nso bae, na ɔhyehyɛɛ wɔn ntadeɛ, na ɔde aboomu bobɔ wɔn mu, na ɔde abotire bobɔɔ wɔn, sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no.
14 Na ɔmaa wɔde bɔne ho afɔdeɛ nantwinini no bae, na Aaron ne ne mma no de wɔn nsa guu bɔne afɔdeɛ nantwinini no atifi. 15Na Mose kumm no, na ɔde ne nsateaa kaa mogya no bi kekaa afɔrebukyia no mmɛn ho hyiae, na ɔyii afɔrebukyia no ho bɔne, na ɔhwiee mogya no petee afɔrebukyia no ase de dwiraa sɛ ɔde repata so. 16Na ɔfaa sradeɛ a ɛwɔ ayamdeɛ no ho nyinaa ne mmerɛboɔ so ntentan no ne sawa mmienu no ne ɛho sradeɛ, na Mose hyee no afɔrebukyia no so. 17Na nantwinini no ara ne ne nwoma ne ne nam ne n’agyanan no, ɔde ogya hyee, nsraban no akyi, sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no.
18 Na ɔde ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ dwennini no bae, na Aaron ne ne mma de wɔn nsa guu odwennini no atifi. 19Na ɔkum no, na Mose hwiee mogya no petee afɔrebukyia no so hyiae, 20na ɔtwitwaa odwennini no mu asinasini, na Mose too tire no ne asinasini no ne sradeɛ no mu gya. 21Na n’ayamdeɛ ne ne nnyawa no, ɔde nsuo hohoroo ho. Na Mose too odwennini mu no nyinaa mu gya, afɔrebukyia no so; ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ a ɛyi hwa hwanhwam ne no, AWURADE gya afɔdeɛ ne no, sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no.
22 Na ɔde odwennini a ɔtɔ so mmienu no, atuhoakyɛ afɔdeɛ dwennini no bae, na Aaron ne ne mma no de wɔn nsa guu odwennini no atifi. 23Na Mose kumm no, na ɔfaa ne mogya no bi de kaa Aaron aso nifa ano ne ne nsa nifa kokurobetie ne ne nan nifa kokurobetie ano. 24Na ɔde Aaron mma no bae, na Mose de mogya no bi kekaa wɔn aso nifa ano ne wɔn nsa nifa kokurobetie ne wɔn nan nifa kokurobetie ano; na Mose hwiee mogya no petee afɔrebukyia no so hyiae. 25Na ɔfaa sradeɛ no ne sradedua no ne sradeɛ a ɛwɔ ayamdeɛ no ho nyinaa ne mmerɛboɔ so ntentan no ne sawa mmienu no ne ɛho sradeɛ ne srɛ nifa no, 26na ɔfaa apiti kɛntɛn a ɛsi AWURADE anim no mu apiti taterɛ baako ne ngo paanoo taterɛ baako ne ɔfam baako de guu sradeɛ ne srɛ nifa no so, 27na ɔde ne nyinaa hyɛɛ Aaron ne ne mma no nsa, na ɔhim yɛɛ ohim afɔdeɛ, AWURADE anim. 28Na Mose gyee wɔn nsam, na ɔtoo mu gya wɔ afɔrebukyia no so wɔ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ no so de yɛɛ atuhoakyɛ afɔdeɛ a ɛyi hwa hwanhwam; Ɛyɛ ogya afɔdeɛ ma AWURADE. 29Na Mose faa atuhoakyɛ afɔdeɛ dwennini no yan no, na ɔhim yɛɛ ohim afɔdeɛ AWURADE anim; ɛyɛɛ Mose dea, sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no.
30Na Mose faa sra ngo no bi ne afɔrebukyia no so mogya no bi de petee Aaron ne ne ntadeɛ ne ne mma ne ne mma ntadeɛ nyinaa so de dwiraa Aaron ne ne ntadeɛ ne ne mma ne ne mma ntadeɛ no. 31Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Aaron ne ne mma no sɛ: Monnoa nam no ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano, na monni no hɔ ara, ɛne atuhoakyɛ afɔdeɛ kɛntɛn no mu paanoo no, sɛdeɛ mehyɛɛ sɛ: Aaron ne ne mma nnie no. 32Na nam ne paanoo no mu deɛ ɛbɛka no, momfa ogya nhye. 33Na mommfiri ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano nnanson nkɔsi da a mo atuhoakyɛ nna no bɛwie duro, ɛfiri sɛ, nnanson na wɔde rehyɛ mo asɔfoɔ. 34Sɛdeɛ wɔreyɛ no nnɛ da yi no, AWURADE na ɔhyɛɛ sɛ wɔnyɛ mfa mpata mma mo. 35Na montena ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano awia ne anadwo nnanson, na monwɛn sɛdeɛ AWURADE ahyɛ no, na moanwuwu, na saa na wɔahyɛ me. 36Na Aaron ne ne mma no dii nsɛm a AWURADE nam Mose so hyɛeɛ no nyinaa so.

english_text:
The First Sacrifices Offered by Aaron and His Sons
1Eight days later Moses called together Aaron, his sons, and Israel's leaders. 2Then he said to Aaron:
Find a young bull and a ram that have nothing wrong with them. Offer the bull to the Lord as a sacrifice for sin and the ram as a sacrifice to please him.
3Tell the people of Israel that they must offer sacrifices as well. They must offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin, and a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to please the Lord. The bull and the ram must be a year old and have nothing wrong with them. 4Then the people must offer a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing and also a grain sacrifice mixed with oil. Do this, because the Lord will appear to you today.
5After the animals and the grain had been brought to the front of the sacred tent, and the people were standing there in the presence of the Lord, 6Moses said:
The Lord has ordered you to do this, so that he may appear to you in all of his glory. 7 Aaron, step up to the altar and offer the sacrifice to please the Lord, then offer the sacrifices for the forgiveness of your sins and for the sins of the people, just as the Lord has commanded.
8Aaron stepped up to the altar and killed the bull that was to be the sacrifice for his sins. 9His sons brought him the blood. He dipped a finger in it, smeared some on the four corners of the bronze altar, and poured out the rest at its foot. 10But he sent up in smoke the fat, the kidneys, and the lower part of the liver, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. 11Then Aaron burned the skin and the flesh outside the camp.
12After Aaron had killed the ram that was sacrificed to please the Lord, Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against all four sides of the altar. 13They brought him each piece of the animal, including the head, and he burned them all on the altar. 14He washed the insides and the hind legs and also sent them up in smoke.
15Next, Aaron sacrificed the goat for the sins of the people, as he had done with the sacrifice for his own sins. 16And so, he burned this sacrifice on the altar in the proper way. 17He also presented the grain sacrifice and burned a handful of the flour on the altar as part of the morning sacrifice.
18 Finally, he killed the bull and the ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing on the people. Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against the four sides of the altar. 19His sons placed all the fat, as well as the kidneys and the lower part of the liver 20on top of the choice ribs. 21Then Aaron burned the fat on the altar and lifted up the ribs and the right hind leg to show that these were dedicated to the Lord. This was done just as the Lord had instructed Moses.
22 Aaron held out his hand and gave the people his blessing, before coming down from the bronze altar where he had offered the sacrifices. 23He and Moses went into the sacred tent, and when they came out, they gave the people their blessing. Then the Lord appeared to the people in all of his glory. 24The Lord sent fiery flames that burned up everything on the altar, and when everyone saw this, they shouted and fell to their knees to worship the Lord.
translation_text:
Asɔfoɔ no hyɛ wɔn adwuma ase
1 Na da a ɛtɔ so nwɔtwe no Mose frɛɛ Aaron ne ne mma no ne Israel mpanimfoɔ, 2na ɔka kyerɛɛ Aaron sɛ: Fa nantwie ba a wode bɛyɛ bɔne ho afɔdeɛ ne odwennini a wode bɛyɛ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ, wɔnni mu, na fa bra AWURADE anim. 3Na Israelfoɔ no nso, kasa kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Momfa ɔpapo mmɛyɛ bɔne ho afɔdeɛ ne nantwie ba ne odwanten ba a wɔadi afe afe a wɔdi mu mmɛyɛ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ, 4ne nantwinini ne odwennini mmɛyɛ asomdwoeɛ afɔdeɛ, na wɔmfa mmɔ afɔdeɛ AWURADE anim ne aduane afɔdeɛ a wɔagu so ngo, ɛfiri sɛ ɛnnɛ na AWURADE bɛyi ne ho akyerɛ mo. 5Na wɔde deɛ Mose hyɛeɛ no baa ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no anim, na asafo no nyinaa twe bae bɛgyinaa AWURADE anim. 6Na Mose kaa sɛ: Yei ne asɛm a AWURADE hyɛeɛ no, monyɛ, na AWURADE animuonyam nyi ne ho nkyerɛ mo. 7 Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Aaron sɛ: Twe pini afɔrebukyia no ho, na bɔ wo hyeɛ afɔdeɛ ne wo bɔne ho afɔdeɛ, na pata ma wo ho ne ɔman no; na fa ɔman no ayɛyɛdeɛ bra, na pata ma wɔn, sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛeɛ no.
8Na Aaron twe pinii afɔrebukyia no ho, na ɔkum ne bɔne ho afɔdeɛ nantwie ba no. 9Na ne mma no de mogya no kɔmaa no, na ɔde ne nsateaa bɔɔ mogya no mu de kekaa afɔrebukyia no mmɛn ho, na ɔhwiee mogya no petee afɔrebukyia no ase. 10 Na bɔne ho afɔdeɛ no mu sradeɛ ne sawa ne mmerɛboɔ so ntentan no, ɔtoo mu gya, afɔrebukyia no so, sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no. 11Na ɛnam no ne nwoma no deɛ, ɔde ogya hyee no nsraban no akyi.
12 Na ɔkumm ɔhyeɛ aboa afɔdeɛ no nso, na Aaron mma no de mogya no brɛɛ no, na ɔhwie petee afɔrebukyia no so hyiae. 13Na wɔde ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ no asinasini ne ne tiri no brɛɛ no, na ɔhyee no afɔrebukyia no so. 14Na ɔhohoroo ayamdeɛ ne nnyawa no ho, na ɔhyee no ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ a ɛwɔ afɔrebukyia no soɔ no so.
15Ɛnna ɔde ɔman no afɔdeɛ no baeɛ, na ɔfaa bɔne ho afɔdeɛ papo a ɔyɛ ɔman no deɛ no kumm no de bɔɔ bɔne ho afɔdeɛ sɛ kane deɛ no. 16Na ɔde ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ no bae, na ɔbɛyɛɛ no sɛdeɛ ne yɛbea teɛ no. 17Na ɔde aduane afɔdeɛ no bae, na ɔfaa emu nsa ma hyee no afɔrebukyia no so kaa anɔpa ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ no ho. 18Ɛnna ɔkumm nantwinini ne odwennini a ɛyɛ ɔman no asomdwoeɛ afɔdeɛ no, na Aaron mma no de mogya no brɛɛ no, na ɔhwie petee afɔrebukyia no so hyiae. 19Na nantwinini ne odwennini no sradeɛ no, sradedua no ne deɛ ɛkata sawa ho no ne mmerɛboɔ so ntentan no, 20wɔde sradeɛ no nyinaa guu ɔyan no so, na wɔhyee sradeɛ no afɔrebukyia no so. 21 Na ɔyan no ne srɛ nifa no, Aaron him de yɛɛ ohim afɔdeɛ, AWURADE anim, sɛdeɛ Mose hyɛeɛ no. 22 Ɛnna Aaron maa ne nsa so kyerɛɛ ɔman no, na ɔhyiraa wɔn. Na ɔbɔɔ bɔne ho afɔdeɛ, ne ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ ne asomdwoeɛ afɔdeɛ wieeɛ no, ɔsianee.
23 Na Mose ne Aaron hyɛnee ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no mu; na wɔfirii adie no, wɔhyiraa ɔman no. Ɛnna AWURADE animuonyam yii ne ho kyerɛɛ ɔman no nyinaa.
24 Na ogya firii AWURADE anim bɛhyee afɔrebukyia no so ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ ne sradeɛ no. Na ɔman no nyinaa hunui, na wɔde anigyeɛ huroe, na wɔde wɔn anim butubutuu fam.

english_text:
Nadab and Abihu
1Nadab and Abihu were two of Aaron's sons, but they disobeyed the Lord by burning incense to him on a fire pan, when they were not supposed to. 2Suddenly the Lord sent fiery flames and burned them to death. 3Then Moses told Aaron that this was exactly what the Lord had meant when he said:
“I demand respect
from my priests,
and I will be praised
by everyone!”
Aaron was speechless.
4Moses sent for Mishael and Elzaphan, the two sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel. Then he told them, “Take these two dead relatives of yours outside the camp far from the entrance to the sacred tent.” 5So they dragged the dead men away by their clothes.
6Then Moses told Aaron and his other two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar:
Don't show your sorrow by messing up your hair and tearing your priestly clothes, or the Lord will get angry. He will kill the three of you and punish everyone else. It's all right for your relatives, the people of Israel, to mourn for those he destroyed by fire. 7But you are the Lord's chosen priests, and you must not leave the sacred tent, or you will die.
Aaron and his two sons obeyed Moses.
8The Lord said to Aaron:
9When you or your sons enter the sacred tent, you must never drink beer or wine. If you do, you will die right there! This law will never change. 10You must learn the difference between what is holy and what isn't holy and between the clean and the unclean. 11You must also teach the people of Israel everything that I commanded Moses to say to them.
12 Moses told Aaron and his two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar:
The grain sacrifice that was offered to give thanks to the Lord is very holy. So make bread without yeast from the part that wasn't sent up in smoke and eat it beside the altar. 13The Lord has said that this belongs to you and your sons, and that it must be eaten in a holy place. 14-15 But the choice ribs and the hind leg that were lifted up may be eaten by your entire family, as long as you do so in an acceptable place. These parts are yours from the sacrifices that the people offer to ask the Lord's blessing. This is what the Lord has commanded, and it will never change.
16When Moses asked around and learned that the ram for the sin sacrifice had already been burned on the altar, he became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar and said, 17 “Why didn't you eat the meat from this sacrifice in an acceptable place? It is very holy, and the Lord has given you this sacrifice to remove Israel's sin and guilt. 18Whenever an animal's blood isn't brought into the sacred tent, I commanded you to eat its meat in an acceptable place, but you burned it instead.”
19Their father Aaron replied, “Today two of my sons offered the sacrifice for sin and the sacrifice to please the Lord, and look what has happened to me! Would the Lord have approved if I had eaten the sacrifice for sin?”
20Moses was satisfied with Aaron's reply.
translation_text:
Nadab ne Abihu ho asɛm
1Na Aaron mma Nadab ne Abihu fefaa wɔn gyasɔ adeɛ, na wɔde ogya guguu mu, na wɔde aduhwam guguu so, na wɔde ananagya a ɔnhyɛɛ wɔn ho mmara baa AWURADE anim. 2 Na ogya firii AWURADE anim bɛhyee wɔn, na wɔwuwuu AWURADE anim. 3 Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Aaron sɛ: Ɛno ne deɛ AWURADE kaa sɛ:
Wɔn a wɔtwe pini me no mu
na mɛyɛ me ho kronkron,
na ɔman no nyinaa anim
na mɛhyɛ me ho animuonyam.
4 Na Aaron yɛɛ komm. Ɛnna Mose frɛɛ Aaron n’agya nuabarima Usiel mma Misael ne Elsafan baeɛ, na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Montwe mpini, na mommɛsoa mo nuanom no mfiri kronkronbea anim nkɔ nsraban no akyi. 5Na wɔtwe bae bɛsoaa wɔn, wɔn ntadeɛ mu, de wɔn kɔɔ nsraban no akyi sɛdeɛ Mose kaeɛ no. 6 Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Aaron ne ne mma Eleasa ne Itamar sɛ: Mommpɛsɛ mo ti, na monnsunsuane mo ntadeɛ mu, na moanwuwu, na abufuo amma asafo no nyinaa so, nanso mo nuanom, Israel fie nyinaa, nsu wɔn a AWURADE de ogya ahye wɔn yi. 7Na mommfiri ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano nso, na moanwuwu, ɛfiri sɛ AWURADE sra ngo no wɔ mo so. Na wɔyɛɛ sɛdeɛ Mose kaeɛ no.
8Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Aaron sɛ: 9 Wo ne wo mma nyinaa, ansa na mobɛhyɛne ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no mu no, monnnom bobesa anaa nsa biara, na moanwuwu. Ɛnyɛ daa ahyɛdeɛ, mo awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ nyinaa mu. 10Na moahunu ade kronkron ne adeɛ a ɛnyɛ kronkron ne adeɛ a ɛho teɛ ne deɛ ɛho nteɛ ntam nsonsonoeɛ, 11na moakyerɛkyerɛ Israelfoɔ ahyɛdeɛ a AWURADE nam Mose so ka kyerɛɛ wɔn no nyinaa.
12Na Mose kasa kyerɛɛ Aaron ne ne mma Eleasa ne Itamar a wɔkaeɛ no sɛ: Momfa AWURADE gya afɔdeɛ mu aduane a ɛkaeɛ no, na monni no apiti, afɔrebukyia no ho, ɛfiri sɛ ɛyɛ akronkronneɛ mu ade kronkron. 13 Monni no deɛ ɛhɔ yɛ kronkron, na ɛyɛ AWURADE gya afɔdeɛ ho kyɛfa ma wo ne wo mma, ɛfiri sɛ saa na wɔahyɛ me. 14 Na ohim yan no ne mmasoɔ srɛ no, monni no deɛ ɛhɔ teɛ, wo ne wo mmammarima ne wo mmammaa nyinaa, ɛfiri sɛ ɛyɛ wo kyɛfa ne wo mma kyɛfa a wɔde ama mo afiri Israelfoɔ asomdwoeɛ afɔdeɛ mu. 15Mmasoɔ srɛ ne ohim yan no na wɔmfa nka sradeɛ a wɔhyeɛ no ho mmra, na wɔnhim no ohim afɔdeɛ, AWURADE anim, na ɛnyɛ wo deɛ ne wo mma deɛ nyɛ daa kyɛfa, sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛeɛ no.
16Na bɔne ho afɔdeɛ papo no, Mose hwehwɛɛ no brɛɛ ara yie, na hwɛ, wɔahye no. Na ne bo fuu Aaron mma Eleasa ne Itamar a wɔkaeɛ no, na ɔkaa sɛ: 17Adɛn nti na moanni bɔne ho afɔdeɛ no wɔ kronkronbea hɔ? Ɛfiri sɛ ɛyɛ akronkronneɛ mu ade kronkron, na ɛno na wɔde ama mo, sɛ monsoa asafo no mmusuo no, na mompata mma wɔn, AWURADE anim. 18 Hwɛ, wɔamfa ne mogya no amma kronkronbea dan no mu; anka ɛsɛ sɛ modi no kronkronbea hɔ, sɛdeɛ mehyɛɛ mo no. 19Na Aaron kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Hwɛ, ɛnnɛ wɔde wɔn bɔne ho afɔdeɛ ne wɔn hyeɛ afɔdeɛ aba AWURADE anim, na adeɛ a ɛte seyie abɛto me yi; na sɛ medi bɔne ho afɔdeɛ nnɛ a, ɛbɛsɔ AWURADE ani anaa? 20Na Mose teeɛ no, n’akoma tɔɔ ne yam.

english_text:
Clean and Unclean Animals
(Deuteronomy 14.3-21)
1 The Lord told Moses and Aaron 2to say to the community of Israel:
You may eat 3any animal that has divided hoofs and chews the cud. 4-8But you must not eat animals such as camels, rock badgers, and rabbits that chew the cud but don't have divided hoofs. And you must not eat pigs—they have divided hoofs, but don't chew the cud. All of these animals are unclean, and you are forbidden even to touch their dead bodies.
9-12You may eat anything that lives in water and has fins and scales. But it would be disgusting for you to eat anything else that lives in water, and you must not even touch their dead bodies.
13-19Eagles, vultures, buzzards, crows, ostriches, hawks, sea gulls, owls, pelicans, storks, herons, hoopoes, and bats are also disgusting, and you are forbidden to eat any of them.
20-23The only winged insects you may eat are locusts, grasshoppers, and crickets. All other winged insects that crawl are too disgusting for you to eat.
24-28Don't even touch the dead bodies of animals that have divided hoofs but don't chew the cud. And don't touch the dead bodies of animals that have paws. If you do, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
29-30Moles, rats, mice, and all kinds of lizards are unclean. 31Anyone who touches their dead bodies or anything touched by their dead bodies becomes unclean until evening. 32If something made of wood, cloth, or leather touches one of their dead bodies, it must be washed, but it is still unclean until evening. 33If any of these animals is found dead in a clay pot, the pot must be broken to pieces, and everything in it becomes unclean. 34If you pour water from this pot on any food, that food becomes unclean, and anything drinkable in the pot becomes unclean.
35If the dead body of one of these animals touches anything else, including ovens and stoves, that thing becomes unclean and must be destroyed. 36A spring or a cistern where one of these dead animals is found is still clean, but anyone who touches the animal becomes unclean. 37If the dead body of one of these animals is found lying on seeds that have been set aside for planting, the seeds remain clean. 38But seeds that are soaking in water become unclean, if the dead animal is found in the water.
39If an animal that may be eaten happens to die, and you touch it, you become unclean until evening. 40If you eat any of its meat or carry its body away, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
41-42Don't eat any of those disgusting little creatures that crawl or walk close to the ground. 43If you eat any of them, you will become just as disgusting and unclean as they are. 44 I am the Lord your God, and you must dedicate yourselves to me and be holy, just as I am holy. Don't become disgusting by eating any of these unclean creatures. 45I brought you out of Egypt so that I could be your God. Now you must become holy, because I am holy!
46-47I have given these laws so that you will know what animals, birds, and fish are clean and may be eaten, and which ones are unclean and may not be eaten.

Mmoa a wɔnnie ne deɛ wɔnnnie
(Deuteronomium 14.3-21)
1 Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron see wɔn sɛ: 2 Monkasa nkyerɛ Israelfoɔ sɛ: Yeinom ne mmoa a monni wɔ asase so mmoa nyinaa mu: 3Ntɔteboa mu wɔn a wɔwɔ tɔte a emu apaeɛ na wɔn tɔte mu apae koraa, na wɔpu deɛ wɔadie wesa no, ɛno na monnie. 4Yeinom nko na monnnie, wɔn a wɔpu wesa anaa wɔn tɔte mu apaeɛ: Yoma, ɛfiri sɛ ɔpu wesa deɛ, nanso ne tɔte mu mpae, enti ne ho nte mma mo; 5ne atwaboa, ɛfiri sɛ ɔpu wesa deɛ, nanso ne tɔte mu mpae, ne ho nte mma mo; 6ne adanko, ɛfiri sɛ ɔpu wesa deɛ, nanso ne tɔte mu mpae, ne ho nte mma mo; 7ne prako, ɛfiri sɛ ne tɔte mu apae koraa deɛ, nanso ɔmpu nwesa, ne ho nte mma mo. 8Monnni wɔn nam, na monnka wɔn afunu; wɔn ho nte mma mo.
9Yei ne deɛ monnie deɛ ɛwɔ nsuo mu nyinaa mu: Deɛ ɛwɔ ntɛtɛ ne abon, nsuo mu, ɛpo ne nsuwansuwa mu, ɛnonom na monnie. 10Na biribiara a ɛnni ntɛtɛ ne abon, ɛpo ne nsuwansuwa mu, adeɛ a ɛwɔ nsuo mu nyinaa a nkwa wɔ mu nyinaa, ɛyɛ akyiwadeɛ ma mo. 11Na ɛnyɛ mo akyiwadeɛ, monnni wɔn nam, na wɔn afunu nso, monkyi. 12Adeɛ biara a ɛnni ntɛtɛ ne abon wɔ nsuo mu no yɛ mo akyiwadeɛ.
13Na yeinom na monkyire ntuboa mu; monnni, wɔyɛ akyiwadeɛ: Ɔkɔdeɛ, ɔkɔrewa, ɔkomfufuo, 14ɔkompɛtɛ, asansa, sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ, 15ne anene ahodoɔ nyinaa, 16sohori, anadwo-akorɔma, ɛpo so asomfenakatakyi, akorɔma, sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ, 17ne patubiaa, ɛpo so anene, patukɛseɛ, 18bakanoma, nantwinoma, ɔpɛtɛ, 19sukɔnkɔn, asukɔnkɔn ahodoɔ, asɔkwaa ne apan. 20Ntuboa manyamanya a wɔnante nan nnan so nyinaa nyɛ akyiwadeɛ mma mo. 21Nanso yeinom na monnie ntuboa nyinaa a wɔnante nan nnan soɔ nyinaa mu, wɔn a wɔwɔ aprɛ mmienu wɔ wɔn nan soɔ a wɔde hurihuri asase so no; 22wɔn mu deɛ monnie nie: Ntutummɛ ahodoɔ, nketekyire ahodoɔ, mfuntie ahodoɔ, mmɛbɛ ahodoɔ. 23Na ntuboa manyamanya a wɔwɔ nan nnan nyinaa yɛ akyiwadeɛ ma mo. 24 Na yeinom na mode gu mo ho fi; obiara a ɔka wɔn afunu no ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ. 25Na obiara a ɔsoa wɔn afunu no, ɔnsi ne ntadeɛ, ɛfiri sɛ ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ. 26Ntɔteboa a wɔn tɔte mu apaeɛ, nanso emu nwie paeɛ na wɔmpu nwesa no nyinaa ho nte mma mo; obiara a ɔka wɔn no, ne ho nte. 27Na mmoa a wɔnam nan nnan soɔ nyinaa mu wɔn a wɔnam wɔn nsa ne wɔn nan mu no, wɔn ho nte mma mo; obiara a ɔka wɔn funu no, ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ. 28Na deɛ ɔsoa wɔn funu bi no nsi ne ntadeɛ, na ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ; wɔn ho nte mma mo.
29Na mmoa a wɔwea asase soɔ mu wɔn a wɔn ho nte mma mo nie: Ahweaa, akura, ne nkoterɛ ahodoɔ; 30ne hwinamanhwan, ɔmampam, ɔkoterɛ, bɔmɔte ne abosomakoterɛ. 31Yeinom ne wɔn a wɔn ho nte mma mo, mmoa a wɔwea nyinaa mu; sɛ wɔwu a, obiara a ɔka wɔn no, ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ. 32Na adeɛ biara a wɔn mu bi awu atɔ soɔ no, ɛho nte: Dua adeɛ biara oo, atadeɛ oo, nwoma oo, awere oo, adeɛ biara a wɔde yɛ adwuma; wɔmfa nhyɛ nsuo mu, na ɛho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ ansa na ɛho ate. 33Na kukuo biara a wɔn mu bi bɛhwe mu no, deɛ ɛwɔ mu nyinaa ho nte, na kukuo no nso mommɔ no. 34Aduane a wɔdie biara a nsuo no bi bɛgu mu no ho nte, na anonneɛ biara a wɔnom adeɛ biara a ɛte saa mu no ho nte. 35Na adeɛ biara a wɔn funu ho biribi bɛhwe soɔ, ɛho nte: Fononoo oo, bukyia oo, wɔmmubu: Ɛho nte, na mommu no sɛ ɛho nte. 36Nanso nsuo aniwa anaa abura a nsuo wɔ mu deɛ, ɛho te ara; na biribiara a ɛka wɔn funu no, ɛho nte. 37Na sɛ wɔn funu bi hwe kuadeɛ a wɔdua biara so a, kuadeɛ no ho te; 38na sɛ wɔde nsuo gu kuadeɛ no so na wɔn afunu bi hwe so a, ɛho nte mma mo. 39Na sɛ mmoa a modie no bi wu a, deɛ ɔka ne funu no ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ. 40 Na deɛ ɔdi ne funu no bie no nsi ne ntadeɛ, na ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ; na deɛ ɔsoa ne funu no nsi ne ntadeɛ, na ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ.
41Na adeɛ biara a ɛwea fam yɛ akyiwadeɛ, monnni. 42Adeɛ biara a ɛnam yafunu soɔ ne adeɛ biara a ɛnam nan nnan so kɔsi adeɛ biara a ɛwɔ nan bebree soɔ, wɔn a wɔwea fam nyinaa mu no, monnni, ɛfiri sɛ ɛyɛ akyiwadeɛ. 43Monnyɛ mo ho akyiwadeɛ wɔ mmoa a wɔwea no biara ho, na monnyɛ mo ho fi a ɛmma mo ho nteɛ wɔ wɔn ho. 44 Na mene AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn, enti monte mo ho na monyɛ kronkron, ɛfiri sɛ meyɛ kronkron; enti mommma mo kra ho nnkum, adeɛ biara a ɛwea a ɛtwe ne ho ase no ho. 45 Na mene AWURADE a meyii mo Misraim asase so sɛ mɛyɛ mo Nyankopɔn no; enti monyɛ kronkron, ɛfiri sɛ meyɛ kronkron. 46Yei ne aboa biara a wɔwɔ nsuo mu ne nnomaa ne aboa biara a wɔwea fam nyinaa ho mmara, 47sɛ wɔmfa mpae adeɛ a ɛho nteɛ ne deɛ ɛho teɛ mu, ne mmoa a wɔdie ne mmoa a wɔnnie mu.

english_text:
What Women Must Do after Giving Birth
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to the community of Israel:
If a woman gives birth to a son, she is unclean for seven days, just as she is during her monthly period. 3 Her son must be circumcised on the eighth day, 4but her loss of blood keeps her from being completely clean for another 33 days. During this time she must not touch anything holy or go to the place of worship. 5Any woman who gives birth to a daughter is unclean for two weeks, just as she is during her period. And she won't be completely clean for another 66 days.
6When the mother has completed her time of cleansing, she must come to the front of the sacred tent and bring to the priest a year-old lamb as a sacrifice to please me and a dove or a pigeon as a sacrifice for sin. 7After the priest offers the sacrifices to me, the mother will become completely clean from her loss of blood, whether her child is a boy or a girl. 8 If she cannot afford a lamb, she can offer two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice to please me and the other as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_text:
Awoɔ akyiri ahodwira
1Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 2 Kasa kyerɛ Israelfoɔ no sɛ: Sɛ ɔbaa bi nyinsɛn na ɔwo ɔbabanin a, ne ho nte nnanson te sɛ ne nsabuo nna mu a ne ho nteɛ no. 3 Na da a ɛtɔ so nwɔtwe no, wɔntwa abɔfra no twetia. 4Na ɔntena tannan mu adaduasa nnammiɛnsa n’ahodwira mogya mu; ɔnnka ade kronkron biara na ɔmmma kronkronbea hɔ kɔsi sɛ n’ahodwira nna bɛwie duro. 5Na sɛ ɔwo ɔbaa a, ne ho nte nnawɔtwe mmienu sɛ ne nsabuo nna mu, na ɔntena tannan mu adaduosia nnansia n’ahodwira mogya mu.
6 Na sɛ ahodwira nna no wie du ma ɔbabanin anaa ɔbabaa no a, ɔmfa odwanten ba a wadi afe a wɔde bɛbɔ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ ne aborɔnoma ba anaa anyankuku a wɔde bɛbɔ bɔne ho afɔdeɛ mmra ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano mmɛma ɔsɔfoɔ no. 7Na ɔmfa mmra AWURADE anim, na ɔmpata mma no, na ne ho nte mfiri ne mogyaguo no mu. Yei ne mmara a ɛda hɔ ma ɔbaa a wawo ɔbabarima anaa ɔbabaa no. 8 Na sɛ ne nsa anso odwan ba so a, ɔmfa anyankuku mmienu anaa mmorɔnoma mma mmienu mmra mmɛma, baako nyɛ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ, na baako nso nyɛ bɔne ho afɔdeɛ, na ɔsɔfoɔ no mpata mma no, na ne ho nte.

english_text:
Skin Diseases
1The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
2If sores or boils or a skin rash should break out and start spreading on your body, you must be brought to Aaron or to one of the other priests. 3If the priest discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
4But if the infected area is white and only skin deep, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, the priest will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 5If the disease hasn't spread by that time, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days. 6Then if the disease hasn't become any worse or spread, the priest will say, “You are clean. It is only a sore. After you wash your clothes, you may go home.”
7However, if the disease comes back, you must return to the priest. 8If it is discovered that the disease has started spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
9Any of you with a skin disease must be brought to a priest. 10If he discovers that the sore spot is white with pus and that the hair around it has also turned white, 11he will say, “This is leprosy. You are unclean and must stay away from everyone else.” 12-13But if the disease has run its course and only the scars remain, he will say, “You are clean.” 14-15If the sores come back and turn white again, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
16-17However, if the sores heal and only white spots remain, the priest will say, “You are now clean.”
18-19If you have a sore that either swells or turns reddish-white after it has healed, then you must show it to a priest. 20If he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 21But if the white area is only on the surface of the skin and hasn't become any worse, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
22If the sore begins spreading during this time, the priest will say, “You are unclean because you have a disease.” 23But if it doesn't spread, and only a scar remains, he will say, “You are now clean.”
24If you have a burn that gets infected and turns red or reddish-white, 25a priest must examine it. Then if he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “The burn has turned into leprosy, and you are unclean.” 26But if the priest finds that the hair in the infected area hasn't turned white and that the sore is only skin deep and it is healing, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 27On the seventh day the priest will examine you again, and if the infection is spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 28However, if the infection hasn't spread and has begun to heal, and if only a scar remains, he will say, “Only a scar remains from the burn, and you are clean.”
29If you have a sore on your head or chin, 30it must be examined by a priest. If the infection seems more than skin deep, and the hair in it has thinned out and lost its color, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 31On the other hand, if he discovers that the itchy spot is only skin deep, but that the hair still isn't healthy, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 32By that time, if the itch hasn't spread, if the hair seems healthy, and if the itch is only skin deep, 33you must shave off the hair around the infection, but not those on it. Then the priest will tell you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days. 34By that time, if the itch hasn't spread and seems no more than skin deep, he will say, “You are clean; now you must wash your clothes.”
35-36Later, if the itch starts spreading, even though the hair is still healthy, the priest will say, “You are unclean.” 37But if he thinks you are completely well, he will say, “You are clean.”
38If white spots break out on your skin, 39but the priest discovers that it is only a rash, he will say, “You are clean.”
40-41If you become bald on any part of your head, you are still clean. 42-43But if a priest discovers that a reddish-white sore has broken out on the bald spot and looks like leprosy, he will say, 44“This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
45If you ever have leprosy, you must tear your clothes, leave your hair uncombed, cover the lower part of your face, and go around shouting, “I'm unclean! I'm unclean!” 46As long as you have the disease, you are unclean and must live alone outside the camp.
47-50If a greenish or reddish spot appears anywhere on any of your clothing or on anything made of leather, you must let the priest examine the clothing or the leather. He will put it aside for seven days, 51and if the mildew has spread in that time, he will say, “This is unclean 52because the mildew has spread.” Then he will burn the clothing or the piece of leather.
53If the priest discovers that the mildew hasn't spread, 54he will tell you to wash the clothing or leather and put it aside for another seven days, 55after which he will examine it again. If the spot hasn't spread, but is still greenish or reddish, the clothing or leather is unclean and must be burned. 56But if the spot has faded after being washed, he will tear away the spot. 57Later, if the spot reappears elsewhere on the clothing or the leather, you must burn it. 58Even if the spot completely disappears after being washed, it must be washed again before it is clean.
59These are the rules for deciding if clothing is clean or unclean after a spot appears on it.
translation_text:
Kwata ho mmara
1 Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron sɛ: 2Sɛ biribi ba onipa honam wedeɛ mu, sɛ nsoa oo, ntwintwameeɛ oo, ntampeɛ oo, na ɛdidi ne honam wedeɛ mu yɛ kwata ntotɔeɛ a, wɔmfa no mmrɛ Ɔsɔfoɔ Aaron anaa ne mma, asɔfoɔ no mu baako. 3 Na sɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ honam wedeɛ mu ntotɔeɛ no, na ntotɔeɛ no so nwi adane fitaa, na ntotɔeɛ no atotɔ mu asene ne honam wedeɛ no a, ɛyɛ kwata ntotɔeɛ; na ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ no a, ɔmmu no deɛ ne ho nteɛ. 4Na sɛ ɛyɛ ne honam wedeɛ mu ntampeɛ fitaa, na sɛ wɔhwɛ na ɛntotɔ mu nsene ne wedeɛ no, na ɛso nwi nnanee fitaa a, ɛnneɛ, ɔsɔfoɔ no nto ɔyarefoɔ no mu nnanson. 5Na ɛda a ɛtɔ so nson no, ɔsɔfoɔ no nhwɛ, na sɛ ɔhunu sɛ ntotɔeɛ no te sɛdeɛ ɛteɛ n’ani so na ɛnyerɛɛ ne wedeɛ mu a, ɔsɔfoɔ no nto no mu nnanson bio. 6Na sɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ no da a ɛtɔ so nson no bio na sɛ ntotɔeɛ no ani adum na ɛntrɛɛ ne wedeɛ mu a, ɔsɔfoɔ no mmu no sɛ deɛ ne ho teɛ, ɛyɛ ntwintwameeɛ; na ɔnsi n’atadeɛ na ne ho ate. 7Nanso ɔde ne ho akɔkyerɛ ɔsɔfoɔ wɔ n’ahoteɛ ho no akyiri no, sɛ ntwintwameeɛ no yerɛ ne wedeɛ mu a, wɔmma ɔsɔfoɔ no nhwɛ no bio; 8na sɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ, na hwɛ, ntwintwameeɛ no ayerɛ wedeɛ no mu a, ɔsɔfoɔ no mmu no deɛ ne ho nteɛ; ɛyɛ kwata.
9Sɛ kwata ntotɔeɛ wɔ onipa bi ho a, wɔmfa no mmrɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no. 10Na sɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ, na hwɛ, nsoa fitaa bi wɔ wedeɛ no mu a adane nwi no fitaa, na ɛnam mono repu nsoaeɛ no mu a, 11ɛyɛ kwata dada a ɛwɔ ne honam wedeɛ mu, na ɔsɔfoɔ no mmu no sɛ ne ho nte. Ɔnnto no mu; na ne ho nte. 12Na sɛ kwata no apue afiri wedeɛ mu akata ɔyarefoɔ no honam nyinaa firi n’atifi kɔsi ne nan ase, baabiara a ɔsɔfoɔ no ani bɛhwɛ no, 13na ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ, na kwata no akata ne honam nyinaa so a, ɔmmu ɔyarefoɔ no sɛ ne ho te; ne ho nyinaa adane fitaa a, ne ho te. 14Nanso berɛ biara a wɔbɛhunu ne ho ɛnam mono no, ne ho nte. 15Na sɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ ɛnam mono no a, ɔmmu no deɛ ne ho nteɛ; ɛnam mono no ho nte, ɛyɛ kwata. 16Na sɛ ɛnam mono no sane dane fitaa, na ɔba ɔsɔfoɔ no nkyɛn, 17na ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ, na sɛ ntotɔeɛ no adane fitaa a, ɛnneɛ, ɔsɔfoɔ no mmu no deɛ ne ho teɛ; ne ho ate.
18Sɛ mpɔmpɔ si obi honam wedeɛ mu na ɛsa, 19na soa fitaa bi anaa ntampeɛ fitaa a ɛbereɛ ba mpɔmpɔ no ananmu a, wɔmma ɔsɔfoɔ no nhwɛ. 20Na sɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ, na sɛ ɛhɔ atotɔ mu asene wedeɛ no na emu nwi adane fitaa a, ɔsɔfoɔ no mmu no deɛ ne ho nteɛ; ɛyɛ kwata ntotɔeɛ, apue wɔ mpɔmpɔ no mu. 21Na sɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ na sɛ nwi fitaa bi nni mu, na ɛntotɔɔ mu nsenee wedeɛ no na ani dum a, ɔsɔfoɔ no nto no mu nnanson; 22na sɛ ɛyerɛ wedeɛ no mu a, ɔsɔfoɔ no mmu no deɛ ne ho nteɛ: Ɛyɛ ntotɔeɛ. 23 Na sɛ ntampeɛ no te sɛdeɛ ɛteɛ na ɛnyerɛe a, ɛyɛ mpɔmpɔ no twa, na ɔsɔfoɔ no mmu no deɛ ne ho teɛ.
24Anaasɛ ogya kuro bi ba honam wedeɛ no mu, na ekuro no so bɔn repu yɛ ntampeɛ a ɛhoa fitaa na emu gyegyeɛ anaasɛ ɛhoa fitaa, 25na sɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ, na sɛ ntampeɛ no mu nwi adane fitaa na wɔhwɛ a atotɔ mu asene wedeɛ no a, ɛyɛ kwata, na apue ogya kuro no mu, na ɔsɔfoɔ no mmu no deɛ ne ho nteɛ: Ɛyɛ kwata ntotɔeɛ. 26Na sɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ, na sɛ enwi fitaa nni ntampeɛ no mu, na ɛntotɔɔ mu nsenee wedeɛ no, na ani dum a, ɔsɔfoɔ no nto no mu nnanson. 27Na da a ɛtɔ so nson no, ɔsɔfoɔ no hunu sɛ ayerɛ wedeɛ no mu a, ɔsɔfoɔ no mmu no deɛ ne ho nteɛ: Ɛyɛ kwata ntotɔeɛ. 28 Na sɛ ntampeɛ no te sɛdeɛ ɛteɛ na ɛnyerɛe wɔ wedeɛ no mu na ani dum a, ɛyɛ soa a ogya kuro no asoa, na ɔsɔfoɔ no mmu no deɛ ne ho teɛ; na ɛyɛ ogya kuro no bɔn.
29Na ɔbarima anaa ɔbaa bi, sɛ biribi tɔ n’atifi anaa ne bɔgyesɛ mu, 30na ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ ntotɔeɛ no, na sɛ atɔ mu asene wedeɛ no, na enwi kɔkɔɔ nhweanhweaa wɔ mu a, ɔsɔfoɔ no mmu no sɛdeɛ ne ho nteɛ; ɛyɛ ntutuiɛ, ɛyɛ etire anaa bɔgyesɛ mu kwata. 31Na ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ ntutuiɛ ntotɔeɛ no, na sɛ ɛhɔ ntɔɔ mu nsenee wedeɛ no, na enwi tuntum nso nni mu a, ɔsɔfoɔ no nto deɛ ntutuiɛ atotɔ no no mu nnanson. 32Na sɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ ɔyarefoɔ no da a ɛtɔ so nson no, na sɛ ntutuiɛ no nyerɛe na enwi kɔkɔɔ mmaa mu, na ntutuiɛ no ntɔɔ mu nsenee wedeɛ no a, 33ɔnyi ne ho nwi, na ɔnnyi ntutuiɛ no so, na ɔsɔfoɔ no nto deɛ ntutuiɛ ayɛ no no mu nnanson bio. 34Na sɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ ntutuiɛ no da a ɛtɔ so nson no, na sɛ ntutuiɛ no nyerɛɛ wedeɛ no mu na ɛhɔ ntɔɔ mu nsenee wedeɛ no a, ɛnneɛ, ɔsɔfoɔ no mmu no deɛ ne ho teɛ; na ɔnsi ne ntadeɛ na ne ho ate. 35Na sɛ ɛno akyi, ntutuiɛ no yerɛ, 36na ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ no, na sɛ ntutuiɛ no ayerɛ wedeɛ no mu a, ɔsɔfoɔ no nnhwehwɛ enwi kɔkɔɔ; ne ho nte. 37Na sɛ ɔhunu ntutuiɛ no sɛ ɛte sɛdeɛ ɛteɛ na enwi tuntum afu mu a, na ntutuiɛ no asa; ne ho te, na ɔsɔfoɔ no mmu no deɛ ne ho teɛ.
38Na sɛ ntampeɛ fitaa ba ɔbarima anaa ɔbaa wedeɛ ani, 39na ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ, na sɛ ntampeɛ a ani dum fitaa wɔ wɔn honam wedeɛ mu a, ɛyɛ ɛyam a ayerɛ wedeɛ mu; ne ho te.
40Na sɛ ɔbarima bi tiri pa a, ɔyɛ atipa; ne ho te. 41Na sɛ n’apampam anim fam na apa a, ɔyɛ atipa; ne ho te. 42Na sɛ biribi fitaa a ɛbereɛ tɔ n’atipa no mu anaasɛ n’apampam paeɛ no mu a, ɛyɛ kwata a ɛrepue n’atipa anaa n’apampam paeɛ no mu. 43Na sɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ, na sɛ ntotɔeɛ fitaa a ɛbereɛ asoa n’atipa no anaa n’apampam paeɛ no mu a ɛte sɛ honam wedeɛ mu kwata a, 44ɔyɛ ɔkwatani; ne ho nte; buo na ɔsɔfoɔ no mmu no deɛ ne ho nteɛ; ne tiri so na ne ntotɔeɛ no wɔ.
45Na ɔkwatani a yadeɛ no wɔ ne ho nsunsuane ne ntadeɛ mu, na ɔmpɛsɛ ne ti, na ɔnkata ne soro anofafa, na ɔnteam sɛ: Me ho nte, me ho nte! 46 Nna dodoɔ a yadeɛ no wɔ ne ho no, teɛ na ne ho nteɛ; ɔno nko na ɔntena, nsraban no akyi na ɔntena.
47Na sɛ kwata ntotɔeɛ wɔ atadeɛ bi mu, sɛ ɛwɔ kuntutam anaa asaawatam, 48anaa nsa anaa mfa a wɔde nwono asaawatam anaa kuntutam anaa nwoma anaa adeɛ biara a wɔde nwoma ayɛ mu, 49na sɛ ntotɔeɛ no biri anaasɛ ɛbere ntoma anaa nwoma no anaa nsa anaa mfa no anaa adeɛ biara a wɔde nwoma ayɛ mu a, ɛyɛ kwata ntotɔeɛ, wɔmma ɔsɔfoɔ no nhwɛ. 50Na sɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ ntotɔeɛ no a, ɔnto adeɛ a ntotɔeɛ no wɔ mu no mu nnanson. 51Na ɛda a ɛtɔ so nson no, ɔhunu sɛ ntotɔeɛ no ayerɛ atadeɛ no anaa nsa anaa mfa anaa nwoma no anaa biribiara a wɔde nwoma ayɛ no mu a, na ntotɔeɛ no yɛ kwata a ɛsɛe adeɛ; ɛho nte. 52Na ɔnhye ntoma no, sɛ nsa no anaa mfa no oo, anaa kuntu anaa asaawa anaa nwoma adeɛ biara mu na ntotɔeɛ no wɔ oo, ɛfiri sɛ ɛyɛ kwata a ɛsɛe adeɛ. Ogya na wɔmfa nhyeɛ.
53Na sɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ, na sɛ ntotɔeɛ no nterɛɛ atadeɛ no mu wɔ nsa anaa mfa anaa nwoma adeɛ biara mu a, 54ɛnneɛ, ɔsɔfoɔ no nhyɛ na wɔnsi adeɛ a ntotɔeɛ no wɔ mu no, na ɔnto mu nnanson bio. 55Na ntotɔeɛ no sie akyiri no ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ, na sɛ ntotɔeɛ no ani nsakyerae na ɛnyerɛe nso a, ɛho nte, wɔmfa ogya nhye; ani akuku oo, akyire akuku oo, ɛyɛ nweweeɛ.
56Na sɛ ne sie akyiri no ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ, na sɛ ntotɔeɛ no ani dum a, ɔnte mfiri ntoma no anaa nsa anaa mfa no mu. 57Na sɛ wɔhunu bio wɔ ntoma no mu wɔ nsa anaa mfa anaa nwoma adeɛ biara mu a, ɛyɛ kwata a ɛrepue, wɔmfa ogya nhye deɛ ntotɔeɛ no wɔ mu no. 58Na ntoma no, mfa anaa nsa anaa nwoma adeɛ biara a wɔbɛsie na ntotɔeɛ no bɛfiri mu no, wɔnsi bio na ɛho ate. 59Yei ne mmara a ɛda hɔ ma kwata ntotɔeɛ, kuntutam anaa asaawatam anaa nsa anaa mfa anaa nwoma adeɛ biara mu, na wɔde abu no adeɛ a ɛho teɛ anaa adeɛ a ɛho nteɛ.

english_text:
The Ceremony for People Healed of Leprosy
1The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
2-3 After you think you are healed of leprosy, you must ask for a priest to come outside the camp and examine you. And if you are well, 4he will order someone to bring out two live birds that are acceptable for sacrifice, together with a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant. 5The priest will order someone to kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water. 6Then he will dip the other bird, the cedar, the red yarn, and the hyssop in the blood of the dead bird. 7Next, he will sprinkle you seven times with the blood and say, “You are now clean.” Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away.
8After this you must wash your clothes, shave your entire body, and take a bath before you are completely clean. You may move back into camp, but you must not enter your tent for seven days. 9Then you must once again shave your head, face, and eyebrows, as well as the hair on the rest of your body. Finally, wash your clothes and take a bath, and you will be completely clean.
10On the eighth day you must bring to the priest two rams and a year-old female lamb that have nothing wrong with them; also bring 300 milliliters of olive oil and 3 kilograms of your finest flour mixed with oil. 11Then the priest will present you and your offerings to me at the entrance to my sacred tent. 12There he will offer one of the rams, together with the oil, as a sacrifice to make things right. He will also lift them up to show that they are dedicated to me. 13This sacrifice is very holy. It belongs to the priest and must be killed in the same place where animals are killed as sacrifices for sins and as sacrifices to please me.
14The priest will smear some of the blood from this sacrifice on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot. 15He will then pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand, 16dip a finger of his right hand into the oil, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred tent. 17Next, the priest will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot, 18-20and he will pour the rest of the oil from his palm on your head. Then he will offer the other two animals—one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice. After this you will be completely clean.
21If you are poor and cannot afford to offer this much, you may offer a ram as a sacrifice to make things right, together with 300 milliliters of olive oil and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil as a grain sacrifice. The priest will then lift these up to dedicate them to me. 22Depending on what you can afford, you must also offer either two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me. 23The priest will offer these to me in front of the sacred tent on the eighth day.
24-25The priest will kill this ram for the sacrifice to make things right, and he will lift it up with the olive oil in dedication to me. Then he will smear some of the blood on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot.
26The priest will pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand, 27then dip a finger of his right hand in the oil and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred tent. 28He will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot, just as he did with the blood of the sacrifice to make things right. 29-31And he will pour the rest of the oil from his palm on your head.
Then, depending on what you can afford, he will offer either the doves or the pigeons together with the grain sacrifice. One of the birds is the sacrifice for sin, and the other is the sacrifice to please me. After this you will be completely clean.
32These are the things you must do if you have leprosy and cannot afford the usual sacrifices to make you clean.
When There Is Mildew in a House
33The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
34After I have given you the land of Canaan as your permanent possession, here is what you must do, if I ever put mildew on the walls of any of your homes. 35First, you must say to a priest, “I think there is mildew on the wall of my house.”
36The priest will reply, “Empty the house before I inspect it, or else everything in it will be unclean.”
37If the priest discovers greenish or reddish spots that go deeper than the surface of the walls, 38he will have the house closed for seven days. 39Then he will return and check to see if the mildew has spread. 40-41If so, he will order someone to scrape the plaster from the walls, remove the stones covered with mildew, then haul everything off and dump it in an unclean place outside the town. 42Afterwards the wall must be repaired with new stones and fresh plaster.
43If the mildew appears a second time, 44the priest will come and say, “This house is unclean. It's covered with mildew that can't be removed.” 45Then he will have the house torn down and every bit of wood, stone, and plaster hauled off to an unclean place outside the town. 46Meanwhile, if any of you entered the house while it was closed, you will be unclean until evening. 47And if you either slept or ate in the house, you must wash your clothes.
48On the other hand, if the priest discovers that mildew hasn't reappeared after the house was newly plastered, he will say, “This house is clean—the mildew has gone.” 49Then, to show that the house is now clean, he will get two birds, a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant and bring them to the house. 50He will kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water 51-52and let its blood drain into the pot. Then he will dip the cedar, the hyssop, the yarn, and the other bird into the mixture of blood and water. Next, he will sprinkle the house seven times with the mixture, then the house will be completely clean. 53Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away, ending the ceremony for purifying the house.
54-57These are the things you must do if you discover that you are unclean because of an itch or a sore, or that your clothing or house is unclean because of mildew.
translation_text:
Akwatafoɔ ahodwira
1Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 2 Yei ne mmara a ɛda hɔ ma ɔkwatani, ɛda a wɔbu no sɛ ne ho ateɛ no. Wɔmfa no mmrɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no, 3na ɔsɔfoɔ no mfiri adi nkɔ nsraban no akyi; na sɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ na sɛ kwata ntotɔeɛ no asa ɔkwatani no ho a, 4ɔsɔfoɔ no nhyɛ mma wɔmfa nnomaa a wɔn ho teɛ mmienu animono ne tweneduro dua ne koogyan ne adwera mma deɛ wɔrebɛte ne ho no mmra. 5Na ɔsɔfoɔ no nhyɛ mma wɔnkum nnomaa no mu baako, ayowa bi mu, mmasuo so. 6Na anomaa nikanfoɔ no deɛ, ɔmfa no ne tweneduro dua no ne koogyan ne adwera no, na ɔmfa ne nyinaa ne anomaa nikanfoɔ no mmɔ anomaa a wɔaku no mmasuo soɔ no mogya mu, 7 na ɔmfa mpete deɛ ɔbɛte ne ho afiri ne kwata ho no so mprɛnson, na ɔnte ne ho, na ɔnnyaa anomaa nikanfoɔ no mma no nkɔ wiram. 8 Na deɛ wɔate ne ho no nsi ne ntadeɛ na ɔnyi ne nwi nyinaa koraa, na ɔmfa nsuo nnware na ne ho ate; na ɛno akyiri no ɔmmra nsraban no mu, nanso ɔntena ne ntomadan akyi nnanson. 9Na da a ɛtɔ so nson no, ɔnyi ne ho nwi nyinaa, ne tiri ne ne bɔgyesɛ ne n’anintɔnnwi nyinaa na ɔnyie; na ɔnsi ne ntadeɛ, na ɔmfa nsuo nnware ne honam, na ne ho ate.
10Na ɛda a ɛtɔ so nwɔtwe no, ɔmfa nnwanten mma mmienu a wɔdi mu, ne odwammaa bedeɛ baako a wadi afe a ɔdi mu, ne aduane afɔdeɛ esiam efa abupɛn du mu mmiɛnsa a wɔde ngo afɔre, ne ngo toa ma baako mmra. 11Na ɔsɔfoɔ a ɔte ne ho no mfa ɔbarima a wɔrete ne ho no ne nnoɔma no mmɛgyina AWURADE anim, ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano. 12Na ɔsɔfoɔ no mfa nnwanten no mu baako mmra, sɛ asodie ho afɔdeɛ ne ngo toa ma no, na ɔnhim no ohim afɔdeɛ, AWURADE anim; 13 na ɔnkum odwanten ba no deɛ wɔkum bɔne ho afɔdeɛ ne ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ hɔ, deɛ ɛhɔ yɛ kronkron, ɛfiri sɛ asodie ho afɔdeɛ no nso yɛ asɔfoɔ no dea, te sɛ bɔne ho afɔdeɛ, ɛyɛ akronkronneɛ mu ade kronkron. 14 Na ɔsɔfoɔ no mfa asodie ho afɔdeɛ mogya no bi nkeka deɛ wɔrete ne ho no aso nifa ne ne nsa nifa kokurobetie ne ne nan nifa kokurobetie ano. 15Na ɔsɔfoɔ no mfa ngo toa no mu bi nhwie ngu ɔno ara ne nsa benkum mu; 16 na ɔsɔfoɔ no mfa ne nsateaa nifa mmɔ ngo a ɛwɔ ne nsa benkum mu no mu, na ɔmfa ne nsateaa nka ngo no bi mpete mprɛnson, AWURADE anim; 17na ngo a ɛbɛka ne nsam no, ɔsɔfoɔ no mfa bi nkeka deɛ wɔrete ne ho no aso nifa ne ne nsa nifa kokurobetie ne ne nan nifa kokurobetie ano, asodie ho afɔdeɛ mogya no so; 18na ngo a ɛbɛka ɔsɔfoɔ no nsam no, ɔnhwie ngu deɛ wɔrete ne ho no atifi, na ɔsɔfoɔ no mpata mma no, AWURADE anim. 19Na ɔsɔfoɔ no mmɔ bɔne ho afɔdeɛ no, na ɔmpata mma deɛ wɔrete ne ho afiri ne ho fi mu no; na ɛno akyiri no, ɔnkum ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ aboa no; 20na ɔsɔfoɔ no nhye ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ ne aduane afɔdeɛ no afɔrebukyia no so, na ɔsɔfoɔ no mpata mma no na ne ho ate.
21Na sɛ ɔdi hia na ne nsa anso yeinom so a, ɛnneɛ ɔmfa odwanten ba baako mmɛyɛ asodie ho afɔdeɛ nyɛ ohim afɔdeɛ mfa mpata mma no, ne aduane afɔdeɛ esiam olonka abupɛn du mu baako a wɔde ngo afɔre, ne ngo toa ma 22 ne anyankuku mmienu anaa mmorɔnoma mma mmienu a ne nsa bɛso soɔ; baako nyɛ bɔne ho afɔdeɛ na baako nyɛ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ; 23na n’ahodwira da a ɛtɔ so nwɔtwe no, ɔmfa mmrɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano, AWURADE anim. 24Na ɔsɔfoɔ no mfa asodie ho afɔdeɛ dwanten ba no ne ngo toa ma no, na ɔnhim no ohim afɔdeɛ, AWURADE anim. 25Na ɔnkum asodie ho afɔdeɛ dwanten ba no, na ɔsɔfoɔ no mfa asodie ho afɔdeɛ mogya no bi nkeka deɛ wɔrete ne ho no aso nifa ne ne nsa nifa kokurobetie ne ne nan nifa kokurobetie ano; 26na ɔsɔfoɔ no mfa ngo no ngu ɔno ara ne nsa benkum mu, 27na ɔsɔfoɔ no mfa ne nsateaa nifa nka ngo a ɛwɔ ne nsa benkum mu no bi mpete mprɛnson, AWURADE anim; 28na ɔsɔfoɔ no mfa ngo a ɛwɔ ne nsam no bi nkeka deɛ wɔrete ne ho no aso nifa ne ne nsa nifa kokurobetie ne ne nan nifa kokurobetie ano, deɛ asodie ho afɔdeɛ no mogya no wɔ no; 29na ngo a ɛbɛka ɔsɔfoɔ no nsam no, ɔnhwie ngu deɛ wɔrete ne ho no atifi mfa mpata mma no, AWURADE anim. 30Na ɔmfa anyankuku anaa mmorɔnoma mma a ne nsa bɛso soɔ no mu baako, 31adeɛ a ne nsa bɛso soɔ no mu baako nyɛ bɔne ho afɔdeɛ, na baako nyɛ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ mpae aduane afɔdeɛ no so, na ɔsɔfoɔ no mpata mma deɛ wɔrete ne ho no, AWURADE anim. 32Yei ne mmara a ɛda hɔ ma deɛ kwata atotɔ no a ne nsa nso n’ahodwira adeɛ soɔ no.
Adan a wɔagu ho fi
33Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron sɛ: 34Sɛ moduru Kanaan asase a mede merema mo sɛ monni soɔ no so, na sɛ mede kwata ntotɔeɛ metotɔ mo dibea asase no so fie bi ho a, 35 ɛnneɛ efie no wura no mmra mmɛka nkyerɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no sɛ: Ɛyɛ me sɛ biribi a ɛte sɛ ntotɔeɛ wɔ me fie hɔ. 36Na ɔsɔfoɔ no nhyɛ mma wɔnyi efie no mu nnoɔma mfiri adi ansa na ɔsɔfoɔ no ahyɛne mu akɔhwɛ ntotɔeɛ no, na efie no mu nnoɔma nyinaa ho angu fi; na ɛno akyiri no ɔsɔfoɔ no nhyɛne mu nkɔhwɛ efie no. 37 Na ɔsɔfoɔ no hwɛ ntotɔeɛ no, na sɛ ntotɔeɛ no wɔ efie no fasuo ho, nkekaeɛ apopobibire anaa kɔkɔɔ, na ani atotɔ mu asene ɔfasuo no a, 38ɔsɔfoɔ no mfiri efie no mu mmra ɛpono ano, na ɔnto efie no mu nnanson. 39Na sɛ ɛda a ɛtɔ so nson no ɔsɔfoɔ no sane ba, na ɔbɛhwɛ, na sɛ ntotɔeɛ no ayerɛ efie no fasuo ho a, 40ɔsɔfoɔ no mma wɔntutu aboɔ a ntotɔeɛ no wɔ mu no nto ngu kuro no akyi deɛ ɛhɔ nteɛ; 41na wɔnwewɛre efie no mu nhyia, na wɔmfa dɔteɛ a wɔwewɛreeɛ no nkɔgu kuro no akyi deɛ ɛhɔ nteɛ; 42na wɔmfa aboɔ foforɔ nhyehyɛ aboɔ no ananmu, na wɔmfa dɔteɛ foforɔ mma efie no ho.
43Na sɛ aboɔ no tutuo ne efie no ho wewerɛ ne ɛho ma akyiri no ntotɔeɛ no sane bɛpue efie no mu, 44na ɔsɔfoɔ no ba na ɔbɛhwɛ, na sɛ ntotɔeɛ no ayerɛ efie no mu a, ɛyɛ efie no mu kwata a ɛsɛe adeɛ; ɛho nte. 45Enti ɔnnwiri efie no ngu fam, n’aboɔ ne ne mpuna ne efie no ho dɔteɛ nyinaa, na ɔnsesa mfiri adi nkɔ kuro no akyi nkɔgu deɛ ɛhɔ nteɛ. 46 Na deɛ ɔbɛkɔ efie no mu nna a wɔato mu nyinaa no, ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ, 47na deɛ ɔda efie hɔ no nsi ne ntadeɛ, na deɛ ɔdidi fie hɔ no nsi ne ntadeɛ.
48Na sɛ efie no ho ma akyi ɔsɔfoɔ no ba bɛhwɛ, na sɛ ntotɔeɛ no nyerɛɛ efie no mu a, ɛnneɛ ɔsɔfoɔ no mmu efie no sɛ ɛho te, ɛfiri sɛ ntotɔeɛ no asa. 49Na ɔmfa nnomaa mmienu ne tweneduro dua ne koogyan ne adwera nnwira efie no. 50 Na ɔnkum nnomaa no mu baako ayowa mu, mmasuo so, 51na ɔmfa tweneduro dua ne adwera ne koogyan ne anomaa animono no mmɔ anomaa a wɔaku no no mogya ne mmasuo no mu, na ɔmfa mpete efie no ho mprɛnson, 52na ɔmfa anomaa no mogya ne mmasuo ne anomaa animono no ne tweneduro dua ne adwera ne koogyan no nnwira efie no, 53 na ɔnnyaa anomaa animono no kuro no akyi mma no nkɔ wiram, na ɔmpata mma efie no, na ɛho ate. 54Yei ne mmara a ɛda hɔ ma kwata ntotɔeɛ nyinaa ne ntutuiɛ, 55ne ntoma ne efie ho kwata, 56nsoa ne ntwintwameeɛ ne ntampeɛ, 57sɛ ɛnkyerɛkyerɛ berɛ a adeɛ ho nteɛ ne berɛ a ɛho teɛ mu; yei ne kwata ho mmara.

Sexual Uncleanness
1The Lord told Moses and Aaron 2to say to the community of Israel:
Any man with an infected penis is unclean, 3whether it is stopped up or keeps dripping. 4Anything that he rests on or sits on is also unclean, 5-7and if you touch either these or him, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
8If you are spit on by the man, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 9-10Any saddle or seat on which the man sits is unclean. And if you touch or carry either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 11If the man touches you without first washing his hands, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 12Any clay pot that he touches must be destroyed, and any wooden bowl that he touches must be washed.
13Seven days after the man gets well, he will be considered clean, if he washes his clothes and takes a bath in spring water. 14On the eighth day he must bring either two doves or two pigeons to the front of my sacred tent and give them to a priest. 15The priest will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me, then I will consider the man completely clean.
16Any man who has a flow of semen must take a bath, but he still remains unclean until evening. 17If the semen touches anything made of cloth or leather, these must be washed, but they still remain unclean until evening. 18After having sex, both the man and the woman must take a bath, but they still remain unclean until evening.
19When a woman has her monthly period, she remains unclean for seven days, and if you touch her, you must take a bath, but you remain unclean until evening. 20-23Anything that she rests on or sits on is also unclean, and if you touch either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 24Any man who has sex with her during this time becomes unclean for seven days, and anything he rests on is also unclean.
25Any woman who has a flow of blood outside her regular monthly period is unclean until it stops, just as she is during her monthly period. 26Anything that she rests on or sits on during this time is also unclean, just as it would be during her period. 27If you touch either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
28Seven days after the woman gets well, she will be considered clean. 29On the eighth day, she must bring either two doves or two pigeons to the front of my sacred tent and give them to a priest. 30He will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me; then I will consider the woman completely clean.
31When any of you are unclean, you must stay away from the rest of the community of Israel. Otherwise, my sacred tent will become unclean, and the whole nation will die.
32-33These are the things you men must do if you become unclean because of an infected penis or if you have a flow of semen. And these are the things you women must do when you become unclean either because of your monthly period or an unusual flow of blood. This is also what you men must do if you have sex with a woman who is unclean.

Mmarima ahosene fi
1Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron sɛ: 2 Monkasa nkyerɛ Israelfoɔ no nse wɔn sɛ: Ɔbarima biara sɛ ne ho sene gu a, n’ahosene no nti ne ho nte. 3Na deɛ ɛgu ne ho fi n’ahosene no mu nie: Sɛ n’ahosene firi ne honam anaasɛ n’ahosene ma ne honam ano si a, ɛyɛ ne ho figuo. 4Mpa biara a deɛ ne ho sene no bɛda so no ho nte, na adeɛ biara a ɔbɛtena soɔ no ho nte. 5Na deɛ ɔka ne mpa no nsi ne ntadeɛ na ɔmfa nsuo nnware, na ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ; 6na deɛ ɔtena adeɛ a deɛ ne ho sene no tenaa soɔ no, ɔnsi ne ntadeɛ na ɔmfa nsuo nnware, na ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ. 7Na deɛ ɔka deɛ ne ho sene no honam no, ɔnsi ne ntadeɛ na ɔmfa nsuo nnware na ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ; 8na sɛ deɛ ne ho sene no to ntasuo gu deɛ ne ho teɛ so a, ɔnsi ne ntadeɛ na ɔmfa nsuo nnware, na ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ. 9Na aboa so adwa biara a ɔhosenefoɔ no bɛtena soɔ no ho nte; na obiara a ɔka biribiara a ɛwɔ ɔhosenefoɔ no ase no ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ. 10Na deɛ ɔsoa saa adeɛ no nsi ne ntadeɛ na ɔmfa nsuo nnware, na ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ. 11Na obiara a ɔhosenefoɔ no amfa nsuo anhohoro ne nsa na ɔbɛka no no, ɔnsi ne ntadeɛ na ɔmfa nsuo nnware, na ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ. 12 Na kukuo a ɔhosenefoɔ no bɛka no, wɔmmɔ, na dua adeɛ biara deɛ, wɔmfa nsuo nhohoro ho.
13Na sɛ ɔhosenefoɔ no ho te firi n’ahosene no mu a, ɔnkan nnanson ngu n’ahofire so, na ɔnsi ne ntadeɛ, na ɔmfa mmasuo nnware ne honam, na ne ho ate. 14 Na da a ɛtɔ so nwɔtwe no, ɔmfa anyankuku mmienu anaa mmorɔnoma mma mmienu mmra AWURADE anim, ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano, na ɔmfa mma ɔsɔfoɔ no. 15Na ɔsɔfoɔ no mfa baako nyɛ bɔne ho afɔdeɛ, na baako no nso ɔmfa nyɛ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ, na ɔsɔfoɔ no mpata mma no AWURADE anim mfiri n’ahosene no mu.
16 Na sɛ ɔbarima bi ahoba firi ne mu a, ɔmfa nsuo nnware ne honam nyinaa, na ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ. 17Na ntoma biara anaa nwoma biara a ahoba bɛgu mu no, wɔmfa nsuo nsi, na ɛho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ. 18Na sɛ ɔbarima ne ɔbaa da na ahoba gu no a, wɔmfa nsuo nnware na wɔn ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ.
Mmaa ahosene fi
19 Na ɔbaa sɛ ne ho sene na mogya firi ne honam mu gu a, ɔntena ne nsabuo no mu nnanson, na obiara a ɔka no no ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ. 20Na adeɛ biara a ɔda soɔ ne nsabuo mu no ho nte, na adeɛ a ɔtena soɔ no ho nte. 21Na obiara a ɔka ne mpa no, ɔnsi ne ntadeɛ na ɔmfa nsuo nnware, na ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ; 22na obiara a ɔka adeɛ biara a watena soɔ no, ɔnsi ne ntadeɛ na ɔmfa nsuo nnware na ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ; 23na sɛ biribi wɔ mpa no so anaasɛ adeɛ a watena soɔ no so a, obi ka a, ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ. 24Na sɛ ɔbarima ne no da na ne nsabuo adeɛ no bi ka ne ho a, ne ho nte nnanson, na ne mpa a ɔda soɔ no nyinaa ho nte.
25Na ɔbaa sɛ ne ho sene mogya gu nna pii, na ɛnyɛ ne nsabuo berɛ, anaasɛ ne ho sene tra ne nsabuo a, ɛnneɛ n’ahosene a ɛho nteɛ nna no nyinaa ne ho nte te sɛ ne nsabuo nna mu. 26Ne mpa a ɔda soɔ biara n’ahosene nna nyinaa mu no nyɛ no sɛ ne nsabuo mpa, na adeɛ biara a ɔtena soɔ no ho nte sɛ ne nsabuo mu deɛ no. 27Na obiara a ɔka nnoɔma yi no ho nte, na ɔnsi ne ntadeɛ na ɔmfa nsuo nnware, ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ.
28Na sɛ ne ho te firi n’ahosene no mu a, ɔnkan nnanson mfa, na ɛno akyiri no ne ho ate. 29 Na da a ɛtɔ so nwɔtwe no, ɔmfa anyankuku mmienu anaa mmorɔnoma mma mmienu mmrɛ ɔsɔfoɔ, ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano. 30Na ɔsɔfoɔ no mfa baako mmɔ bɔne ho afɔdeɛ, na baako no ɔmfa mmɔ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ, na ɔsɔfoɔ no mpata mma no, AWURADE anim, mfiri n’ahosene a ɛho nteɛ no mu.
31Na momma Israelfoɔ no nyi wɔn ho mfiri wɔn fi mu, na wɔanwuwu wɔn fi mu sɛ wɔrekɔgu me tenabea a ɛwɔ wɔn mu no ho fi.
32Yei ne mmara a ɛda hɔ ma deɛ ne ho sene ne deɛ ne ho nsuo firi ne mu gu ne ho fi, 33ne ɔbaa a ne ho nyɛ no den ne nsabuo mu, ne deɛ ne ho sene, ɔbarima oo, ɔbaa oo, ne ɔbarima a ɔne ɔbaa a ne ho nteɛ bɛda.

english_text:
The Great Day of Forgiveness
1-2 Two of Aaron's sons had already lost their lives for disobeying the Lord, so the Lord told Moses to say to Aaron:
I, the Lord, appear in a cloud over the place of mercy on the sacred chest, which is behind the inside curtain of the sacred tent. And I warn you not to go there except at the proper time. Otherwise, you will die!
3 Before entering this most holy place, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for your sins and a ram as a sacrifice to please me. 4You will take a bath and put on the sacred linen clothes, including the underwear, the robe, the sash, and the turban. 5Then the community of Israel will bring you a ram and two goats, both of them males. The goats are to be used as sacrifices for sin, and the ram is to be used as a sacrifice to please me.
6Aaron, you must offer the bull as a sacrifice of forgiveness for your own sins and for the sins of your family. 7Then you will lead the two goats into my presence at the front of the sacred tent, 8where I will show you which goat will be sacrificed to me and which one will be sent into the desert to the demon Azazel. 9After you offer the first goat as a sacrifice for sin, 10the other one must be presented to me alive, before you send it into the desert to take away the sins of the people.
11You must offer the bull as a sacrifice to ask forgiveness for your own sins and for the sins of your family. 12Then you will take a fire pan of live coals from the bronze altar, together with two handfuls of finely ground incense, into the most holy place. 13There you will present them to me by placing the incense on the coals, so that the place of mercy will be covered with a cloud of smoke. Do this, or you will die right there! 14Next, use a finger to sprinkle some of the blood on the place of mercy, which is on the lid of the sacred chest; then sprinkle blood seven times in front of the chest.
15 Aaron, you must next sacrifice the goat for the sins of the people, and you must sprinkle its blood inside the most holy place, just as you did with the blood of the bull. 16By doing this, you will take away the sins that make both the most holy place and the people of Israel unclean. Do the same for the sacred tent, which is here among the people. 17Only you are allowed in the sacred tent from the time you enter until the time you come out. 18After leaving the tent, you will purify the bronze altar by smearing each of its four corners with some of the blood from the bull and from the goat. 19Use a finger to sprinkle the altar seven times with the blood, and it will be completely clean from the sins of the people.
20After you have purified the most holy place, the sacred tent, and the bronze altar, you must bring the live goat to the front of the tent. 21 There you will lay your hands on its head, while confessing every sin the people have committed, and you will appoint someone to lead the goat into the desert, so that it can take away their sins. 22Finally, this goat that carries the heavy burden of Israel's sins must be released deep in the desert.
23-24 Aaron, after this you must go inside the sacred tent, take a bath, put on your regular priestly clothes, and leave there the clothes you put on before entering the most holy place. Then you will come out and offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices for your sins and for the sins of the people. 25The fat from these sacrifices for sin must be sent up in smoke on the bronze altar.
26The one who led the goat into the desert and sent it off to the demon Azazel must take a bath and wash his clothes before coming back into camp. 27 The remains of the bull and the goat whose blood was taken into the most holy place must be taken outside the camp and burned. 28And whoever does this must take a bath and change clothes before coming back into camp.
The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
29 On the tenth day of the seventh month of each year, you must go without eating to show sorrow for your sins, and no one, including foreigners who live among you, is allowed to work. 30This is the day on which the sacrifice for the forgiveness of your sins will be made in my presence, 31and from now on, it must be celebrated each year. Go without eating and make this a day of complete rest just like the Sabbath. 32The high priest must offer the sacrifices for cleansing from sin, while wearing the sacred linen clothes. 33He will offer these sacrifices for the most holy place, the sacred tent, the bronze altar, all the priests, and for the whole community. 34You must celebrate this day each year—it is the Great Day of Forgiveness for all the sins of the people of Israel.
Moses did exactly as the Lord had commanded.
translation_text:
Mpata Da
1 Na Aaron mma baanu no wuo a wɔbaa AWURADE anim na wɔwuiɛ no akyiri no, AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose, 2 na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Kasa kyerɛ wo nua Aaron sɛ ɔnnhyɛne kronkronbea hɔ nnkɔ ntwamutam no akyi mpata adwa a ɛwɔ adaka no soɔ no anim berɛ nyinaa mu, na wanwu, ɛfiri sɛ mununkum no mu na meyi me ho mekyerɛ, mpata adwa no so. 3 Na yei ne deɛ Aaron mfa nhyɛne kronkronbea hɔ: Nantwininiburuwa a wɔde bɛbɔ bɔne ho afɔdeɛ ne odwennini a wɔde bɛbɔ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ. 4 Ɔnhyɛ nwera atadeɛ kronkron no, na nwera twakoto nkata ne ho, na nwera aboomu no mmɔ n’asene, na ɔmmɔ nwera abotitene no, yei ne ntade kronkron no; ɔmfa nsuo nnware ne ho ansa na wahyɛ. 5Na ɔnnye Israel asafo no hɔ mpapo mmienu, na wɔmfa mmɔ bɔne ho afɔdeɛ, ne odwennini baako, na wɔmfa mmɔ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ. 6 Na Aaron mfa bɔne ho afɔdeɛ nantwinini a ɛyɛ ne deɛ no mmra, na ɔmfa mpata mma ɔno ara ne ho ne ne fie. 7Na ɔmfa mpapo mmienu no mmɛgyina AWURADE anim, ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano. 8 Na Aaron ntwe mpapo mmienu no so tonto, AWURADE tonto baako ne Asasel tonto baako. 9Na Aaron mfa ɔpapo a AWURADE tonto bɔɔ no no mmra mmɛbɔ bɔne ho afɔdeɛ. 10Na ɔpapo a Asasel tonto bɔɔ no no, ɔmfa no animono nnyina AWURADE anim mfa mpata mma no na wɔnkɔgya no nkɔ serɛ so mma Asasel.
11Na Aaron mfa bɔne ho afɔdeɛ nantwinini a ɛyɛ ne deɛ no mmra mfa mpata mma ɔno ara ne ho ne ne fie, na ɔnkum bɔne ho afɔdeɛ nantwinini a ɛyɛ ne deɛ no. 12Na ɔmfa ogyasɔ adeɛ nnyansramma ma mfiri afɔrebukyia no so, AWURADE anim, ne aduhwam a wɔasi no fekɔfekɔ ne nsa mmienu ma, na ɔmfa nkɔ ntwamutam no akyi. 13Na ɔmfa aduhwam no ngu ogya no so, AWURADE anim, na aduhwam no wisie nkata mpata adwa a ɛwɔ Adanseɛ no soɔ no ho, na wanwu. 14Na ɔmfa nantwinini no mogya no bi, na ɔmfa ne nsateaa nka mpete mpata adwa no so anim fam, na ɔmfa ne nsateaa nka mogya no bi mpete mpata adwa no anim hɔ mprɛ nson.
15 Na ɔnkum bɔne ho afɔdeɛ papo a ɔyɛ ɔman no deɛ no, na ɔmfa ne mogya nkɔ ntwamutam no akyi, na ɔmfa mogya no nyɛ sɛdeɛ ɔde nantwinini no mogya no yɛeɛ no, na ɔmfa mpete mpata adwa no so ne mpata adwa no anim, 16 na ɔmpata mma kronkronbea no, Israelfoɔ no afideɛ, ne wɔn mmara a wɔto, wɔn bɔne nyinaa nti; na saa na ɔnyɛ mma ahyiaeɛ ntomadan a ɛsi wɔn mu ɛsiane wɔn afideɛ no nti. 17Na onipa biara nntena ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no mu, berɛ a ɔhyɛne hɔ kɔpata kronkronbea no mu, kɔsi sɛ ɔbɛfiri adie a wapata ama ɔno ara ne ne fie ne Israelfoɔ asafo nyinaa. 18 Na ɔmfiri adi mmra afɔrebukyia a ɛsi AWURADE anim no ho, na ɔmpata mma no, na ɔmfa nantwinini no mogya no bi ne ɔpapo no mogya no bi nkeka afɔrebukyia no mmɛn ho nhyia, 19na ɔmfa ne nsateaa nka mogya no bi mpete so mprɛ nson, na ɔnte ho nyɛ no kronkron mfiri Israelfoɔ no afideɛ mu.
20Na sɛ ɔpata ma kronkronbea ne ahyiaeɛ ntomadan ne afɔrebukyia no wie a, ɔmfa ɔpapo animono no mmra. 21Na Aaron mfa ne nsa mmienu ngu ɔpapo animono no atifi, na ɔnka Israelfoɔ no mfomsoɔ nyinaa ne wɔn mmarato nyinaa sɛdeɛ wɔn bɔne teɛ no ɔmfa ngu ɔpapo no atifi, na ɔmma ɔbarima bi a ɔwɔ hɔ nkɔgyaa no mma no nkɔ ɛserɛ so, 22na ɔpapo no nsoa wɔn mfomsoɔ nyinaa mfa nkɔ asase fo so.
23Na Aaron nhyɛne ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no mu, na ɔnyi nwera atadeɛ a ɔhyɛ kɔɔ kronkronbea no, na ɔnnya no hɔ. 24Na ɔmfa nsuo nnware ne ho deɛ ɛhɔ yɛ kronkron, na ɔnhyɛ ne ntadeɛ na ɔmfiri adi nkɔbɔ ne hyeɛ afɔdeɛ ne ɔman no hyeɛ afɔdeɛ, na ɔmpata mma ɔno ara ne ho ne ɔman no. 25Na ɔnhye bɔne ho afɔdeɛ sradeɛ no afɔrebukyia no so. 26Na deɛ ɔde ɔpapo no kɔ kɔgyaa no maa Asasel no nsi ne ntadeɛ, na ɔmfa nsuo nnware ne ho, na ɛno akyi ansa na ɔmmra nsraban no mu. 27 Na bɔne ho afɔdeɛ nantwinini ne bɔne ho afɔdeɛ papo a wɔde wɔn mogya kɔɔ kronkronbea hɔ kɔpataeɛ no, wɔmfa wɔn mfiri nkɔ nsraban no akyi, na wɔmfa ogya nhye wɔn nwoma ne wɔn nam ne wɔn agyanan. 28Na deɛ ɔkɔ kɔhyeeɛ no nsi ne ntadeɛ na ɔmfa nsuo nnware ne ho, na ɛno akyi ansa na waba nsraban no mu.
29Na yei nyɛ mo daa ahyɛdeɛ: Bosome a ɛtɔ so nson no da a ɛtɔ so du no, mommrɛ mo ho ase, kuromani oo, ɔhɔhoɔ a ɔbɛsoɛ mo mu oo, monnyɛ adwuma biara. 30 Na da no na wɔpata ma mo de dwira mo, na mo ho ate afiri mo bɔne nyinaa mu, AWURADE anim. 31Ɛnyɛ mo ɔhome mu homeda na mommrɛ mo ho ase: Ɛyɛ daa ahyɛdeɛ. 32Na mpata no, ɔsɔfoɔ a wɔasra no ngo a wɔde ahyɛ ne nsa sɛ ɔnni sɔfoɔ nsi n’agya ananmu no na ɔmpata, na ɔnhyɛ nwera ntadeɛ no, ntade kronkron no, 33na ɔmpata mma kronkronbea kronkron no, na ɔmpata mma ahyiaeɛ ntomadan ne afɔrebukyia no, na ɔmpata mma ɔsɔfoɔ no ne ɔman asafo mu no nyinaa. 34Na yei nyɛ mo daa ahyɛdeɛ na wɔde apata ama Israelfoɔ afiri wɔn bɔne nyinaa mu prɛko daa afirinhyia. Na Mose yɛɛ sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ no no.

english_text:
Where To Offer Sacrifices
1The Lord told Moses 2to tell Aaron, his sons, and everyone else in Israel:
3-4Whenever you kill any of your cattle, sheep, or goats as sacrifices to me, you must do it at the entrance to the sacred tent. If you don't, you will be guilty of pouring out blood, and you will no longer belong to the community of Israel. 5And so, when you sacrifice an animal to ask my blessing, it must not be done out in a field, 6but in front of the sacred tent. Then a priest can splatter its blood against the bronze altar and send its fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 7Don't ever turn from me again and offer sacrifices to goat-demons. This law will never change.
8Remember! No one in Israel, including foreigners, is to offer a sacrifice anywhere 9except at the entrance to the sacred tent. If you do, you will no longer belong to my people.
Do Not Eat Blood
The Lord said:
10 I will turn against any of my people who eat blood. This also includes any foreigners living among you. 11 Life is in the blood, and I have given you the blood of animals to sacrifice in place of your own. 12That's also why I have forbidden you to eat blood. 13Even if you should hunt and kill a bird or an animal, you must drain out the blood and cover it with soil.
14The life of every living creature is in its blood. That's why I have forbidden you to eat blood and why I have warned you that anyone who does will no longer belong to my people.
15If you happen to find a dead animal and eat it, you must take a bath and wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening. 16If you don't take a bath, you will suffer for what you did wrong.
translation_text:
Mmoa no kum
1Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 2Kasa kyerɛ Aaron ne ne mma ne Israelfoɔ nyinaa, na ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Yei ne asɛm a AWURADE ahyɛ ho mmara sɛ: 3Obiara a ɔwɔ Israel fie a ɔkum nantwie anaa odwanten anaa abirekyie nsraban no mu anaasɛ ɔku no nsraban no akyire, 4 na ɔmfa mma ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano mmɛyɛ ayɛyɛdeɛ mma AWURADE wɔ tenabea anim no, wɔbɛbu mogya agu ne so, waka mogya agu, na wɔbɛtwa saa onipa no afiri ne man mu atwene, 5na ama Israelfoɔ de wɔn afɔdeɛ a wɔkum wɔ ɛserɛ soɔ no abrɛ asɔfoɔ no ama wɔde abrɛ AWURADE wɔ ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano, na wɔakum abɔ AWURADE asomdwoeɛ afɔdeɛ. 6Na ɔsɔfoɔ no mfa mogya no mpete AWURADE afɔrebukyia no so, ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano, na ɔnhye sradeɛ no na ɛnyi hwa hwanhwam mma AWURADE.
7 Na wɔnnkum wɔn afɔrebɔdeɛ mmma mpapo abosom a wɔdi wɔn akyiri adwamammɔ soɔ no bio. Na ɛnyɛ daa ahyɛdeɛ mma wɔn, wɔn awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ nyinaa mu. 8Na wɔn deɛ, ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Obiara a ɔfiri Israel fie anaa ahɔhoɔ a wɔabɛsoɛ wɔn mu no mu a ɔbɛbɔ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ anaa okum afɔdeɛ bie, 9 na wamfa amma ahyiaeɛ ntomadan ano ammɛbɔ amma AWURADE no, wɔbɛtwa no afiri ne man mu atwene.
10 Na obiara a ɔfiri Israel fie anaa ahɔhoɔ a wɔabɛsoɛ wɔn mu no mu a ɔdi mogya biara no, mɛma m’ani asa saa ɔkra a ɔdi mogya no, na matwa no afiri ne man mu atwene. 11 Ɛfiri sɛ ɔhonam biara nkwa wɔ mogya no mu, na mede ama mo, afɔrebukyia no so sɛ wɔmfa mpata mma mo ho; na mogya na wɔde pata ma ɔkra. 12Ɛno nti na mese Israelfoɔ sɛ: Mo mu biara nnni mogya, na ɔhɔhoɔ a wabɛsoɛ mo mu no nso nnni mogya. 13Na obiara a ɔfiri Israel mma ne ahɔhoɔ a wɔabɛsoɛ mo mu no a wɔyɛ ha kum aboa anaa anomaa a wɔdie no, wɔnhwie ne mogya ngu na wɔmfa dɔteɛ nkata so. 14 Na ɔhonam nyinaa deɛ, ne mogya ne ne nkwa, enti na mese Israelfoɔ sɛ: Monnni nam biara mogya, ɛfiri sɛ honam nyinaa nkwa ne ne mogya; obiara a ɔdie no, wɔbɛtwa no atwene.
15 Na obiara a ɔdi deɛ wawuo anaasɛ deɛ wɔatete no, kuromani oo, ɔhɔhoɔ oo, ɔnsi ne ntadeɛ na ɔmfa nsuo nnware, na ne ho nte kɔsi anwummerɛ ansa na ne ho ate; 16na sɛ wansi ne ntadeɛ na wannware ne ho a, ɛnneɛ ɔnsoa ne mmusuo.

english_text:
Forbidden Sex
1The Lord told Moses 2to tell the people of Israel:
I am the Lord your God! 3So don't follow the customs of Egypt where you used to live or those of Canaan where I am bringing you. 4I am the Lord your God, and you must obey my teachings. 5 Obey them and you will live. I am the Lord.
6Don't have sex with any of your close relatives, 7especially your own mother. This would disgrace your father. 8 And don't disgrace him by having sex with any of his other wives. 9 Don't have sex with your sister or stepsister, whether you grew up together or not. 10Don't disgrace yourself by having sex with your granddaughter 11or half sister 12-13 or a sister of your father or mother. 14Don't disgrace your uncle by having sex with his wife. 15 Don't have sex with your daughter-in-law 16 or sister-in-law. 17 And don't have sex with the daughter or granddaughter of any woman that you have earlier had sex with. You will be having sex with her closest relatives, and that would make you unclean. 18As long as your wife is alive, don't cause trouble for her by taking one of her sisters as a second wife.
19 When a woman is having her monthly period, she is unclean, so don't have sex with her.
20 Don't have sex with another man's wife—that would make you unclean.
21 Don't sacrifice your children on the altar fires to the god Molech. I am the Lord your God, and that would disgrace me.
22 It is disgusting for a man to have sex with another man.
23 Anyone who has sex with an animal is unclean.
24Don't make yourselves unclean by any of these disgusting practices of those nations that I am forcing out of the land for you. They made themselves 25and the land so unclean, that I punished the land because of their sins, and I made it vomit them up. 26-27Now don't do these sickening things that make the land filthy. Instead, obey my laws and teachings. 28Then the land won't become sick of you and vomit you up, just as it did them. 29-30If any of you do these vulgar, disgusting things, you will be unclean and no longer belong to my people. I am the Lord your God, and I forbid you to follow their sickening way of life.
translation_text:
Nna mu akyiwadeɛ
1Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 2Kasa kyerɛ Israelfoɔ na ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Mene AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn. 3 Misraim asase a motenaa soɔ no so nneyɛɛ deɛ, monnyɛ. Na Kanaan asase a mede mo rekɔ soɔ no so nneyɛɛ nso, monnyɛ, na monnni wɔn ahyɛdeɛ so. 4M’atemmudeɛ na monyɛ, na monkora m’ahyɛdeɛ sɛ mobɛdi soɔ. 5 Mene AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn. Na monkora m’ahyɛdeɛ ne m’atemmudeɛ a onipa a ɔyɛ no bɛnya mu nkwa no. Mene AWURADE.
6Obiara nnkɔ ne bogya biara a ɔyɛ ne honam no ho nnkɔyi n’adagya so. Mene AWURADE. 7Nyi w’agya anaa wo na adagya so; wo na ne no, nyi n’adagya so. 8 Nyi w’agya yere adagya so; w’agya adagya ne no. 9 Wo nuabaa a ɔyɛ w’agya ba anaa wo na ba no, wɔwoo no efie oo, wɔwoo no baabi oo, nyi wɔn adagya so. 10Wo babanin babaa anaa wo babaa babaa, nyi wɔn adagya so, ɛfiri sɛ ɛyɛ w’adagya. 11W’agya yere babaa a w’agya awo no no, ɔyɛ wo nuabaa, nyi n’adagya so. 12Nyi w’agya nuabaa adagya so; ɔyɛ w’agya honam. 13Nyi wo na nuabaa adagya so, ɛfiri sɛ ɔyɛ wo na honam. 14Nyi w’agya nuabarima adagya so nkɔ ne yere ho; wo na kumaa ne no. 15 Nyi w’ase adagya so; wo babarima yere ne no, nyi n’adagya so. 16 Nyi wo nua yere adagya so; ɛyɛ wo nua adagya. 17 Nyi ɔbaa bi ne ne ba adagya so; mfa ne babanin babaa anaa ne babaa babaa nyi wɔn adagya so; ne honam ne wɔn; ɛyɛ abusudeɛ. 18Na mfa ɔbaa ne ne nua nware sɛ wobɛma wɔatwe kora, sɛ ɔda so te aseɛ no, wobɛyi n’adagya so aka ne ho.
19 Na nkɔ ɔbaa a ne nsabuo mu ne ho nteeɛ no ho nkɔyi n’adagya so. 20 Na wo ne wo yɔnko yere nnna, na mfa wo ho nsuo mma no mfa ngu wo ne no ho fi. 21 Na mfa w’asefoɔ mu bi mmɔ afɔdeɛ mmma Molek, na ngu wo Nyankopɔn din ho fi; mene AWURADE. 22 Na wo ne ɔbarima nnna ɔbaa nna; ɛyɛ akyiwadeɛ. 23 Wo ne aboa biara nnna mmfa nngu wo ho fi; na ɔbaa bi nnnyina aboa bi anim nnnane ne ho mmma no; ɛyɛ basabasayɛ.
24Mommfa nnoɔma yi biara nngu mo ho fi, ɛfiri sɛ yeinom nyinaa na amanaman a merebɛtu wɔn afiri mo anim yi de agu wɔn ho fi, 25na asase no so agu fi, enti na meretua ɛso amumuyɛ no so ka, na asase no afe ɛsotefoɔ no agu. 26Na mo deɛ, monni m’ahyɛdeɛ ne m’atemmudeɛ so, na monnyɛ saa akyiwadeɛ yi mu biara, kuromani oo, ɔhɔhoɔ a wabɛsoɛ mo mu oo, 27ɛfiri sɛ saa akyiwadeɛ yi nyinaa na asase no sofoɔ a wɔdi mo anim no ayɛ, na asase no so agu fi. 28Na asase no amfe mo angu sɛ moagu ho fi, sɛdeɛ ɛfee amanaman a wɔdii mo anim no guiɛ no. 29Na obiara a ɔbɛyɛ saa akyiwadeɛ yi mu biara no, wɔbɛtwa wɔn a wɔyɛ no afiri wɔn man mu atwene. 30Enti monhwɛ m’ahwɛdeɛ, na moanyɛ ahyɛdeɛ a wɔkyire a wɔdii mo anim yɛeɛ no amfa angu mo ho fi: Mene AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn.

english_text:
Moral and Religious Laws
1The Lord told Moses 2 to say to the community of Israel:
I am the Lord your God. I am holy, and you must be holy too! 3-4 Respect your father and your mother, honor the Sabbath, and don't make idols or images. I am the Lord your God.
5When you offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, be sure to follow my instructions. 6You may eat the meat either on the day of the sacrifice or on the next day, but you must burn anything left over on the third day. 7If you eat any of it on the third day, the sacrifice will be disgusting to me, and I will reject it. 8In fact, you will be punished for not respecting what I say is holy, and you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
9 When you harvest your grain, always leave some of it standing along the edges of your fields and don't pick up what falls on the ground. 10Don't strip your grapevines clean or gather the grapes that fall off the vines. Leave them for the poor and for those foreigners who live among you. I am the Lord your God.
11 Do not steal or tell lies or cheat others.
12 Do not misuse my name by making promises you don't intend to keep. I am the Lord your God.
13 Do not steal anything or cheat anyone, and don't fail to pay your workers at the end of each day.
14 I am the Lord your God, and I command you not to make fun of the deaf or to cause a blind person to stumble.
15 Be fair, no matter who is on trial—don't favor either the poor or the rich.
16Don't be a gossip, but never hesitate to speak up in court, especially if your testimony can save someone's life.
17 Don't hold grudges. On the other hand, it's wrong not to correct someone who needs correcting. 18 Don't be angry or try to take revenge. I am the Lord, and I command you to love others as much as you love yourself.
