The whole lampstand, including its decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered gold 32with three branches on each of its two sides. 33There are to be three decorative almond blossoms on each branch 34and four on the stem. 35There must also be a blossom where each pair of branches comes out from the stem. 36The lampstand, including its branches and decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered pure gold. 37The lamp on the top and those at the end of each of its six branches must be made so as to shine toward the front of the lampstand. 38The tongs and trays for taking care of the lamps are to be made of pure gold. 39The lampstand and its equipment will require 35 kilograms of pure gold, 40 and they must be made according to the pattern I showed you on the mountain.
translation_text:
Ntamadan ho afɔrebɔde
(Eksodɔs 35.4-9)
1Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 2 Ka kyerɛ Israelfo no na wɔmmɛma me soma afɔrebɔde. Obiara a ne koma ka no nkyɛn na munnye me soma afɔrebɔde. 3Na eyi ne soma afɔrebɔde a munnye wɔn nkyɛn no: sika ne dwetɛ ne kɔbere mfrafrae, 4ne bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fufu ne mmirekyi nwi, 5ne adwennini nhoma a wɔahyɛ no kɔkɔɔ ne sukraman nhoma ne ɔkanto nnua, 6kanea ho ngo, ɔsra ngo ne nnuhuam a wɔhyew ho nnuru, 7apopobibiri abo ne abo a wɔde besisi asɔfotade no ne adɛbo no mu no. 8Na ma wɔnyɛ tenabea kronkron mma me na mentena wɔn mu. 9 Sɛnea me ara merebɛkyerɛ wo tenabea no tebea ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa tebea no nyinaa no, saa ara na monyɛ no.
Apam adaka no yɛbea
(Eksodɔs 37.1-9)
10 Na wɔmfa ɔkanto nyɛ adaka a ne tenten bɛyɛ basafa biako ne fa, na ne tɛtrɛtɛ bɛyɛ anammɔn abien ne fa, na ne korɔn bɛyɛ anammɔn abien ne fa. 11Na fa sika amapa dura ho, emu ne ɛho nyinaa na dura, na yɛ sika hankare twa ho hyia. 12Na gu sika nkaa anan, na fa tuatua ne nan anan no ho; nkaa abien nni ɔfa ha, na nkaa abien nni ɔfa ha. 13Na fa ɔkanto sinsen mpoma, na fa sika dura ho. 14Na fa poma no wurawura nkaa no mu wɔ adaka no nkyɛn mu, na wɔmfa nsoa adaka no. 15Mpoma no nwurawura adaka no ho nkaa no mu; wonnyiyi mmfi mu. 16 Na fa Adanse a mede mɛma wo no hyɛ adaka no mu.
17 Na fa sika amapa yɛ mpata agua, ne tenten bɛyɛ basafa biako ne fa, na ne tɛtrɛtɛ bɛyɛ anammɔn abien ne fa. 18Na yɛ sika kerubim abien, ɔboro adwuma na fa yɛ, na fa sisi mpata agua no ti abien no so. 19Na yɛ kerub biako wɔ ti ha ne kerub biako wɔ ti ha. Mpata agua no mu na momma kerubim no nyi adi wɔ ne ti abien no so. 20Na kerubim no ntrɛtrɛw wɔn ntaban mu ɔsoro mfa wɔn ntaban no nkata mpata agua no so, na wɔn ani nkyerɛkyerɛ wɔn ho; mpata agua no so na kerubim no ani nkyerɛkyerɛ. 21 Na fa mpata agua no si adaka no so, na adaka no mu na fa Adanse a mede mɛma wo no hyɛ. 22 Na ɛhɔ na me ne wo behyia, na mafi mpata agua no so wɔ kerubim abien a wɔwɔ Adanse adaka no so no ntam maka wo nneɛma a mɛhyɛ wo sɛ fa kyerɛ Israelfo no nyinaa.
Ɔpon no ho nhyehyɛe
(Eksodɔs 37.10-16)
23 Na fa ɔkanto yɛ ɔpon, ne tenten basafa baako, na ne tɛtrɛtɛ anammɔn biako ne fa, na ne korɔn bɛyɛ anammɔn abien ne fa. 24Na fa sika amapa dura ho, na fa sika hankare twa ho hyia. 25Na yɛ ɛho mfomfamho a ne trɛw te sɛ nsam hyia, na fa sika hankare twa mfomfamho no ho hyia. 26Na yɛ sika nkaa anan, na fa nkaa no sisi ntwea anan a ɛwowɔ ne nan ho no so. 27Mfomfamho no ase pa ara na nkaa no nni, na ɛnyɛ nea wɔde mpoma bewurawura mu de asoa ɔpon no. 28Na fa ɔkanto sinsen mpoma no, na fa sika duradura ho, na wɔde asoa ɔpon no. 29Na yɛ ɛso nsanka ne nsankawa ne nkora ne nkuruwa a wɔde behwie; sika amapa na fa yɛ. 30 Na fa kyerɛ abodoo sisi ɔpon no so wɔ m'anim daa yi.
Kaneadua no
(Eksodɔs 37.17-24)
31 Na fa sika amapa yɛ kaneadua; ɔboro adwuma na fa yɛ kaneadua no, ne nan ne ne dua; ɛho nhwiren no nkuramu, ne kukuduuduu ne ne nhwiren no mfi ɛno ara mu. 32Na nsa asia ntuatua ho, kaneadua no nsa abiɛsa ntuatua ɔfa ha, na kaneadua no nsa abiɛsa nso ntuatua ɔfa ha. 33Nhwiren nkuramu abiɛsa a ɛte sɛ ɔsonkoran de wɔ nsa biako ho, ne kukuduuduu ne ne nhwiren, na nhwiren nkuramu abiɛsa a ɛte sɛ ɔsonkoran de wɔ nsa biako ho, ne kukuduuduu ne ne nhwiren. Saa ara na yɛ wɔ nsa asia a etuatua kaneadua no ho no ho. 34Na kaneadua no ho, nhwiren nkuramu a ɛte sɛ ɔsonkoran de anan, ne kukuduuduu ne ne nhwiren. 35Na kukuduuduu nsisi nsa abien abien a etuatua ho no ase, wɔ nsa asia a etuatua kaneadua no mu no ase. 36Ɛho kukuduuduu ne ɛho nsa no mfi mu ara, ne nyinaa sika amapa na wɔmfa nyɛ no ɔboro adwuma biako. 37Na yɛ ɛso akanea asɔn, na wɔmfa n'akanea no nsisi so, na ɛnnɛw wɔ anim nkyerɛ fa hɔ. 38Na ɛho adabaw ne ho nso nkukuwa nyɛ sika amapa. 39Sika amapa dwetikɛse biako na wɔmfa nyɛ, ne ɛho nneɛma yi nyinaa. 40 Na hwɛ na yɛ no sɛnea ne nsusuwso a wɔde akyerɛ wo bepɔw no so no te no.

english_text:
Curtains and Coverings for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 36.8-19)
The Lord said to Moses:
1The top of the sacred tent must be made from ten pieces of the finest linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. 2Make each piece twelve meters long and two meters wide 3and sew them together into two panels with five sections each. 4-6Put 50 loops of blue cloth along one of the wider sides of each panel, then fasten the two panels at the loops with 50 gold hooks.
7-8As the material for protecting the tent, use goat hair to weave eleven sections of cloth 13 meters by 2 meters each. 9Sew five of the sections together to make one panel. Then sew the other six together to make a second panel, and fold the sixth section double over the front of the tent. 10Put 50 loops along one of the wider sides of each panel 11and fasten the two panels at the loops with 50 bronze hooks. 12-13The panel of goat hair will be a meter longer than the tent itself, so fold 50 centimeters of the material behind the tent and on each side as a protective covering. 14Make two more coverings—one with tanned ram skins and the other with fine leather.
The Framework for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 36.20-34)
The Lord said:
15Build a framework of acacia wood for the walls of the sacred tent. 16Make each frame 4 meters high and 66 centimeters wide 17with two wooden pegs near the bottom. 18-21Place two silver stands under each frame with sockets for the pegs, so the frames can be joined together. Put 20 of these frames along the south side and 20 more along the north. 22For the back wall along the west side use six frames 23-24with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. Make certain that these corner frames are joined from top to bottom. 25Altogether, this back wall will have eight frames with two silver stands under each one.
26-27Make five crossbars for each of the wooden frames, 28with the center crossbar running the full length of the wall. 29Cover the frames and the crossbars with gold and attach gold rings to the frames to run the crossbars through. 30Then set up the tent in the way I showed you on the mountain.
The Curtain inside the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 36.35-38)
The Lord said:
31-33 Make a curtain to separate the holy place from the most holy place. Use fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. Cover four acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a silver stand. Then fasten gold hooks to the posts and hang the curtain there.
34Inside the most holy place, put the sacred chest that has the place of mercy on its lid. 35Outside the most holy place, as you face the curtain, put the table for the sacred bread on the right side and the gold lampstand on the left.
36For the entrance to the tent, use a piece of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework. 37Cover five acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a bronze stand. Then put gold hooks on the posts and hang the curtain there.
translation_text:
Ntamadan no ho nhyehyɛe
(Eksodɔs 36.8-38)
1 Na tenabea no, yɛ no ntama du a ɛyɛ asaawa fitaa a wɔafira ne bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi. Yɛ emu kerubim a ɛyɛ ntamanwene mu adwinni. 2Ntama no biako tenten nyɛ basafa dunan, na ntama no biako tɛtrɛtɛ nyɛ basafa abien; ntama no nyinaa nsusuwii nyɛ biako. 3Wɔmfa ntama no anum ntoatoa so, biako ntoa biako so; na ntama no anum nso ntoatoa so, biako ntoa biako so. 4Na fa bibiri bobɔ ntama biako mmuano so nhentia wɔ ano wɔ ntoae no so. Saa ara na yɛ wɔ ntama a edi akyiri no mmuano so ntoae a ɛto so abien no so. 5Nhentia aduonum na bobɔ wɔ ntama biako ano, na nhentia aduonum nso na bobɔ wɔ ntama a ɛwɔ ntoae a ɛto so abien no so no ano; nhentia no nni mmɔanim. 6Na yɛ sika nkɔtɔkorɔ aduonum, na fa nkɔtɔkorɔ no yɛ ma ntama no biako ntoa biako so, na tenabea no nyɛ biako.
7Na fa mmirekyi nwi yɛ ntama, na fa yɛ tenabea no so ntamadan; yɛ no ntama dubiako. 8Ntama no biako tenten nyɛ basafa dunum, na ntama no biako tɛtrɛtɛ nyɛ basafa abien; ntama dubiako no nsusuwii nyɛ biako. 9Na fa ntama no mu anum toatoa yɛ no biako, na fa asia nso toatoa yɛ no biako, na bukaw ntama a ɛto so asia no ma ɛnkata ntamadan no so wɔ anim. 10Na bobɔ nhentia aduonum wɔ ntama biako a edi akyiri no mmuano so wɔ ntoae no so, ne nhentia aduonum nso wɔ ntoae a ɛto so abien no ntama no mmuano so. 11Na yɛ kɔbere nkɔtɔkoro aduonum, na fa nkɔtɔkorɔ no suso nhentia no mu, na ma ntamadan no ntoa nyɛ biako. 12Na ntamadan no ntama nkae a ɛboro so no, ntama fa no a aka no, nsensɛn tenabea no akyi. 13Na ntamadan no ntama no tenten no mu basafa biako a ɛboro so wɔ nkyɛn ha ne basafa biako a ɛboro so wɔ nkyɛn ha no nsensɛn tenabea no nkyɛn mu ne nkyɛn mu wɔ ha ne ha nkata so.
14Na fa adwennini nhoma a wɔahyɛ no kɔkɔɔ yɛ ntamadan no nkataso, na fa sukraman nhoma yɛ ɛno so nkataso.
15 Na fa ɔkanto yɛ tenabea no ntaaboo a esisi hɔ. 16Taaboo biako tenten nyɛ basafa anum, na taaboo biara tɛtrɛtɛ nyɛ bɛyɛ anammɔn abien ne fa. 17Nan abien ntuatua taaboo biako ase, na biribi nsuso nan biako ne biako mu; saa na yɛ tenabea no ntaaboo nyinaa ho. 18Na yɛ tenabea no ntaaboo no: Ntaaboo aduonu nni nifa fam nkyerɛ nifa. 19Na yɛ ntaaboo aduonu no ase dwetɛ nnyinaso aduanan, nnyinaso abien abien nhyehyɛ ntaaboo no mmiako mmiako ase mma ne nan abien abien no. 20Na tenabea no nkyɛn biako a edi benkum fam no, ntaaboo aduonu na enni hɔ, 21ne ne dwetɛ nnyinaso aduanan, ntaaboo no mmiako mmiako ase nnyinaso abien abien. 22Na tenabere no akyi fam a ɛkyerɛ atɔe no, yɛ hɔ ntaaboo asia. 23Na yɛ tenabea no akyi twea abien no so ntaaboo abien. 24Na ɛmpam ho mfi fam nkɔ, nanso ɛnyɛ mu nkodu ne hin so wɔ nea kaa a edi kan no tua hɔ; saa na n'abien nyinaa nyɛ, na enni twea abien no so. 25Na ɛnyɛ ntaaboo awotwe ne ne dwetɛ nnyinaso dunsia, taaboo biako ase nnyinaso abien ne taaboo biako no ase nnyinaso abien.
26 Na fa ɔkanto yɛ mmeamu; anum nyɛ tenabea no nkyɛn biako ntaaboo no de, 27na mmeamu anum nso nyɛ tenabea no nkyɛn biako no ntaaboo no de, na mmeamu anum nso nyɛ tenabea no akyi wɔ atɔe fam ntaaboo no de. 28Na mfinimfini mmeamu a ɛfa ntaaboo no mfinimfini no ntwam mfi ti nkodu ti. 29Na ntaaboo no, fa sika duradua ho, na fa sika yɛ ɛho nkaa no ma ɛnyɛ mmeamu no hyehyɛbea, na fa sika duradura mmeamu no ho nso. 30 Na si tenabea no sɛnea ne nsusuwso a wɔayi akyerɛ wo bepɔw no so no te no.
31 Na fa bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa a wɔafira yɛ mmɔhɔɔ; ntamanwene mu adwinni a kerubim wɔ mu na wɔnyɛ no. 32Na fa sensɛn ɔkanto adum anan a wɔaduradura ho sika ho; ne nkɔtɔkorɔ nyɛ sika, na ensisi dwetɛ nnyinaso anan so. 33 Na fa mmɔhɔɔ no sensɛn nsoam no ase, na fa Adanse adaka no besi mmɔhɔɔ no akyi, na mmɔhɔɔ no ntwa kronkronbea ne kronkron mu kronkronbea no mu mma mo. 34 Na fa mpata agua no si Adanse adaka no so wɔ kronkron mu kronkronbea hɔ. 35 Na fa ɔpon no si mmɔhɔɔ no anim, na kaneadua no nni ɔpon no ntentenso wɔ tenabea no nkyɛn mu nifa fam, na fa ɔpon no si nkyɛn mu benkum fam. 36Na fa bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa a wɔafira nwene nkyeremu fa yɛ ntamadan no ano nkataano. 37Na fa ɔkanto adum anum yɛ nkataano no, na fa sika duradura ho, na ne nkɔtɔkoro nyɛ sika, na fa kɔbere nnyinaso anum gu ase.

english_text:
The Altar for Offering Sacrifices
(Exodus 38.1-7)
The Lord said to Moses:
1Use acacia wood to build an altar 2.25 meters square and 1.34 meters high, 2and make each of the four top corners stick up like the horn of a bull. Then cover the whole altar with bronze, including the four horns. 3All the equipment for the altar must also be made of bronze—the pans for the hot ashes, the shovels, the sprinkling bowls, the meat forks, and the fire pans. 4-5Halfway up the altar build a ledge around it, and cover the bottom half of the altar with a decorative bronze grating. Then attach a bronze ring beneath the ledge at the four corners of the altar. 6-7Cover two acacia wood poles with bronze and put them through the rings for carrying the altar. 8Construct the altar in the shape of an open box, just as you were shown on the mountain.
The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 38.9-20)
The Lord said:
9-15Surround the sacred tent with a courtyard 44 meters long on the south and north and 22 meters wide on the east and west. Use 20 bronze posts on bronze stands for the south and north and 10 for the west. Then hang a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods.
Place three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hang a curtain 6.67 meters wide on each set of posts. 16Use four more of these posts for the entrance way, then hang on them an embroidered curtain of fine linen nine meters long and woven with blue, purple, and red wool.
17-18Make the curtains that surround the courtyard 2.25 meters high and hang them from the bronze posts with silver hooks and rods. 19Make the rest of the equipment for the sacred tent of bronze, including the pegs for the tent and for the curtain surrounding the courtyard.
The Oil for the Lamp in the Holy Place
(Leviticus 24.1-4)
The Lord said to Moses:
20Command the people of Israel to supply you with the purest olive oil. Do this so the lamp will keep burning 21in front of the curtain that separates the holy place from the most holy place, where the sacred chest is kept. Aaron and his sons are responsible for keeping the lamp burning every night in the sacred tent. The Israelites must always obey this command.
translation_text:
Afɔremuka no ho nhyehyɛe
1 Na fa ɔkanto yɛ afɔremuka no: ne tenten basafa abien ne fa ne tɛtrɛtɛ basafa abien ne fa; afɔremuka no nyɛ ahinanan, na ne sorokɔ nso nyɛ basafa biako ne fa. 2Na yɛ ne mmɛn sisi ne twɔtwɔw anan so; emu ara na ne mmɛn no mfi, na fa kɔbere dura ho. 3Na yɛ ɛho nseaa a wɔde ne nso begu mu, ne ne sesaw ade ne ne nkora ne n'adinam ne ne nsramma kukuwa, ɛho nneɛma nyinaa, kɔbere na fa yɛ. 4Na fa kɔbere nwene ntontan wɔ ho, sɛnea wɔnwene ɔtan, na yɛ ɔtan no so kɔbere nkaa anan wɔ ne twea anan no so. 5Na fa si afɔremuka no bamma ho wɔ ase, na ɔtan no nnu afɔremuka no mfinimfini. 6Na sinsen afɔremuka no ho mpoma, ɔkanto mpoma, na fa kɔbere duradura ho. 7Na wɔmfa mpoma no nwurawura nkaa no mu, na mpoma no nhyehyɛ afɔremuka no nkyɛn nkyɛn, na wɔde asoa. 8 Fa ntaaboo yɛ, na emu nna ɔkwan. Sɛnea wɔakyerɛ wo bepɔw no so no, saa ara na wɔnyɛ no.
Tenabea no adiwo
(Eksodɔs 38.9-20)
9 Na yɛ tenabea no adiwo! Na adiwo mmɔhɔɔ a wɔde asaawa fitaa a wɔafira anwene a ne tenten si basafa aduonum nni hɔ wɔ ɔfa biako wɔ nifa fam a ɛkyerɛ nifa, 10ne n'adum aduonu ne ne nnyinaso aduonu a wɔde kɔbere ayɛ; na adum no nkoropɛe ne ne mmeae nyɛ dwetɛ. 11Saa ara nso na benkum fam tenten mu no, mmɔhɔɔ a ne tenten basafa aduonum ne n'adum aduonu ne ne kɔbere nnyinaso aduonu nni; na adum no nkoropɛe ne ne mmeae no nyɛ dwetɛ. 12Na adiwo no tɛtrɛtɛ a ɛkyerɛ atɔe fam no, mmɔhɔɔ basafa aduonum anum nni hɔ; n'adum du ne ne nnyinaso du. 13Na adiwo no tɛtrɛtɛ a edi anim fam a ɛkyerɛ apuei nyɛ basafa aduonum anum: 14nkyɛn ha mmɔhɔɔ no nyɛ basafa ason ne fa, n'adum abiɛsa ne ne nnyinaso abiɛsa; 15na nkyɛn ha nso mmɔhɔɔ no nyɛ basafa ason ne fa, n'adum abiɛsa ne ne nnyinaso abiɛsa. 16Na adiwo no ano pon no nkataano nyɛ basafa du; wɔmfa bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa a wɔafira a ɛyɛ nkyeremu; n'adum anan ne ne nnyinaso anan. 17Adum no a etwa adiwo no ho hyia nyinaa mmeae a ɛbeabea ho nyɛ dwetɛ, ne nkɔtɔkorɔ nso nyɛ dwetɛ, na ne nnyinaso nyɛ kɔbere.
18Adiwo no tenten nyɛ basafa aduonum, na ne tɛtrɛtɛ nso nyɛ basafa aduonum anum, na ne korɔn nso basafa abien ne fa; mmɔhɔɔ no nyɛ nwera a wɔafira n'asaawa, na ne nnyinaso nyɛ kɔbere. 19Tenabea no ho som nyinaa mu adwinni nyinaa ne ne mmofunnua nyinaa ne adiwo no ho mmofunnua nyinaa nyɛ kɔbere.
Kanea no ngo
(Lewitikɔs 24.1-4)
20 Na wo nso hyɛ Israelfo no na wɔmmrɛ wo ngodua aba a wɔasiw ngo gyenennyenen, na wɔmfa nsɔ kanea no, na akanea no nsisi so daa yi; 21na Aaron ne ne mma nhwɛ so, ahyiae ntamadan no mu, ntwamu mmɔhɔɔ a ɛkata Adanse no anim no anim, mfi anwummere nkosi anɔpa wɔ AWURADE anim. Ɛnyɛ daa ahyɛde a Israelfo nni so, wɔn awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu.

english_text:
The Clothes for the High Priest
(Exodus 39.1-7)
The Lord said to Moses:
1Send for your brother Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. They are the ones I have chosen from Israel to serve as my priests. 2Make Aaron some beautiful clothes that are worthy of a high priest. 3Aaron is to be dedicated as my high priest, and his clothes must be made only by persons who possess skills that I have given them. 4Here are the items that need to be made: a breastpiece, a priestly vest, a robe, an embroidered shirt, a turban, and a sash. These sacred clothes are to be made for your brother Aaron and his sons who will be my priests. 5Use only gold and fine linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool, for making these clothes.
The Vest for the High Priest
(Exodus 39.2-7)
The Lord said:
6-8Make the entire priestly vest of fine linen skillfully woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and decorate it with gold. It is to have two shoulder straps to support it and a sash that fastens around the waist.
9-12Put two onyx stones in gold settings, then attach one to each of the shoulder straps. On one of these stones engrave the names of Israel's first six sons in the order of their birth. And do the same with his remaining six sons on the other stone. In this way Aaron will always carry the names of the tribes of Israel when he enters the holy place, and I will never forget my people.
13-14Attach two gold settings to the shoulder straps and fasten them with two braided chains of pure gold.
The Breastpiece for the High Priest
(Exodus 39.8-21)
The Lord said:
15From the same costly material make a breastpiece for the high priest to use in finding out what I want my people to do. 16It is to be 22 centimeters square and folded double 17with four rows of three precious stones: In the first row put a carnelian, a chrysolite, and an emerald; 18in the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond; 19in the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst; 20and in the fourth row a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. Mount the stones in delicate gold settings 21and engrave on each of them the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
22-25Attach two gold rings to the upper front corners of the breastpiece and fasten them with two braided gold chains to gold settings on the shoulder straps. 26Attach two other gold rings to the lower inside corners next to the vest 27and two more near the bottom of the shoulder straps right above the sash. 28Then take a blue cord and tie the two lower rings on the breastpiece to those on the vest. This will keep the breastpiece in place.
29In this way Aaron will have the names of the twelve tribes of Israel written on his heart each time he enters the holy place, and I will never forget my people. 30 He must also wear on his breastpiece the two small objects that he uses to receive answers from me.
The Other High-Priestly Clothes
(Exodus 39.22-26,30,31)
The Lord said:
31Under his vest Aaron must wear a robe of blue wool 32with an opening in the center for his head. Be sure to bind the material around the collar to keep it from wearing out. 33-34 Along the hem of the robe weave pomegranates of blue, purple, and red wool with a gold bell between each of them. 35If Aaron wears these clothes when he enters the holy place as my high priest, the sound of the bells will be heard, and his life will not be in danger.
36On a narrow strip of pure gold engrave the words: “Dedicated to the Lord.” 37Fasten it to the front of Aaron's turban with a blue cord, 38so he can wear it on his forehead. This will show that he will take on himself the guilt for any sins the people of Israel commit in offering their gifts to me, and I will forgive them.
39Make Aaron's robe and turban of fine linen and decorate his sash with fancy needlework.
The Clothes for the Other Priests
(Exodus 39.27-29)
40Since Aaron's sons are priests, they should also look dignified. So make robes, sashes, and special caps for them. 41Then dress Aaron and his sons in these clothes, pour olive oil on their heads, and ordain them as my priests.
42Make linen shorts for them that reach from the waist down to the thigh, so they won't expose themselves. 43Whenever they enter the sacred tent or serve at the altar or enter the holy place, they must wear these shorts, or else they will be guilty and die. This same rule applies to any of their descendants who serve as priests.
translation_text:
Asɔfo Ntade
(Eksodɔs 39.1-7)
1 Afei, ma wo nua Aaron ne ne mmabanin mfi Israelfo mu mmra wo nkyɛn, na wɔabɛyɛ m'asɔfo: Aaron, Nadab ne Abihu, Eleasar ne Itamar, Aaron mma no.
2Na pam kronkronyɛ ntade ma wo nua Aaron, anuonyam ne fɛw so. 3 Na ka kyerɛ wɔn a wɔwɔ nyansa koma a mede nyansa honhom mahyɛ wɔn mu amaama no nyinaa na wɔmpam Aaron ntade no, na wɔmfa nyɛ no kronkron, na onni me sɔfo.
4 Na ntade a wɔmpam ni: Adɛbo ne asɔfotade ne batakari ne atade yuu a wɔanwene no adamadam ne abotiri ne abɔso; na wɔmpam kronkronyɛ ntade mma wo nua Aaron ne ne mmabanin, na wɔnhyɛ nni me sɔfo. 5Na wɔmfa sika ne bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa nyɛ.
6Na wɔmfa ntamanwene mu anyansadwuma so mfa sika ne bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa a wɔafira nyɛ asɔfotade no. 7Ennya mmati abien a ɛtoa ano ano, na wɔmfa ntoa. 8Na asɔfotade fɛfɛ no nkyekyɛmu mfi mu ara, sɛnea ne yɛbea no te, sika ne bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa a wɔafira. 9Na fa apopobibiri abo abien, na kurukyerɛw Israel mma no din wɔ so. 10Wɔn din no asia nkɔ ɔbo biako so, na wɔn din asia a aka no nso nkɔ ɔbo biako so, sɛ wɔn awo ntoatoaso te. 11Abodwumfo adwuma, nsɔanode nkurukyerɛwee na fa kurukyerɛw abo abien no so, sɛnea Israel mma no din te; na fa sika mfofaano twa ho hyia. 12Na fa abo abien no sisi asɔfotade no mmati so, na ɛnyɛ nkae abo mma Israelfo no, na Aaron nsoa wɔn din ne mmati abien so nkɔ Awurade anim mfa nyɛ nkae. 13Na yɛ sika mfofaano 14ne sika ntweaban abien; wɔw no mmɛsa yɛ no sɛ nhama, na fa ntweaban a wɔawɔw no mmɛsa no hyehyɛ mfofaano no so.
15Na yɛ atemmu adɛbo, ntamanwene mu anyansadwuma, yɛ no sɛnea asɔfotade no yɛbea te; sika, bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa a wɔafira na fa yɛ. 16Ɛnyɛ ahinanan, na wommukaw nto so; ne tenten nyɛ nsama, na ne trɛw nyɛ nsama. 17Na fa abo sisi mu, abo kyerɛpɛn anan: kyerɛpɛn a edi kan nyɛ bogyanambo, akratebo ne ahabammonobo; 18na kyerɛpɛn a ɛto so abien no nyɛ nsramabo, hoabo ne bɔwerɛbo; 19na kyerɛpɛn a ɛto so abiɛsa no nyɛ akutuhonobo, mfrafraebo ne beredumbo; 20na kyerɛpɛn a ɛto so anan no nyɛ sikabereɛbo, apopobibiribo ne ahwehwɛbo; ne nsisimu no, sika mfofaano ntwa ho nhyia. 21Na abo no ano nyɛ sɛ Israel mma no din ano te, dumien, sɛ wɔn din no te; ɛnyɛ nsɔanode nkurukyerɛwee, sɛnea din no te mmiako mmiako, sɛ mmusuakuw dumien no te. 22Na fa sika amapa yɛ adɛbo no so ntweaban a wɔawɔw no mmɛsa sɛ nhama. 23Na yɛ adɛbo no so sika nkaa abien, na fa nkaa abien no hyehyɛ adɛbo no twea abien so. 24Na fa sika mmɛsa abien no toatoa adɛbo no twea so nkaa no mu. 25Na mmɛsa abien no ano abien a aka no, fa toatoa mfofaano abien no mu, na fa hyehyɛ asɔfotade no mmati abien no so anim fam. 26Na yɛ sika nkaa abien fa hyehyɛ adɛbo no twea abien no so, ano a ɛwɔ emu fam kyerɛ asɔfotade no. 27Na yɛ sika nkaa abien bio fa hyehyɛ asɔfotade no afaafa abien no so anim fam wɔ ase a ɛbɛn ne ntoae no, asɔfotade no nkyekyeremu no so. 28Na wɔmfa bibiri nhama nkyekyere adɛbo no nkaa no nsuso asɔfotade no nkaa no mu, na ɛmfam asɔfotade no nkyekyeremu no atifi, na adɛbo no antwitwiw amfi asɔfotade no so. 29Na Aaron nsoa Israel mma din atemmu adɛbo no mu ne koma so, mfa nkɔ kronkronbea hɔ, na ɛnyɛ AWURADE anim nkae daa yi.
30 Na fa Urim ne Tumim no hyɛ atemmu adɛbo no mu, na sɛ Aaron rekɔ Awurade anim a, ɛnna ne koko so, na Aaron nsoa Israelfo no atemmu ne koma so, AWURADE anim daa.
31 Na fa birisi nko ara yɛ asɔfotade no ase batakari. 32Na tokuru nna mfinimfini wɔ n'atifi, na wɔmfa ntamabena a wɔanwene mman tokuru no ano nhyia te sɛ nkatabo mu tokuru, na ansuane. 33Na mmuano no so no wɔmfa bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi nyɛ ateaa aba sɛso ntwa ho nhyia, na sika nnɔnnɔmma nsensɛn ntam ntam nhyia. 34Sika adɔmma ne ateaa aba, sika adɔmma ne ateaa aba ntwa batakari no mmuano ho nhyia. 35 Na Aaron nhyɛ nsom, na sɛ ɔhyɛn kronkronbea hɔ AWURADE anim na ofi adi a, wɔate ne nnyigyei na wanwu.
36 Na boro sika amapa tratraa, na kurukyerɛw so sɛ nsɔanode nkurukyerɛwee sɛ: Kronkron ma AWURADE. 37Na fa fam bibiri hama so, na ɛntena abotiri no so; abotiri no anim na ɛmfam. 38Na ɛmfam Aaron moma so, na Aaron nsoa mmusu biara a aba akronkronne a Israelfo yɛ no kronkron, wɔn ayɛyɛde kronkron nyinaa mu no; na ɛntena ne moma so daa, na ama AWURADE ani asɔ wɔn.
39 Na nwene nwera adamadam atade yuu no, na yɛ nwera abotiten, na yɛ adenwene abɔso.
40Na Aaron mma no nso, yɛ ntade ma wɔn, na yɛ abɔmu ma wɔn, na yɛ abotiri bi ma wɔn, na wɔn anim nyɛ nyam na wɔn ho nyɛ fɛ. 41 Na fa hyehyɛ wo nua Aaron ne ne mma a wɔka ne ho no, na sra wɔn ngo, na hyɛ wɔn asɔfo, na dwira wɔn, na wonni me sɔfo. 42Na yɛ nwera ntwakoto ma wɔn, na ɛnkata wɔn adagyaw so mfi asen nkosi nsrɛkyiri. 43Na Aaron ne ne mma no, sɛ wɔreba ahyiae ntamadan no mu anaasɛ wɔrebɛn afɔremuka no abɛsom kronkronbea hɔ a, wɔnhyehyɛ, na wɔanni mmusu na wɔanwu; ɛnyɛ daa atɔremude mma no ne n'asefo a wobedi n'akyi no.

english_text:
Instructions for Ordaining Priests
(Leviticus 8.1-36)
The Lord said to Moses:
1When you ordain Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests, choose a young bull and two rams that have nothing wrong with them. 2Then from your finest flour make three batches of dough without yeast. Shape some of it into larger loaves, some into smaller loaves mixed with olive oil, and the rest into thin wafers brushed with oil. 3Put all of this bread in a basket and bring it when you come to sacrifice the three animals to me.
4Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the sacred tent and tell them to wash themselves. 5Dress Aaron in the priestly shirt, the robe that goes under the sacred vest, the vest itself, the breastpiece, and the sash. 6Put on his turban with its narrow strip of engraved gold 7and then ordain him by pouring olive oil on his head.
8Next, dress Aaron's sons in their special shirts, 9caps, and sashes, then ordain them, because they and their descendants will always be priests.
10Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, where Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head. 11Kill the bull near my altar in front of the tent. 12Use a finger to smear some of its blood on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest of the blood on the ground next to the altar. 13Then take the fat from the animal's insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and send them up as an offering to me in the smoke from the altar. 14But the meat, the skin, and the food still in the bull's stomach must be burned outside the camp as an offering to ask forgiveness for the sins of the priests.
15Bring one of the rams to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head. 16Kill the ram and splatter its blood against all four sides of the altar. 17Cut up the ram, wash its insides and legs, and lay all of its parts on the altar, including the head. 18 Then make sure that the whole animal goes up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
19Bring the other ram to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head. 20Kill the ram and place some of its blood on Aaron's right ear lobe, his right thumb, and the big toe of his right foot. Do the same for each of his sons and splatter the rest of the blood against the four sides of the altar. 21Then take some of the blood from the altar, mix it with the oil used for ordination, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his clothes, and also on his sons and their clothes. This will show that they and their clothes have been dedicated to me.
22This ram is part of the ordination service. So remove its right hind leg, its fat tail, the fat on its insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 23Take one loaf of each kind of bread from the basket, 24and put this bread, together with the meat, into the hands of Aaron and his sons. Then they will lift it all up to show that it is dedicated to me. 25After this, put the meat and bread on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
26You may eat the choice ribs from this second ram, but you must first lift them up to show that this meat is dedicated to me.
27-28In the future, when anyone from Israel offers the ribs and a hind leg of a ram either to ordain a priest or to ask for my blessing, the meat belongs to me, but it may be eaten by the priests. This law will never change.
29-30After Aaron's death, his priestly clothes are to be handed down to each descendant who succeeds him as high priest, and these clothes must be worn during the seven-day ceremony of ordination.
31Boil the meat of the ordination ram in a sacred place, 32then Aaron and his sons are to eat it together with the three kinds of bread at the entrance to the sacred tent. 33At their ordination, a ceremony of forgiveness was performed for them with this sacred food, and only they have the right to eat it. 34If any of the sacred food is left until morning, it must be completely burned.
35Repeat this ordination ceremony for Aaron and his sons seven days in a row, just as I have instructed you. 36Each day you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for sin and as a way of purifying the altar. In addition, you must smear the altar with olive oil to make it completely holy. 37Do this for seven days, and the altar will become so holy that anyone who touches it will become holy.
Daily Sacrifices
(Leviticus 6.8-13; Numbers 28.1-8)
The Lord said:
38Each day you must sacrifice two lambs a year old, 39one in the morning and one in the evening. 40-41With each lamb offer one kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of pure olive oil, and also pour out a liter of wine as an offering. The smell of this sacrifice on the fires of the altar will be pleasing to me. 42-43You and your descendants must always offer this sacrifice on the altar at the entrance to the sacred tent.
People of Israel, I will meet and speak with you there, and my shining glory will make the place holy. 44Because of who I am, the tent will become sacred, and Aaron and his sons will become worthy to serve as my priests. 45I will live among you as your God, 46and you will know that I am the Lord your God, the one who rescued you from Egypt, so that I could live among you.
translation_text:
Aaron ne ne Mma asɔfohyɛ ho nhyehyɛe
(Lewitikɔs 8.1-36)
1 Na eyi na yɛ fa dwira wɔn, na wonni me sɔfo: Fa nantwiforo biako ne adwennini abien a wonni dɛm, 2ne apiti abodoo ne tetare a wɔagu mu ngo, ne apiti fam a wɔasra ho ngo; awisam na fa yɛ. 3Na fa gu kɛntɛn biako mu, na engu kɛntɛn no mu na fa bra, ɛne nantwinini ne adwennini abien no. 4Na fa Aaron ne ne mma no bra ahyiae ntamadan no ano, na fa nsu guare wɔn. 5Na fa ntade no hyɛ Aaron, atade yuu ne asɔfotade ase batakari ne asɔfotade ne adɛbo no, na fa asɔfotade no nkyekyeremu no bɔ ne mu, 6 na fa abotiten no bɔ ne ti, na fa kronkronyɛ ahyehyɛde no fam abotiten no anim, 7 na fa ɔsra ngo hwie gu n'atifi fa sra no. 8Na fa ne mma no nso bra, na hyehyɛ wɔn ntade yuu. 9 Na fa abɔso bobɔ Aaron ne ne mma no mu, na bobɔ wɔn abotiri; na asɔfodwuma nyɛ wɔn de sɛ daa atɔremude: sɛɛ na hyɛ Aaron ne ne mma asɔfo. 10Na ma wɔmfa nantwinini no mmra ahyiae ntamadan no anim, na Aaron ne ne mma no mfa wɔn nsa ngu nantwi no atifi. 11Na kum nantwi no AWURADE anim, ahyiae ntamadan no ano. 12Na fa nantwi no mogya no bi, na fa wo nsatea bɔ mu sra afɔremuka no mmɛn no ho; na hwie mogya no nyinaa gu afɔremuka no ase. 13 Na yi srade a ɛkata ayamde no ho nyinaa ne nea ɛsensɛn mmerɛbo no ho no, ne asaabo abien no ne ɛso srade no, na hyew afɔremuka no so. 14 Nantwi no nam ne ne nhoma ne ne bin de, fa ogya hyew nsra no akyi, ɛyɛ bɔne ho afɔre.
15Na fa odwennini biako, na Aaron ne ne mma no mfa wɔn nsa ngu odwennini no atifi. 16Na kum odwennini no, na fa ne mogya pete afɔremuka no ho hyia. 17Na twitwa odwennini no asinasin, na hohoro n'ayamde ne ne nnyawa ho, na fa gu n'asinasin no ne ne ti so. 18Na hyew odwennini mu no nyinaa afɔremuka no so. Ɛyɛ AWURADE hyew afɔre, ade a eyi hua huamhuam, ɛyɛ AWURADE ogya afɔre. 19Na fa odwennini biako no, na Aaron ne ne mma mfa wɔn nsa ngu odwennini no atifi. 20Na kum odwennini no, na fa ne mogya no bi, na fa ka Aaron aso nifa ne ne mma no aso nifa ano ne wɔn nsa nifa kokurobeti ano ne wɔn nan nifa kokurobeti ano, na fa mogya no pete afɔremuka no ho hyia. 21Na fa afɔremuka no so mogya no bi ne ɔsra ngo no bi, na fa petepete Aaron ne ne ntade so, ne ne mma no ne ne mma ntade nso so, na ennwira no ne ne ntade ne ne mma ne ne mma ntade no nso. 22 Na afei fa odwennini no srade ne ne srade dua no ne srade a ɛkata n'ayamde ho ne nea ɛsensɛn ne mmerɛbo ho ne n'asaabo abien ne ɛho srade ne ne srɛ nifa no, efisɛ ɛyɛ asɔfohyɛ dwennini, 23ne abodoo sebɔw biako ne abodoo tetare a wɔagu mu ngo biako ne ɔfam biako fi apiti kɛntɛn a esi AWURADE anim no mu, 24na fa ne nyinaa gu Aaron ne ne mma no nsam him di akɔneaba yɛ AWURADE anim ohim afɔre. 25Na gye wɔn nsam, na ka ano gya afɔremuka no so ɔhyew afɔre no so, na enyi hua huamhuam, AWURADE anim. Ɛyɛ AWURADE ogya afɔre. 26Na fa Aaron asɔfohyɛ dwennini no yan, na him yɛ ohim afɔre ma AWURADE, na ɛnyɛ wo kyɛfa. 27 Na yɛ Aaron ne ne mma asɔfohyɛ dwennini him yan ne ɛsoma srɛ a wɔahim na wɔama so no kronkron, 28na ɛnyɛ Aaron ne ne mma de, daa atɔremude a efi Israelfo nsam, efisɛ ɛyɛ ɛsoma afɔre. Ɛnyɛ ɛsoma afɔre a Israel mma de fi wɔn asomdwoe afɔrebɔde mu bɔ, wɔn soma afɔre a wɔbɔ ma AWURADE.
29 Na Aaron ntade kronkron no nyɛ ne mma de wɔ n'akyi, na wɔnsra wɔn ngo wɔ mu, na wɔmfa nhyɛ wɔn asɔfo. 30Ne mma mu nea obesi n'ananmu adi sɔfo no nhyɛ no nnansɔn ansa na waba ahyiae ntamadan no mu abɛsom kronkronbea hɔ. 31Na fa asɔfohyɛ dwennini no, na noa ne nam no nea ɛhɔ yɛ kronkron. 32Na Aaron ne ne mma no nni odwennini no nam ne kɛntɛn no mu abodoo no, ahyiae ntamadan no ano. 33Na wonni nneɛma a wɔde pata maa wɔn de hyɛɛ wɔn asɔfo na wɔde dwiraa wɔn no, nanso ɔhɔho nnni bi, efisɛ ɛyɛ kronkron. 34Na sɛ asɔfohyɛ nam no ne abodoo no bi ka ma ade kye so a, ɛnne fa ogya hyew nea ɛkae no; wonnni, efisɛ ɛyɛ kronkron. 35Na sɛɛ na yɛ Aaron ne ne mma no, sɛnea mahyɛ wo yi nyinaa; nnansɔn na fa hyɛ wɔn asɔfo. 36Na fa nantwinini bɔ bɔne ho afɔre daa, na ɛnyɛ mpata. Na sɛ wɔrepata afɔremuka no so a, prapra ɛho bɔne, na sra no ngo fa yɛ no kronkron. 37Nnansɔn na pata afɔremuka no so yɛ no kronkron, na afɔremuka no ayɛ akronkronne mu kronkron. Obiara a ɔka afɔremuka no nyɛ kronkron.
Daa hyew afɔre
38 Na eyi ne afɔre a bɔ afɔremuka no so: nguanten mma abien a wɔadi afe afe na fa bɔ so afɔre da biara da. 39 Fa oguan ba no biako bɔ afɔre anɔpa, na fa oguan ba biako no bɔ afɔre anwummere; 40na fa asikresam efa abupɛn du mu biako a wɔde ngo dua aba a wɔasiw ngo susutoa abupɛn anan mu biako agu so, ne bobesa susutoa abupɛn anan mu biako ahwiesa ka oguammaa biako ho. 41Na oguammaa biako no, fa no bɔ afɔre anwummere, na yɛ no sɛ anɔpa aduan afɔre no ne ɛho ahwiesa no, na enyi hua huamhuam, ɛyɛ AWURADE ogya afɔre. 42Ɛnyɛ daa hyew afɔre mo awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu a mommɔ no ahyiae ntamadan no ano, AWURADE anim, nea me ne mo behyia na me ne wo akasa hɔ. 43 Na ɛhɔ na me ne Israelfo behyia, na wɔafa m'anuonyam so ayɛ kronkron. 44Na mɛma ahyiae ntamadan ne afɔremuka no ayɛ kronkron, na mɛma Aaron ne ne mma ayɛ kronkron, na wɔadi me asɔfo.
45Na mɛtena Israelfo mu, na mayɛ wɔn Onyankopɔn, 46na wɔahu sɛ mene AWURADE wɔn Nyankopɔn a miyii wɔn fii Misraim asase so sɛ mɛtena wɔn mu no, mene AWURADE, wɔn Nyankopɔn.

english_text:
The Altar for Burning Incense
(Exodus 37.25-28)
The Lord said to Moses:
1Build an altar of acacia wood where you can burn incense. 2Make it 45 centimeters square and 90 centimeters high, and make each of its four corners stick up like the horn of a bull. 3Cover it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it. 4Then below the edging on opposite sides attach two gold rings through which you can put the poles for carrying the altar. 5These poles are also to be made of acacia wood covered with gold.
6Put the altar in front of the inside curtain of the sacred tent. The chest with the place of mercy is kept behind that curtain, and I will talk with you there. 7-8From now on, when Aaron takes care of the lamps each morning and evening, he must burn sweet-smelling incense to me on the altar. 9Burn only the proper incense on the altar and never use it for grain sacrifices or animal sacrifices or drink offerings. 10 Once a year Aaron must purify the altar by smearing on its four corners the blood of an animal sacrificed for sin, and this practice must always be followed. The altar is sacred because it is dedicated to me.
The Money for the Sacred Tent
11The Lord said to Moses:
12Find out how many grown men there are in Israel and require each of them to pay me to keep him safe from danger while you are counting them. 13-15 Each man over 19, whether rich or poor, must pay me the same amount of money, weighed according to the official standards. 16This money is to be used for the upkeep of the sacred tent, and because of it, I will never forget my people.
The Large Bronze Bowl
(Exodus 38.8)
17The Lord said to Moses:
18-21 Make a large bronze bowl and a bronze stand for it. Then put them between the altar for sacrifice and the sacred tent, so the priests can wash their hands and feet before entering the tent or offering a sacrifice on the altar. Each priest in every generation must wash himself in this way, or else he will die right there.
The Oil for Dedication and Ordination
(Exodus 37.29)
22 The Lord said to Moses:
23-25Mix four liters of olive oil with the following costly spices: six kilograms of myrrh, three kilograms of cinnamon, three kilograms of cane, and six kilograms of cassia. Measure these according to the official standards. Then use this sacred mixture 26for dedicating the tent and chest, 27the table with its equipment, the lampstand with its equipment, the incense altar with all its utensils, 28the altar for sacrifices, and the large bowl with its stand. 29By dedicating them in this way, you will make them so holy that anyone who even touches them will become holy.
30When you ordain Aaron and his sons as my priests, sprinkle them with some of this oil, 31and say to the people of Israel: “This oil must always be used in the ordination service of a priest. It is holy because it is dedicated to the Lord. 32So treat it as holy! Don't ever use it for everyday purposes or mix any for yourselves. 33If you do, you will no longer belong to the Lord's people.”
The Sweet-Smelling Incense
34-35Mix equal amounts of the costly spices stacte, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense, then add salt to make the mixture pure and holy. 36Pound some of it into powder and sprinkle it in front of the sacred chest, where I meet with you. Be sure to treat this incense as something very holy. 37It is truly holy because it is dedicated to me, so don't ever make any for yourselves. 38If you ever make any of it to use as perfume, you will no longer belong to my people.
translation_text:
Aduhuamhyew muka
(Eksodɔs 37.25-28)
1 Na yɛ aduhuamhyew muka, ɔkanto na fa yɛ. 2Ne tenten nyɛ anammɔn biako ne fa, na ne tɛtrɛtɛ nso nyɛ anammɔn biako ne fa, na ɛnyɛ ahinanan, na ne sorokɔ nyɛ basafa baako, na ne mmɛn nso ntuatua mu ara. 3Na fa sika amapa dura ɛso ne ɛho ne ne mmɛn no ho hyia; na yɛ sika hankare twa ho hyia. 4Na yɛ ɛho sika nkaa abien wɔ ne hankare no ase, wɔ n'afanu, na wɔmfa mpoma nwurawura mu, na wɔde asoa. 5Na fa ɔkanto sinsen mpoma no, na duradura ho sika. 6 Na fa si mmɔhɔɔ a ɛwɔ Adanse adaka no ho no anim wɔ mpata agua a esi Adanse no so no anim, nea me ne wo behyia hɔ no. 7 Na Aaron nhyew so aduhuam daa anɔpa; osiesie akanea no a, ɔnhyew aduhuam no. 8Na sɛ Aaron de akanea no sisi so anwummere a, ɔnhyew aduhuam no: ɛyɛ daa aduhuam a wɔnhyew no AWURADE anim, mo awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu. 9 Monnhyew so aduhuam foforo bi, ɔhyew afɔre anaa aduan afɔre, na munnhwie ahwiesa nso nngu so. 10 Na daa afirihyia mu pɛnkoro Aaron mfa bɔne ho mpata afɔre mogya no bi mpata wɔ ne mmɛn no so; daa afe ɔmpata wɔ so pɛnkoro, mo awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu: ɛyɛ akronkronne mu ade kronkron ma AWURADE.
Akra mpata
11Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 12Sɛ wubu Israelfo ano hwehwɛ wɔn dodow a, wɔn kan yi mu no wɔn nyinaa mfa wɔn kra mpata ade mma AWURADE, na, sɛ wɔkan wɔn a, owuyare bi amma wɔn mu. 13Nea wɔmma ni: obiara a wɔkan no fra dodow a wɔkan wɔn no mu no mma dwetɛbona fa, sɛ kronkronbea dwetɛbona no te (dwetɛbona biako yɛ gera aduonu), dwetɛbona fa sɛ AWURADE soma afɔrebɔde. 14Obiara a wadi mfe aduonu ne akyiri a wɔkan no fra dodow a wɔkan wɔn no mu no mfa soma afɔrebɔde yi mma Awurade. 15Sɛ wɔde soma afɔrebɔde no rema AWURADE de apata ama mo kra a, ɔdefo nnto so, na ohiani nso nntew dwetɛbona fa no so. 16Na gyigye mpata sika no Israelfo no nsam, na fa ma ahyiae ntamadan no mu som no, na ɛnyɛ Israelfo no nkae, AWURADE anim, na wɔmfa mpata mma mo kra.
Asankasɔn
17Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 18 Fa ayowa yɛ asankasɔn nso a n'ase nso yɛ ayowa, na wɔaguare mu, na fa si ahyiae ntamadan no ne afɔremuka no ntam, na gu mu nsu. 19Na Aaron ne ne mma mfa nhohoro wɔn nsa ne wɔn nan ho. 20Sɛ wɔrekɔhyɛn ahyiae ntamadan no mu a, wɔmfa nsu nhohoro wɔn ho, na wɔanwuwu; anaasɛ wɔrebɛbɛn afɔremuka no abɛsom abɛbɔ ogya afɔre ama AWRADE a, 21wɔnhohoro wɔn nsa ne wɔn nan ho, na wɔanwuwu; na ɛnyɛ daa atɔremude mma wɔn, ɔno ne n'asefo, wɔn awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu.
Ɔsra ngo
22Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 23Wo nso fa nnuhuam mu atitiriw, kurobow a anene nnwetɛbona ahannum, ne dupapo huamhuam saa fa, ahanu aduonum, ne mmetire huamhuam ahanu aduonum, 24ne bɛwewonua huamhuam ahannum, kronkronbea dwetɛbona so, ne ngodua ngo susutoa biako, 25 na fa yɛ ɔsra ngo kronkron, adufrae a wɔafra no adufrafo nyansa mu, na ɛnyɛ ɔsra ngo kronkron. 26Na fa sra ahyiae ntamadan no ne Adanse adaka no, 27ne ɔpon no ne ɛho nneɛma no nyinaa ne kaneadua no ne ɛho nneɛma no ne aduhuamhyew muka no, 28ne ɔhyew afɔremuka no ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa ne asankasɔn no ne ne ntaase no ho; 29 na dwira ho ma ɛnyɛ akronkronne mu ade kronkron; obiara a ɔka no nyɛ kronkron. 30 Na sra Aaron ne ne mma no ngo yɛ wɔn kronkron, na wonni me asɔfo. 31Na ka kyerɛ Israelfo no sɛ: Eyi nyɛ ɔsra ngo kronkron mma me, mo awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu, 32wonnhwie nngu onipa honam so, na munnsusuw so nnyɛ bi a ɛte sɛ ɛno; ɛyɛ kronkron, ɛnyɛ kronkron mma mo. 33Obiara a ɔbɛfra bi a ɛte sɛ ɛno anaasɛ ɔde bi bɛka ɔhɔho no, wobetwa no afi ne man mu akyene.
34Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Fa nnuhuam, aneneduru ne nworahuam ne prɛkɛsɛ huamhuam ne ohuamfufu gyenennyenen, wonsusuw ne nyinaa pɛ, 35 na fa yɛ aduhuam a wɔhyew, adufrafo nyansa so adufrae a wɔaposa a ɛyɛ gyenennyenen ne kronkron. 36 Na siw bi fekɔfekɔ, na fa bi si Adanse no anim ahyiae ntamadan no mu, nea me ne wo behyia no: Ɛnyɛ mo akronkronne mu ade kronkron. 37Na aduhuam a worebɛyɛ yi, munnsusuw so nnyɛ bi mmfa: Ɛnyɛ wo kronkron mma AWURADE. 38Obiara a ɔbɛyɛ bi a ɛte sɛ ɛno ahuam ahwɛ no, wobetwa no afi ne man mu akyene.

english_text:
The Lord Chooses Bezalel and Oholiab
(Exodus 35.30—36.1)
1The Lord said to Moses:
2I have chosen Bezalel from the Judah tribe to make the sacred tent and its furnishings. 3-5Not only have I filled him with my Spirit, but I have given him wisdom and made him a skilled craftsman who can create objects of art with gold, silver, bronze, precious stones, and wood. 6I have appointed Oholiab from the tribe of Dan to work with him, and I have also given skills to those who will help them make everything exactly as I have commanded you: 7-11the sacred tent with its furnishings, the sacred chest with its place of mercy, the table with all that is on it, the lamp with its equipment, the incense altar, the altar for sacrifices with its equipment, the bronze bowl with its stand, the beautiful priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons, the oil for dedication and ordination services, and the sweet-smelling incense for the holy place.
Laws for the Sabbath
12-13Moses told the Israelites that the Lord had said:
The Sabbath belongs to me. Now I command you and your descendants to always obey the laws of the Sabbath. By doing this, you will know that I have chosen you as my own. 14-15 Keep the Sabbath holy. You have six days to do your work, but the Sabbath is mine, and it must remain a day of rest. If you work on the Sabbath, you will no longer be part of my people, and you will be put to death.
16Every generation of Israelites must respect the Sabbath. 17 This day will always serve as a reminder, both to me and to the Israelites, that I made the heavens and the earth in six days, then on the seventh day I rested and relaxed.
18When God had finished speaking to Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two flat stones on which he had written all his laws with his own hand.
translation_text:
Wɔpaw Besalel ne Oholiab si ntamadan
(Eksodɔs 35.30—36.1)
1 Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 2Hwɛ, mabɔ Hur ba Uri ba Besalel a ofi Yuda abusuakuw mu din mafrɛ no, 3 na mede Onyankopɔn honhom mahyɛ no ma, nyansa ne nhumu ne nimdeɛ ne adwinni ahorow nyinaa mu, 4sɛ ɔmfa nnwen ho ne tirim na onni sika ne dwetɛ ne kɔbere, 5ne abo a wosen sisi ade mu ne nnuasen mu adwinni, na onni adwinhorow nyinaa. 6Na me ara, hwɛ, mafa Ahisamak ba Oholiab a ofi Dan abusuakuw mu maka ne ho; na nnipa a wɔwɔ nyansa koma nyinaa, mede nyansa mahyɛ wɔn komam na wɔnyɛ nea mahyɛ wo yi nyinaa; 7 ahyiae ntamadan no ne Adanse adaka no ne mpata agua no a esi so no ne ntamadan no ho ade nyinaa, 8ne ɔpon no ne ɛho nneɛma ne kaneadua a ɛho tew no ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa ne aduhuamhyew muka no, 9ne ɔhyew afɔremuka no ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa ne asankasɔn ne ne ntaase no, 10ne ɔsom ntade ne ɔsɔfo Aaron ntade kronkron no ne ne mma ntade a wɔde bedi asɔfo no, 11ne ɔsra ngo no ne kronkronbea aduhuam a wɔhyew no. Wɔnyɛ no sɛnea mahyɛ wo nyinaa.
Homedadi
12 Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 13 Na wo nso ka kyerɛ Israelfo no sɛ: Me home nna no ara na munni; na ɛyɛ me ne mo ntam sɛnkyerɛnne, mo awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu, na moahu sɛ me AWURADE na meyɛ mo kronkron. 14 Enti munni homeda no, na ɛyɛ kronkron ma mo; obiara a obegu ho fi no, okum na wobekum no; na obiara a ɔyɛ mu adwuma no, wobetwa saa ɔkra no afi ne man mu akyene. 15Nnansia na wɔmfa nyɛ adwuma, na da a ɛto so ason no yɛ ɔhome mu homeda a ɛyɛ kronkron ma AWURADE; obiara a ɔyɛ adwuma homeda no, okum na wobekum no. 16Enti Israelfo no nhwɛ homeda no na wonni homeda no, wɔn awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu, sɛ daa apam. 17 Me ne Israel ntam sɛnkyerɛnne ne no de kosi daa; na nnansia na AWURADE de yɛɛ ɔsoro ne asase, na da a ɛto so ason no ɔhomee na odwudwoo ne koma. 18 Na ɔne Mose wiee kasa Sinai bepɔw so no, ɔmaa no adanse apon abien, abopon a wɔde Nyankopɔn nsatea akyerɛw so.

english_text:
The People Make an Idol To Worship
(Deuteronomy 9.6-29)
1 After the people saw that Moses had been on the mountain for a long time, they went to Aaron and said, “Make us an image of a god who will lead and protect us. Moses brought us out of Egypt, but nobody knows what has happened to him.”
2Aaron told them, “Bring me the gold earrings that your wives and sons and daughters are wearing.” 3Everybody took off their earrings and brought them to Aaron, 4 then he melted them and made an idol in the shape of a young bull.
All the people said to one another, “This is the god who brought us out of Egypt!”
5When Aaron saw what was happening, he built an altar in front of the idol and said, “Tomorrow we will celebrate in honor of the Lord.” 6 The people got up early the next morning and killed some animals to be used for sacrifices and others to be eaten. Then everyone ate and drank so much that they began to carry on like wild people.
7The Lord said to Moses:
Hurry back down! Those people you led out of Egypt are acting like fools. 8They have already stopped obeying me and have made themselves an idol in the shape of a young bull. They have bowed down to it, offered sacrifices, and said that it is the god who brought them out of Egypt. 9Moses, I have seen how stubborn these people are, 10and I'm angry enough to destroy them, so don't try to stop me. But I will make your descendants into a great nation.
11 Moses tried to get the Lord God to change his mind:
Our Lord, you used your mighty power to bring these people out of Egypt. Now don't become angry and destroy them. 12If you do, the Egyptians will say that you brought your people out here into the mountains just to get rid of them. Please don't be angry with your people. Don't destroy them!
13 Remember the solemn promise you made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. You promised that someday they would have as many descendants as there are stars in the sky and that you would give them land.
14So even though the Lord had threatened to destroy the people, he changed his mind and let them live.
15-16Moses went back down the mountain with the two flat stones on which God had written all of his laws with his own hand, using both sides of the stones.
17When Joshua heard the noisy shouts of the people, he said to Moses, “A battle must be going on down in the camp.”
18But Moses replied, “It doesn't sound like they are shouting because they have won or lost a battle. It sounds more like a wild party!”
19As Moses got closer to the camp, he saw the idol, and he also saw the people dancing around. This made him so angry that he threw down the stones and broke them to pieces at the foot of the mountain. 20He melted the idol the people had made, and he ground it into powder. He scattered it in their water and made them drink it. 21Moses asked Aaron, “What did these people do to harm you? Why did you make them sin in this terrible way?”
22Aaron answered:
Don't be angry with me. You know as well as I do that they are determined to do evil. 23They even told me, “That man Moses led us out of Egypt, but now we don't know what has happened to him. Make us a god to lead us.” 24Then I asked them to bring me their gold earrings. They took them off and gave them to me. I threw the gold into a fire, and out came this bull.
25Moses knew that the people were out of control and that it was Aaron's fault. And now they had made fools of themselves in front of their enemies. 26So Moses stood at the gate of the camp and shouted, “Everyone who is on the Lord's side come over here!”
Then the men of the Levi tribe gathered around Moses, 27and he said to them, “The Lord God of Israel commands you to strap on your swords and go through the camp, killing your relatives, your friends, and your neighbors.”
28The men of the Levi tribe followed his orders, and that day they killed about 3,000 men. 29Moses said to them, “You obeyed the Lord and did what was right, and so you will serve as his priests for the people of Israel. It was hard for you to kill your own sons and brothers, but the Lord has blessed you and made you his priests today.”
30The next day Moses told the people, “This is a terrible thing you have done. But I will go back to the Lord to see if I can do something to keep this sin from being held against you.”
31Moses returned to the Lord and said, “The people have committed a terrible sin. They have made a gold idol to be their god. 32 But I beg you to forgive them. If you don't, please wipe my name out of your book.”
33The Lord replied, “I will wipe out of my book the name of everyone who has sinned against me. 34Now take my people to the place I told you about, and my angel will lead you. But when the time comes, I will punish them for this sin.”
35So the Lord punished the people of Israel with a terrible disease for talking Aaron into making the gold idol.
translation_text:
Wɔma Aaron yɛ sika nantwi ba
(Deuteronomium 9.6-29)
1 Na ɔman no hui sɛ Mose akyɛ na onsian mfi bepɔw no so mma no, ɔman no boaa wɔn ho ano baa Aaron nkyɛn besee no sɛ: Sɔre yɛ anyame ma yɛn, na wonni yɛn anim, efisɛ Mose yi, ɔbarima a okoyii yɛn fii Misraim bae no de, yennim nea ayɛ no. 2Ɛnna Aaron ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Munyiyi sika nkaa a ɛwowɔ mo yerenom ne mo mmabanin ne mo mmabea asom mfa mmrɛ me. 3Na ɔman no nyinaa yiyii sika nkaa a ɛwowɔ wɔn asom no de brɛɛ Aaron. 4 Na ogyei wɔ wɔn nsam, na ɔde pɛe yeyɛe, na ɔyɛɛ no nantwi a wɔagu; na wɔkae sɛ: Israel, eyinom ne wo anyame a woyii wo fii Misraim asase so bae no. 5Na Aaron hui no, osii afɔremuka wɔ n'anim; na Aaron paee sɛ: Ɔkyena ne AWURADE afahyɛ. 6 Na wotuaa ahema bobɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre ne asomdwoe afɔre; na ɔman no tenaa ase didi nomee, na wɔsɔre gorui.
7Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Sian kɔ, na wo man a wode wɔn fi Misraim asase so bae no redi asɛmmɔne; 8 wɔaman afi ɔkwan a mekyerɛɛ wɔn no so ntɛm; wɔayɛ nantwi ba a wɔagu, na wɔasɔre no abɔ afɔre ama no aka sɛ: Israel, eyinom ne wo anyame a woyii wo fii Misraim asase so bae no. 9Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 10 Mahu ɔman yi, na hwɛ, wɔyɛ ɔman a wɔn kɔn asen; na afei ma me kwan na me bo nhuru nhyɛ wɔn, na memmene wɔn, na memfa wo menyɛ ɔman kɛse.
11Na Mose paa AWURADE ne Nyankopɔn kyɛw sɛ: AWURADE, ɛdɛn nti na wo bo huru hyɛ ɔman a wode ahoɔden kɛse ne nsa a ɛyɛ den koyii wɔn Misraim asase so bae no? 12Ɛdɛn nti na Misraimfo nka sɛ: Adwemmɔne bi nti na obeyii wɔn kɔe sɛ okokum wɔn mmepɔw so na wapra wɔn afi asase ani? San fi w'abufuhyew no mu, na ma bɔne a worebɛyɛ wo man no nyɛ wo yaw. 13 Kae Abraham, Isak ne Israel, wo nkoa a wokaa wɔn wo ankasa wo ntam ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Mɛma w'asefo adɔɔso sɛ ɔsoro nsoromma, na asase a maka ho asɛm yi nyinaa, mede mɛma w'asefo na wɔadi so akosi daa, no. 14Na AWURADE nuu ne ho wɔ bɔne a ɔkae sɛ ɔrebɛyɛ ne man no ho.
15Na Mose dan ne ho sian fii bepɔw no so, na adanse apon abien no kura ne nsam, abopon a wɔakyerɛw n'afanu, wɔakyerɛw so ɛha ne ha. 16 Na apon no yɛ Onyankopɔn adwuma, na kyerɛw no yɛ Onyankopɔn kyerɛw a wɔakurukyerɛw apon no so. 17Na Yosua tee sɛ ɔman no rebɔ ose na wɔreyɛ gyegyeegye no, ɔka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Ɔko gyegyeegye wɔ nsra no mu. 18Na ose: Ɛnyɛ nkonimdi ho sebɔ gyegyeegye na ɛnyɛ nkogu ho nteɛm gyegyeegye, na mmom dwomsogye gyegyeegye na mete yi.
19Na Mose bɛn nsra no na ohuu nantwi ba ne asaw no ara pɛ, ne bo fuwii, na ɔtow apon a ɛwɔ ne nsam no gui ma ɛbobɔe bepɔw no ase.
20Na ɔfaa nantwi ba a wɔyɛe no de gya hyewee, na ɔyam no muhumuhu de petee nsu ani maa Israelfo no nomee. 21Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Aaron sɛ: Dɛn na ɔman yi yɛɛ wo na wode bɔne kɛse aba wɔn so yi?
22Ɛnna Aaron se: Mma me wura bo mmfuw, wo ara wunim ɔman yi sɛ bɔne ara na wɔde asi wɔn anim. 23Na wɔka kyerɛɛ me sɛ: Yɛ anyame ma yɛn na wonni yɛn anim, efisɛ Mose yi, ɔbarima a okoyii yɛn fii Misraim asase so bae no, yennim nea ayɛ no. 24Na misee wɔn sɛ: Wɔn a wɔwɔ sika bi no, wonyi. Na wɔde maa me, na metow guu gya mu, na nantwi ba yi fii mu bae.
25Na Mose hui sɛ ɔman no agye nsam (Aaron na ama ɔman no nneyɛe agye nsam ama wɔabɔ adapaa, wɔn atamfo anim no), 26ogyinaa nsraban no tia kae sɛ: Nea ɔwɔ AWURADE afa mmra me nkyɛn. Na Lewifo nyinaa boaboaa wɔn ho ano baa ne nkyɛn. 27Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn se: Momfa mo nkrante mmobɔ mo asen, na muntwa mu nkɔ, na monsan mmra, mfi nsra no tia nkɔ tia, na munkunkum mo nuanom ne mo nnamfonom ne mo afipamfo. 28Na Lewifo no yɛe sɛnea Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn no, na ɛda no ɔman no mu nnipa bɛyɛ mpensa totɔe. 29 Na Mose kae sɛ: Monyɛ mo ho kronkron mma AWURADE nnɛ, sɛ obiara bɛsɔre ahyɛ ne ba ne ne nua po, na mode nhyira aba mo so nnɛ.
30Na ade kyee no, Mose ka kyerɛɛ ɔman no sɛ: Mo de, moayɛ bɔne kɛse, na afei mɛforo makɔ AWURADE nkyɛn, ebia metumi mapata ama mo bɔne no. 31Na Mose san kɔɔ AWURADE nkyɛn kɔkae sɛ: Ao, bɔne kɛse na ɔman yi ayɛ, na wɔayɛ sika anyame afa. 32 Na afei, sɛ wode wɔn bɔne no bekyɛ a! Na sɛ ɛnte saa a, popa me nso fi wo nhoma a woakyerɛw no mu ɛ! 33Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Nea wayɛ me bɔne no, ɔno na mɛpopa no mafi me nhoma mu. 34 Na afei kɔ, na kogya ɔman no kɔ nea maka makyerɛ wo no; hwɛ, me bɔfo bedi w'anim; nanso da a mɛba mabɛhwɛ wɔn no, metua wɔn wɔn bɔne so ka. 35Na sɛ wɔayɛ nantwi ba a Aaron yɛe no nti, AWURADE haw ɔman no.

english_text:
The Lord Tells Israel To Leave Mount Sinai
1 The Lord said to Moses:
You led the people of Israel out of Egypt. Now get ready to lead them to the land I promised their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. 2-3It is a land rich with milk and honey, and I will send an angel to force out those people who live there—the Canaanites, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. But I will not go with my people. They are so rebellious that I would destroy them before they get there.
4-5Even before the Lord said these harsh things, he had told Moses, “These people really are rebellious, and I would kill them at once, if I went with them. But tell them to take off their fancy jewelry, then I'll decide what to do with them.” So the people started mourning, 6and after leaving Mount Sinai, they stopped wearing fancy jewelry.
The Lord Is with His People
7Moses used to set up a tent far from camp. He called it the “meeting tent,” and whoever needed some message from the Lord would go there. 8Each time Moses went out to this tent, everyone would stand at the entrance to their own tents and watch him enter. 9-11Then they would bow down because a thick cloud would come down in front of the tent, and the Lord would speak to Moses face to face, just like a friend. Afterwards, Moses would return to camp, but his young assistant Joshua would stay at the tent.
The Lord Promises To Be with His People
12Moses said to the Lord, “I know that you have told me to lead these people to the land you promised them. But you have not said who will go along to help me. You have said that you are my friend and that you are pleased with me. 13If this is true, let me know what your plans are, then I can obey and continue to please you. And don't forget that you have chosen this nation to be your own.”
14The Lord said, “I will go with you and give you peace.”
15Then Moses replied, “If you aren't going with us, please don't make us leave this place. 16But if you do go with us, everyone will know that you are pleased with your people and with me. That way, we will be different from the rest of the people on earth.”
17So the Lord told him, “I will do what you have asked, because I am your friend and I am pleased with you.”
18Then Moses said, “I pray that you will let me see you in all of your glory.”
19 The Lord answered:
All right. I am the Lord, and I show mercy and kindness to anyone I choose. I will let you see my glory and hear my holy name, 20but I won't let you see my face, because anyone who sees my face will die. 21There is a rock not far from me. Stand beside it, 22and before I pass by in all of my shining glory, I will put you in a large crack in the rock. I will cover your eyes with my hand until I have passed by. 23Then I will take my hand away, and you will see my back. You will not see my face.
translation_text:
AWURADE hyɛ Israel sɛ wɔmfi Bepɔw Sinai ase nkɔ
1 Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Sim fi ha kɔ, wo ne ɔman a wukoyii wɔn fii Misraim bae no, kɔ asase a mekaa ɛho ntam mekyerɛɛ Abraham, Isak ne Yakob sɛ: w'asefo na mede mɛma wɔn, no so. 2 Na mɛsoma ɔbɔfo adi wɔn anim, na matu Kanaanni ne Amorini ne Hetini ne Perisini ne Hewini ne Yebusini no, 3 kɔ asase a nufusu ne ɛwo sen so no so; na merentena wo mu ne wo nkɔ, efisɛ woyɛ ɔman a wo kɔn asen, na mammene wo ɔkwan no mu.
4Na ɔman no tee asɛmmɔne yi no, wodii nkɔmmɔ, na obiara anhyɛ n'ahokekade. 5Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Kɔka kyerɛ Israelfo no sɛ: Moyɛ ɔman a mo kɔn asen; sɛ metena mo mu kakraa bi me ne mo kɔ a, anka mɛhyew mo; na afei munyi mo ho ahokekade, na minhu nea mɛyɛ mo. 6 Ɛnna Israelfo no yiyii wɔn ho ahokekade fi bepɔw Horeb ho hɔ ara.
7 Na Mose faa ntamadan no de kosii nsra no akyi akyirikyiri, na ɔfrɛɛ no ahyiae ntamadan. Na obiara a ɔhwehwɛ AWURADE no fi adi kɔ ahyiae ntamadan no a ɛwɔ nsra no akyi no ho. 8Na sɛ Mose fi adi kɔ ntamadan no ho a, ɔman no nyinaa sɔresɔre kogyinagyina wɔn ntamadan ano, na wɔde Mose akyi hwɛ ara kosi sɛ ɔhyɛn ntamadan no mu.
9 Na sɛ Mose hyɛn ntamadan no mu a, omununkum dum no sian begyina ntamadan no ano, na AWURADE ne Mose kasa. 10Na ɔman no nyinaa hu omununkum dum no sɛ egyina ntamadan no ano a, ɔman no nyinaa sɔresɔre, na obiara kotow sɔre wɔ ne ntamadan ano. 11 Na AWURADE ne Mose di nhwɛanim kasa sɛ onipa ne ne yɔnko kasa. Na ɔsan ba nsra no mu a, ne somfo Nun ba Yosua a ɔyɛ abofra no de, omfi ntamadan no mu.
12 Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Awurade sɛ: Hwɛ wo ara na woka kyerɛ me sɛ: Fa ɔman yi kɔ, nanso womma minhu nea wobɛsoma no na ɔne me akɔ. Nanso wo ara na woaka sɛ: Mede wo din minim wo, na woanya m'anim dom nso. 13 Enti mesrɛ wo, sɛ manya w'anim dom a, ma minhu wo kwan ɛ, na mahu wo, na manya w'anim dom; na hu sɛ nkurɔfo yi yɛ wo man a! 14Na AWURADE kae sɛ: M'anim ne wo bɛkɔ, na mama woakɔhome. 15Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ w'anim ne yɛn renkɔ a, ɛnne mfa yɛn mfi ha nkɔ. 16 Na ɛdɛn na wɔde behu wɔ ha sɛ me ne wo man yi anya w'anim dom, ɛnyɛ wo kɔ a wo ne yɛn bɛkɔ no? Na me ne wo man yi adɛnsow wɔ aman a wɔwɔ asase ani nyinaa mu. 17 Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Asɛm a woaka yi nso, mɛyɛ, efisɛ woanya m'anim adom, na mede wo din minim wo. 18Na Mose kae sɛ: Ɛnne, ma minhu w'anuonyam. 19 Na ose: Mɛma me papa nyinaa asen w'anim, na mɛpae me din YHWH (AWURADE) wɔ w'anim; na medom nea medom no, na mihu nea mihu no mmɔbɔ no mmɔbɔ. 20 Na ose: Wuntumi nhu m'anim, efisɛ onipa renhu m'anim nnya nkwa. 21 Na AWURADE se: Hwɛ, ɔkwan wɔ me nkyɛn ha, na gyina ɔbotan no so; 22 na sɛ m'anuonyam resen a, mede wo mɛhyɛ ɔbo tokuru mu, na mede me nsa makata wo so masen ansa, 23na mayi me nsa, na woahu m'akyi fam; na m'anim de, worenhu.

english_text:
The Second Set of Commandments
(Deuteronomy 10.1-5)
1One day the Lord said to Moses, “Cut two flat stones like the first ones I made, and I will write on them the same commandments that were on the two you broke. 2Be ready tomorrow morning to come up Mount Sinai and meet me at the top. 3No one is to come with you or to be on the mountain at all. Don't even let the sheep and cattle graze at the foot of the mountain.” 4So Moses cut two flat stones like the first ones, and early the next morning he carried them to the top of Mount Sinai, just as the Lord had commanded.
5The Lord God came down in a cloud and stood beside Moses there on the mountain. God spoke his holy name, “the Lord.” 6 Then he passed in front of Moses and called out, “I am the Lord God. I am merciful and very patient with my people. I show great love, and I can be trusted. 7I keep my promises to my people forever, but I also punish anyone who sins. When people sin, I punish them and their children, and also their grandchildren and great-grandchildren.”
8Moses quickly bowed down to the ground and worshiped the Lord. 9He prayed, “Lord, if you really are pleased with me, I pray that you will go with us. It is true that these people are sinful and rebellious, but forgive our sin and let us be your people.”
A Promise and Its Demands
(Exodus 23.14-19; Deuteronomy 7.1-5; 16.1-17)
10The Lord said:
I promise to perform miracles for you that have never been seen anywhere on earth. Neighboring nations will stand in fear and know that I was the one who did these marvelous things. 11I will force out the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, but you must do what I command you today. 12Don't make treaties with any of those people. If you do, it will be like falling into a trap. 13 Instead, you must destroy their altars and tear down the sacred poles they use in the worship of the goddess Asherah. 14I demand your complete loyalty—you must not worship any other god! 15Don't make treaties with the people there, or you will soon find yourselves worshiping their gods and taking part in their sacrificial meals. 16Your men will even marry their women and be influenced to worship their gods.
17 Don't make metal images of gods.
18 Don't fail to observe the Festival of Thin Bread in the month of Abib. Obey me and eat bread without yeast for seven days during Abib, because that is the month you left Egypt.
19 The first-born males of your families and of your flocks and herds belong to me.
20 You can save the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must save every first-born son.
Bring an offering every time you come to worship.
21 Work for six days and rest on the seventh day, even during the seasons for plowing and harvesting. 22 Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
23Your men must come to worship me three times a year, because I am the Lord God of Israel. 24As you advance, I will force the nations out of your land and enlarge your borders. Then no one will try to take your property when you come to worship me these three times each year.
25 When you sacrifice an animal on the altar, don't offer bread made with yeast. And don't save any part of the Passover meal for the next day.
26 I am the Lord your God, and you must bring the first part of your harvest to the place of worship.
Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
27The Lord told Moses to put these laws in writing, as part of his agreement with Israel. 28Moses stayed on the mountain with the Lord for 40 days and nights, without eating or drinking. And he wrote down the Ten Commandments, the most important part of God's agreement with his people.
Moses Comes Down from Mount Sinai
29 Moses came down from Mount Sinai, carrying the Ten Commandments. His face was shining brightly because the Lord had been speaking to him. But Moses did not know at first that his face was shining. 30When Aaron and the others looked at Moses, they saw this, and they were afraid to go near him. 31Moses called out for Aaron and the leaders to come to him, and he spoke with them. 32Then the rest of the people of Israel gathered around Moses, and he gave them the laws that the Lord had given him on Mount Sinai.
33The face of Moses kept shining, and after he had spoken with the people, he covered his face with a veil. 34Moses would always remove the veil when he went into the sacred tent to speak with the Lord. And when he came out, he would tell the people everything the Lord had told him to say. 35They could see that his face was still shining. So after he had spoken with them, he would put the veil back on and leave it on until the next time he went to speak with the Lord.
translation_text:
Mose yɛ abopon foforo
(Deuteronomium 10.1-5)
1 Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Sen abopon abien sɛ kan de no, na menkyerɛw kan apon a wobobɔe no so nsɛm no wɔ so. 2Na siesie wo ho sie anɔpa, na foro bra Sinai bepɔw so anɔpa, na gyina hɔ twɛn me bepɔw no atifi. 3 Mma obiara nnka wo ho mmforo mmma, na mma wonnhu obiara nso bepɔw no so baabiara, na mma nguan anaa anantwi mmmedidi bepɔw no ho. 4Na osen abopon abien sɛ kan de no, na Mose tuaa ahema foro kɔɔ Sinai bepɔw no so, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ no no, na ɔfaa abopon abien no kuraa ne nsam.
5 Na AWURADE nam omununkum mu sianee, na ɔne no begyinaa hɔ, na ɔpaee n'ankasa ne din YHWH (AWURADE) din. 6 Na AWURADE betwaam n'anim, na ɔpaee sɛ: YHWH, YHWH (AWURADE, AWURADE), Onyankopɔn mmɔborohunufo ne ɔdomfo, nea n'abodwo kyɛ na n'adɔeyɛ ne ne nokware dɔɔso pii, 7 nea ɔkora adɔeyɛ ma mpem mpem, na ɔde amumɔyɛ ne mmarato ne bɔne firi, na bem na ɔmma ɔbɔnefo nni, na otua agyanom amumɔyɛ so ka fa mma ne mma mma so kosi awo ntoatoaso abiɛsa ne anan so.
8Na Mose yɛɛ ntɛm kotow fam sɔree; 9na ɔkae sɛ: AWURADE, sɛ manya w'anim dom a, mesrɛ wo, ma AWURADE ntena yɛn mu ne yɛn nkɔ, efisɛ wɔyɛ ɔman a wɔn kɔn asen; na fa yɛn amumɔyɛ ne yɛn bɔne firi yɛn, na fa yɛn yɛ wo de.
AWURADE ne wɔn yɛ apam
(Eksodɔs 23.14-19; Deuteronomium 7.1-5; 16.1-17)
10Na AWURADE kae sɛ: Hwɛ, me de, merepam apam: wo man no nyinaa anim na mɛyɛ anwonwade a wɔnyɛɛ bi da asase nyinaa so ne amanaman nyinaa mu, na ɔman a wɔwɔ wɔn mu no nyinaa ahu AWURADE nnwuma, na ade a merebɛyɛ wo no bɛyɛ hu. 11Di nea mehyɛ wo nnɛ yi so. Hwɛ, meretu Amorini ne Kanaanni ne Hetini ne Perisini ne Hewini ne Yebusini no afi w'anim. 12 Hwɛ wo ho yiye na wo ne nea ɔte asase a worekɔ so no so no ampam, na wɔammɛdan wo mu afiri; 13 na mmom mummubu wɔn afɔremuka na mummuru wɔn ɔbo adum, na muntwitwa wɔn Asera nnua ngu. 14 Na nsɔre onyame foforo bi, efisɛ AWURADE a ne din ne oninkufo no yɛ Onyankopɔn ninkufo: 15na wo ne nea ɔte asase no so ampam, na wodi wɔn anyame akyi bɔ aguaman na wɔbɔ wɔn anyame afɔre a, obi ammɛfrɛ wo na woankodi n'afɔrebɔde no bi, 16 na woanware ne mmabea no bi amma wo ba, na ne mmabea no anni wɔn anyame no akyi ammɔ aguaman, na wɔamma wo mmammarima nso ankodi wɔn anyame no akyi ammɔ aguaman. 17 Nyɛ anyame a wɔagu mfa.
Afahyɛ abiɛsa no
18 Di apiti nnapɔnna no: nnansɔn na di apiti, sɛ mehyɛɛ wo no, ɔsram Abib mu, efisɛ ɔsram Abib mu na wufi Misraim bae. 19Ade biara a ebue ɔyafunu ano ne wo mmoa nyinaa mmakan a wɔyɛ anini no, nantwi oo, oguan oo, me dea. 20 Na afurum abakan de, fa oguan ba sesa no, na sɛ woansesa no a, ɛnne bu ne kɔn mu. Wo mmammarima mu mmakan nyinaa, sesa gye wɔn; na obiara mmfa ne nsapan mmmepue m'anim. 21Nnansia na yɛ adwuma, na ɛda a ɛto so ason no de, home, fɛntɛm bere mu ne otwa bere mu na home. 22Na hyɛ wo nnapɛn fa no, awitwa bere mu adekan de no, ɛne anoboa afahyɛ no, afedan mu. 23Afe mu mpɛn abiɛsa na wo mmarima nyinaa mmepue AWURADE Nyankopɔn, Israel Nyankopɔn, no anim. 24Na metu amanaman no afi w'anim, na matrɛw w'ahye mu; na woreforo akopue AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn anim afirihyia mu mpɛn abiɛsa no a, obiara ani remmere w'asase. 25Mfa mmɔkaw nka w'afɔre a wobɔ no mogya ho, na mma ade nnkye twam afahyɛ afɔre no so. 26W'asase so adekan a ɛbɛba kan no fa bra AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn fi. Nnoa oguan ba ne na nufu mu. 27 Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Kyerɛw nsɛm yi fa, efisɛ nsɛm yi so na migyina me ne wo ne Israelfo no apam.
Mose de abopon no ba
28 Na ɔne AWURADE dii hɔ adaduanan awia ne anadwo, wannidi na wannom. Na ɔkyerɛw apam nsɛm no, nsɛm du no, apon no so.
29Na Mose fi Sinai bepɔw so resian no, na adanse apon abien no kura ne nsam; nanso na Mose onnim sɛ ɔne AWURADE kasae nti, n'anim were ahyerɛn. 30 Na Aaron ne Israelfo no nyinaa huu Mose no, na hwɛ, n'anim were hyerɛn; na wosuroe sɛ wɔbɛbɛn no. 31Na Mose frɛɛ wɔn, na Aaron ne asafo no mu mpanyimfo no nyinaa san baa ne nkyɛn, na Mose ne wɔn kasae. 32Na ɛno akyi no, Israelfo no nyinaa twiw bae, na ɔhyɛɛ wɔn nea AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no Sinai bepɔw so no nyinaa. 33Na Mose ne wɔn wiee ɔkasa no, ɔde nkataanim kataa n'anim. 34 Na sɛ Mose rekɔ AWURADE anim ne no akɔkasa a, oyi nkataanim no de kosi sɛ obefi adi; na ofii adi bɛkaa nea wɔahyɛ no no kyerɛɛ Israelfo no. 35Na Israelfo no huu Mose anim were no sɛ ahyerɛn; na ɔde nkataanim no san kataa n'anim kosii sɛ ɔkɔɔ mu ne no kɔkasae.

english_text:
Laws for the Sabbath
1Moses called together the people of Israel and told them that the Lord had said:
2 You have six days in which to do your work. But the seventh day must be dedicated to me, your Lord, as a day of rest. Whoever works on the Sabbath will be put to death. 3Don't even build a cooking fire at home on the Sabbath.
Offerings for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 25.1-9; 35.10-19)
4Moses told the people of Israel that the Lord had said:
5I will welcome an offering from anyone who wants to give something. You may bring gold, silver, or bronze; 6blue, purple, or red wool; fine linen; goat hair; 7tanned ram skin or fine leather; acacia wood; 8olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices for the oil of dedication and for the incense; or 9onyx stones or other gems for the sacred vest and breastpiece.
10If you have any skills, you should use them to help make what I have commanded: 11the sacred tent with its covering and hooks, its framework and crossbars, and its post and stands; 12the sacred chest with its carrying poles, its place of mercy, and the curtain in front of it; 13the table with its carrying poles and all that goes on it, including the sacred bread; 14the lamp with its equipment and oil; 15the incense altar with its carrying poles and sweet-smelling incense; the ordination oil; the curtain for the entrance to the sacred tent; 16the altar for sacrifices with its bronze grating, its carrying poles, and its equipment; the large bronze bowl with its stand; 17the curtains with the posts and stands that go around the courtyard and the curtain at the entrance; 18the pegs and ropes for the tent and the courtyard; 19and the finely woven priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons.
Gifts for the Lord
20Moses finished speaking, and everyone left. 21Then those who wanted to bring gifts to the Lord, brought them to be used for the sacred tent, the worship services, and the priestly clothes. 22Men and women came willingly and gave all kinds of gold jewelry such as pins, earrings, rings, and necklaces. 23Everyone brought their blue, purple, and red wool, their fine linen, and their cloth made of goat hair, as well as their ram skins dyed red and their fine leather. 24Anyone who had silver or bronze or acacia wood brought it as a gift to the Lord.
25The women who were good at weaving cloth brought the blue, purple, and red wool and the fine linen they had made. 26And the women who knew how to make cloth from goat hair were glad to do so.
27The leaders brought different kinds of jewels to be sewn on the special clothes and the breastpiece for the high priest. 28They also brought sweet-smelling spices to be mixed with the incense and olive oil that were for the lamps and for ordaining the priests. 29Moses had told the people what the Lord wanted them to do, and many of them decided to bring their gifts.
Bezalel and Oholiab
(Exodus 31.1-11)
30Moses said to the people of Israel:
The Lord has chosen Bezalel of the Judah tribe. 31-33Not only has the Lord filled him with his Spirit, but he has given him wisdom and made him a skilled craftsman who can create objects of art with gold, silver, bronze, precious stones, and wood. 34The Lord is urging him and Oholiab from the tribe of Dan to teach others. 35And he has given them all kinds of artistic skills, including the ability to design and embroider with blue, purple, and red wool and to weave fine linen.
translation_text:
Homeda ho nhyehyɛe
1Na Mose hyiaa Israelfo asafo no nyinaa, na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Nsɛm a AWURADE ahyɛ sɛ munni so ni: 2 Nnansia na wɔmfa nyɛ adwuma, na ɛda a ɛto so ason no nyɛ mo homeda kronkron a mode home ma AWURADE; obiara a ɔbɛyɛ mu adwuma no, wobekum no. 3Monnsɔ ogya mo tenabere nyinaa homeda.
Soma afɔrebɔde
(Eksodɔs 25.1-9)
4Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Israelfo asafo no nyinaa sɛ: Asɛm a AWURADE ahyɛ ni: 5 Munyi soma afɔrebɔde wɔ mo mu mmrɛ AWURADE; obiara a ne koma ka no mfa soma afɔrebɔde mmrɛ AWURADE: sika ne dwetɛ ne kɔbere, 6ne bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa ne mmirekyi nwi, 7ne adwennini nhoma a wɔahyɛ no kɔkɔɔ ne sukraman nhoma ne ɔkanto nnua, 8ne kanea no ho ngo ne nnuhuam a wɔde bɛyɛ ɔsra ngo ne ɔhyew aduhuam, 9ne apopobibiri abo ne nsisimu abo a wɔde bɛyɛ asɔfotade ne adɛbo no.
10Na mo mu koma mu anyansafo nyinaa mmra mmɛyɛ ade a AWURADE ahyɛ nyinaa, 11 tenabea no, ne ntamadan ne ne nkataso ne nkɔtɔkoro ne ne ntaaboo a esisi ho, ne mmeamu, n'adum ne ne nnyinaso; 12adaka no ne ne mpoma, mpata agua no ne mmɔhɔɔ a etwa mu no, 13ɔpon no ne ne mpoma ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa ne kyerɛ abodoo no, 14kaneadua no ne ɛho nneɛma ne n'akanea ne kanea no ho ngo, 15ne aduhuamhyew muka no ne ne mpoma ne ɔsra ngo no ne ɔhyew aduhuam no ne tenabea no ano nkataano no; 16ɔhyew afɔremuka no ne ne kɔbere ntontan no, ne mpoma ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa, asankasɔn no ne ne ntaase; 17adiwo no ho mmɔhɔɔ no, n'adum ne ne nnyinaso ne adiwo no abobow ano nkataano no, 18tenabea no ho mmofunnua ne ɛho ntampehama; 19ɔsom ntade a wɔde som kronkronbea hɔ, ɔsɔfo Aaron ntade kronkron no ne ne mma ntade a wɔde bedi asɔfo no.
Ɔman no afɔrebɔde
20Na Israelfo asafo no nyinaa fii Mose anim kɔe. 21 Na wɔbae, obiara a ne koma kanyan no, ne obiara a ne honhom kaa no, na wɔde AWURADE soma afɔrebɔde bae sɛ wɔmfa nyɛ ahyiae ntamadan no ne ɛho som nneɛma nyinaa ne ntade kronkron no. 22Na mmarima ne mmea nyinaa, dodow a wɔn koma pɛ nyinaa bae, na wɔde nkapo ne asom nkaa ne mpɛtea ne krakyere ne sika nnwinne ahorow nyinaa bae, na obiara a ɔpɛ sɛ ɔde sika ohim afɔre brɛ AWURADE, 23ne obiara a ne nsam wɔ bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa ne mmirekyi nwi ne adwennini nhoma kɔkɔɔ ne sukraman nhoma no de bae; 24obiara a okura dwetɛ ne kɔbere mfraefrae soma afɔrebɔde ma AWURADE no de bae. Na obiara a ne nsam wɔ ɔkanto nnua a wɔde bɛyɛ ɔsom nneɛma no biara no nso de bae. 25Na mmea a wɔwɔ nyansa koma nyinaa de wɔn nsa too asaawa, na wɔde nea wɔtoe no bae, bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa; 26na mmea a wɔn koma kaa wɔn nyansa mu nyinaa too mmirekyi nwi asaawa. 27Na mpanyimfo no de apopobibiri abo ne nsisimu abo a wɔde bɛyɛ asɔfotade ne adɛbo no bae, 28ne nnuhuam ne ngo a wɔde bɛyɛ akanea ngo ne ɔsra ngo ne ɔhyew aduhuam no. 29Na Israelfo mu mmarima ne mmea nyinaa a wɔn koma kaa wɔn sɛ wɔmfa nnwuma a Awurade nam Mose so hyɛe sɛ wɔnyɛ no ho biribi mmra no de ayamye ayɛyɛde brɛɛ Awurade.
Ntamadan si ho adwumayɛfo
Ntomadan sie ho adwumayɛfoɔ
(Eksodɔs 31.1-11)
30 Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Israelfo no sɛ: Monhwɛ, AWURADE afrɛ Hura ba Uri ba Besalel a ofi Yuda abusuakuw mu, 31na ɔde Onyankopɔn honhom ahyɛ no ma, nyansa ne nhumu ne nimdeɛ ne adwinni nyinaa mu, 32sɛ onni adwinni horow, sika ne dwetɛ ne kɔbere, 33ne nsisimu abo mu nkurukyerɛwee ne nnua sinsen ne adwinni ahorow, 34na ɔde ahyɛ ne komam sɛ ɔnkyerɛ ebinom nso, ɔno ne Ahisamak ba Oholiab a ofi Dan abusuakuw mu no. 35Wɔn na ɔde komam nyansa ahyɛ wɔn ma sɛ wonni adwinni horow nyinaa, sikadwumfo ne duadwumfo ne ɔnwemfo a odi bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa mu adwinni ne ntamanwemfo de: wɔn a wodi adwinni biara, ne wɔn a wɔbɔ wɔn tirim di adwinni horow.

english_text:
1The Lord has given to Bezalel, Oholiab, and others the skills needed for building a place of worship, and they will follow the Lord's instructions.
2Then Moses brought together these workers who were eager to work, 3and he gave them the gifts that the people of Israel had donated for building the place of worship. In fact, so much was being given each morning, 4that finally everyone stopped working 5and said, “Moses, there is already more than we need for what the Lord has assigned us to do.” 6So Moses sent word for the people to stop giving, and they did. 7But there was already more than enough to do what needed to be done.
The Curtains and Coverings for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 26.1-14)
