8-9The skilled workers got together to make the sacred tent and its linen curtains that were woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. Each of the ten panels was twelve meters long and two meters wide, 10and they were sewn together to make two curtains with five panels each. 11-13Then 50 loops of blue cloth were put along one of the wider sides of each curtain, and the two curtains were fastened together at the loops with 50 gold hooks.
14-15As the material for protecting the tent, goat hair was used to weave eleven sections 13 meters by 2 meters each. 16These eleven sections were joined to make two panels, one with five and the other with six sections. 17Fifty loops were put along one of the wider sides of each panel, 18and the two panels were fastened at the loops with 50 bronze hooks. 19Two other coverings were made—one with fine leather and the other with ram skins dyed red.
The Framework for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 26.15-30)
20Acacia wood was used to build the framework for the walls of the sacred tent. 21Each frame was 4 meters high and 66 centimeters wide 22-26with two wooden pegs near the bottom. Then two silver stands were placed under each frame with sockets for the pegs, so they could be joined together. Twenty of these frames were used along the south side and 20 more along the north. 27Six frames were used for the back wall along the west side 28-29with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. These corner frames were joined from top to bottom. 30Altogether, along the back wall there were eight frames with two silver stands under each of them.
31-33Five crossbars were made for each of the wooden frames, with the center crossbar running the full length of the wall. 34The frames and crossbars were covered with gold, and gold rings were attached to the frames to run the crossbars through.
The Inside Curtain for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 26.31-37)
35They made the inside curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. 36They also made four acacia wood posts and covered them with gold. Then gold rings were fastened to the posts, which were set on silver stands.
37For the entrance to the tent, they used a curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework. 38They made five posts, covered them completely with gold, and set each of them on a gold-covered bronze stand. Finally, they attached hooks for the curtain.
translation_text:
Wɔde ayɛyɛde no brɛ adwumfo no
1Na Besalel ne Oholiab ne wɔn a wɔwɔ nyansa koma a Awurade de nyansa ne nhumu ahyɛ wɔn mu sɛ wonhu ade no yɛ nyinaa na wɔbɛyɛ kronkronbea ɔsom no ho adwuma, sɛnea Awurade ahyɛ no nyinaa. 2Na Mose frɛɛ Besalel ne Oholiab ne komam anyansafo a Awurade de nyansa ahyɛ wɔn koma mu nyinaa, wɔn a wɔn koma kanyan wɔn sɛ wɔmmra adwuma no ho mmɛyɛ nyinaa. 3Na wogyee soma afɔrebɔde a Israelfo de bae sɛ wɔmfa nyɛ kronkronbea som ho adwuma no nyinaa Mose anim sɛ wɔde bɛyɛ. Na wɔkɔɔ so ara de ayamye ayɛyɛde brɛɛ no daa anɔpa. 4Na adwumfo a wɔyɛ kronkronbea no ho adwuma nyinaa fi wɔn nnwuma a wɔreyɛ no ho bae 5bɛka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Ɔman no ama nea wɔde ba adɔɔso sen nea ɛbɛso adwuma a Awurade hyɛe sɛ wɔnyɛ no. 6Na Mose hyɛ ma wɔpaee nsra no mu sɛ: Ɔbarima oo, ɔbea oo, obiara mmfa biribi mmmɛyɛ kronkronbea no ho soma afɔrebɔde bio. 7Ɛnna ɔman no de gyaee ba. Efisɛ nea wɔanya no dɔɔso ma adwuma no nyinaa sɛ wɔde bɛyɛ ama ebi aka.
Ntamadan no siesie
8 Na wɔn a wɔyɛ adwuma no mu komam anyansafo nyinaa yɛɛ tenabea no; wɔde asaawa fitaa a wɔafira ne bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi yɛɛ ntama du, kerubim a ɛyɛ ntamanwene mu adwinni na wɔde yɛe. 9Ntama biara tenten si basafa dunan, na ntama biara tɛtrɛtɛ si basafa abien; ntama no nyinaa nsusuwii yɛ biako. 10Na ɔde ntama no anum toatoaa so ma biako toaa biako so, na ɔde ntama no anum nso toatoaa so ma biako toaa biako so. 11Na ɔde bibiri bobɔɔ ntama biako mmuano so nhentia wɔ ano wɔ ntoae no so, saa ara nso na ɔyɛe, ntama a edi akyiri no mmuano so wɔ ntoae a ɛto so abien no so; 12nhentia aduonum na ɔbobɔe ntama biako ano, na nhentia aduonum nso na ɔbobɔe, ntama a ɛwɔ ntoae a ɛto so abien no so no ano; nhentia no dii mmɔanim. 13Na ɔyɛɛ sika nkɔtɔkorɔ aduonum, na ɔde nkɔtɔkorɔ no toatoaa ntama no, na tenabea no yɛɛ biako.
14Na ɔyɛɛ mmirekyi nwi ntama de yɛɛ ntamadan wɔ tenabea no so; ntama dubiako na ɔyɛe. 15Ntama biako tenten si basafa dunum, na ntama biako tɛtrɛtɛ yɛ basafa abien; ntama dubiako no nsusuwii yɛ pɛ. 16Na ɔde ntama no anum toatoae yɛɛ no biako, na ɔde asia nso toatoae yɛɛ no biako. 17Na ɔbobɔɔ nhentia aduonum, ntama a edi akyiri no mmuano so, wɔ ntoae no so, na ɔbobɔɔ nhentia aduonum nso, ntoae a ɛto so abien no ntama no mmuano so. 18Na ɔyɛɛ kɔbere nkɔtɔkorɔ aduonum de toatoaa ntamadan no, na ayɛ biako.
19Na ɔde adwennini nhoma a wɔahyɛ no kɔkɔɔ yɛɛ ntamadan no nkataso, na ɔde sukraman nhoma yɛɛ ɛno so nkataso.
20 Na ɔde ɔkanto yɛɛ tenabea no ntaaboo a esisi hɔ. 21Taaboo biako tenten yɛ basafa anum, na taaboo biako tɛtrɛtɛ yɛ anammɔn abien ne fa. 22Nan abien tuatua taaboo biako ase, na biribi suso nan biako ne biako no mu: saa na ɔyɛe tenabea ntaaboo no nyinaa ho. 23Na ɔyɛɛ tenabea ntaaboo no: ntaaboo aduonu di nifa fam a ɛkyerɛ nifa. 24Na ɔyɛɛ ntaaboo aduonu no ase dwetɛ nnyinaso aduanan; nnyinaso abien hyɛ ntaaboo no biara ase ma ne nan abien no. 25Na tenabea no nkyɛn biako a edi benkum fam no, ɔde ntaaboo aduonu kosisii hɔ, 26ne ne dwetɛ nnyinaso aduanan, taaboo biara ase nnyinaso abien. 27Na tenabea no akyi fam a ɛkyerɛ atɔe no, ɔde ntaaboo asia kosisii hɔ. 28Na ɔde ntaaboo abien kosisii tenabea no akyi ntwea no so, 29na ɛpam ho fi fam de rekɔ, nanso ɛyɛ mu kodu ne hin so, nea kaa a edi kan no tua hɔ. Saa na ɔyɛɛ n'abien nyinaa ntwea abien no so. 30Na ntaaboo awotwe ne ne dwetɛ nnyinaso dunsia na ɛwɔ hɔ, taaboo biara ase nnyinaso abien.
31 Na ɔde ɔkanto yɛɛ mmeamu, tenabea no nkyɛn biako ntaaboo no de anum, 32ne tenabea no nkyɛn biako no nso ntaaboo no mmeamu anum, ne tenabea no akyi, atɔe fam ntaaboo no de, mmeamu anum. 33Na ɔde mfinimfini mmeamu no beaa ntaaboo no mfinimfini de twaa mu fi ti koduu ti. 34Na ɔde sika duraduraa ntaaboo no ho, na ɔde sika yɛɛ ɛho nkaa no sɛ ɛnyɛ mmeamu no hyehyɛbea, na ɔde sika duraduraa mmeamu no ho.
35 Na ɔde bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa a wɔafira yɛɛ mmɔhɔɔ; ɔyɛɛ no ntamanwene mu adwinni a kerubim wɔ mu. 36Na ɔyɛɛ ho ɔkanto adum anan, na ɔde sika duraduraa ho; ne nkoropɛe yɛ sika; na ɔde dwetɛ nnyinaso anan guu ase.
37Na ɔde bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa a wɔafira nwenee nkyeremu de yɛɛ ntamadan no ano nkataano. 38Na ɔyɛɛ ɛho adum anum ne nkoropɛe, na ɔde sika duraduraa n'atifi ne ne mmeae ho, na ne nnyinaso anum yɛ kɔbere.

english_text:
The Sacred Chest
(Exodus 25.10-22)
1Bezalel built a chest of acacia wood 110 centimeters long, 66 centimeters wide, and 66 centimeters high. 2He covered it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold edging around the top. 3He made four gold rings and attached one of them to each of the four legs of the chest. 4Then he made two poles of acacia wood, covered them with gold, 5and put them through the rings, so the chest could be carried by the poles.
6The entire lid of the chest, which was made of pure gold, was the place of mercy. 7-9On each of the two ends of the chest he made a winged creature of hammered gold. They faced each other, and their wings covered the place of mercy.
The Table for the Sacred Bread
(Exodus 25.23-30)
10Bezalel built a table of acacia wood 88 centimeters long, 44 centimeters wide, and 66 centimeters high. 11-12He covered it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it with a border 75 millimeters thick. 13He made four gold rings and attached one to each of the legs 14near the edging. The poles for carrying the table were placed through these rings 15and were made of acacia wood covered with gold. 16Everything that was to be set on the table was made of pure gold—the bowls, plates, jars, and cups for wine offerings.
The Lampstand
(Exodus 25.31-40)
17Bezalel made a lampstand of pure gold. The whole lampstand, including its decorative flowers, was made from a single piece of hammered gold, 18with three branches on each of its two sides. 19There were three decorative almond blossoms on each branch 20and four on the stem. 21There was also a blossom where each pair of branches came out from the stem. 22The lampstand, including its branches and decorative flowers, was made from a single piece of hammered pure gold. 23-24The lamp and its equipment, including the tongs and trays, were made of about 35 kilograms of pure gold.
The Altar for Burning Incense
(Exodus 30.1-5)
25For burning incense, Bezalel made an altar of acacia wood. It was 45 centimeters square and 90 centimeters high with each of its four corners sticking up like the horn of a bull. 26He covered it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it. 27Then below the edging on opposite sides he attached two gold rings through which he put the poles for carrying the altar. 28These poles were also made of acacia wood and covered with gold.
The Oil for Dedication and the Incense
(Exodus 30.22-38)
29 Bezalel mixed the sacred oil for dedication and the pure spices for the sweet-smelling incense.
translation_text:
Apam adaka no yɛ
(Eksodɔs 25.10-22)
1 Na Besalel de ɔkanto yɛɛ adaka no, ne tenten bɛyɛ basafa biako ne fa, na ne tɛtrɛtɛ bɛyɛ anammɔn abien ne fa, na ne sorokɔ bɛyɛ anammɔn abien ne fa. 2Na ɔde sika amapa duraa emu ne ɛho, na ɔyɛɛ sika hankare twaa ho hyiae. 3Na oguu ɛho sika nkaa anan de tuatuaa ne nan anan ho, nkaa abien wɔ ɔfa ha, na nkaa abien wɔ ɔfa ha. 4Na ɔde ɔkanto sinsen mpoma, na ɔde sika duraduraa ho. 5Na ɔde mpoma no wurawuraa nkaa no mu, adaka no nkyɛn mu, na wɔde asoa adaka no.
6Na ɔde sika amapa yɛɛ mpata agua no, ne tenten bɛyɛ basafa biako ne fa, na ne tɛtrɛtɛ anammɔn abien ne fa. 7Na ɔde sika a wɔaboro yɛɛ kerubim abien ma efii mpata agua no ti abien no mu. 8Ɔyɛɛ kerub biako wɔ ti ha, na ɔyɛɛ kerub biako nso wɔ ti ha; mpata agua no mu na ɔmaa kerubim no fii ne ti abien no so. 9Na kerubim no trɛtrɛw wɔn ntaban mu ɔsoro de wɔn ntaban no kataa mpata agua no so, na wɔn ani kyerɛkyerɛ wɔn ho; na kerubim no ani kyerɛkyerɛ mpata agua no so.
Wɔyɛ ɔpon no
(Eksodɔs 25.23-30)
10 Na ɔde ɔkanto yɛɛ ɔpon no, ne tenten basafa baako, ne tɛtrɛtɛ bɛyɛ anammɔn biako ne fa, na ne sorokɔ bɛyɛ anammɔn abien ne fa. 11Na ɔde sika amapa duraa ho, na ɔyɛɛ ɛho sika hankare hyiae. 12Na ɔyɛɛ ɛho mfomfamho a ne trɛw te sɛ nsam hyiae, na ɔyɛɛ mfomfamho no ho sika hankare hyiae. 13Na oguu ɛho sika nkaa anan, na ɔde nkaa no sisii ntwea anan a ɛwɔ ne nan anan ho no so. 14Mfomfamho no ase pa ara na nkaa a ɛyɛ mpoma a wɔde bɛsoa ɔpon no wurabea no wɔ. 15Na ɔde ɔkanto sinsen mpoma no, na ɔde sika duraduraa ho, na wɔde asoa ɔpon no. 16Na ɔde sika amapa yɛɛ ɔpon no so nneɛma, ne nsanka ne ne nsankawa ne ne nkuruwa ne ne nkora a wɔde behwie.
17 Na ɔde sika amapa yɛɛ kaneadua no, sika a wɔaboro na ɔde yɛɛ kaneadua no, ne nan ne ne dua; ɛho kuruwa, ne kukuduuduu ne ne nhwiren fi ɛno ara mu. 18Na nsa asia tuatua ho, kaneadua no nsa abiɛsa tuatua ɔfa ha, na kaneadua no nsa abiɛsa tuatua ɔfa ha. 19Nkuruwa abiɛsa a ɛte sɛ ɔsonkoran de wɔ nsa biako ho, ne kukuduuduu ne ne nhwiren, na nkuruwa abiɛsa a ɛte sɛ ɔsonkoran de wɔ nsa biako ho, ne kukuduuduu ne ne nhwiren; saa ara na ɛte nsa asia a etuatua kaneadua no ho no ho. 20Na kaneadua no ho nkuruwa a ɛte sɛ ɔsonkoran de si anan, ne kukuduuduu ne ne nhwiren; 21na kukuduuduu no wowɔ nsa abien abien a etuatua ho no ase, nsa asia a etuatua ho no ase. 22Ne kukuduuduu ne ne nsa tua ho ara, ne nyinaa yɛ sika amapa a wɔaboro no biako. 23Na ɔde sika amapa yɛɛ ɛso akanea ason no ne ɛho adabaw ne ɛho nso nkukuwa. 24Sika amapa dwetikɛse biako na ɔde yɛɛ ɛne ɛho nneɛma no nyinaa.
25 Na ɔde ɔkanto yɛɛ aduhuamhyew afɔremuka, ne tenten yɛ anammɔn biako ne fa, na ne tɛtrɛtɛ nso bɛyɛ anammɔn biako ne fa, ɛyɛ ahinanan, ne sorokɔ yɛ basafa baako; ne mmɛn nso tuatua ho ara. 26Na ɔde sika amapa duraa ho, ɛso ne ɛho hyiae, ne ne mmɛn no; na ɔyɛɛ ho sika hankare hyiae. 27Na ɔyɛɛ ɛho sika nkaa abien, ne hankare no ase, ne nkyɛn mu abien no so, sɛ ɛnyɛ mpoma no wurabea na wɔde asoa. 28Na ɔde ɔkanto sinsen mpoma, na ɔde sika duraduraa ho.
29 Na ɔyɛɛ ɔsra ngo kronkron ne ɔhyew aduhuam gyenennyenen no, sɛnea adufrafo fra no.

english_text:
The Altar for Offering Sacrifices
(Exodus 27.1-8)
1Bezalel built an altar of acacia wood for offering sacrifices. It was 2.25 meters square and 1.34 meters high 2with each of its four corners sticking up like the horn of a bull, and it was completely covered with bronze. 3The equipment for the altar was also made of bronze—the pans for the hot ashes, the shovels, the bowls, the meat forks, and the fire pans. 4About halfway up the altar he built a ledge around it and covered the bottom half of the altar with a decorative bronze grating. 5Then he attached a bronze ring beneath the ledge at the four corners to put the poles through. 6He covered two acacia wood poles with bronze and 7put them through the rings for carrying the altar, which was shaped like an open box.
The Large Bronze Bowl
(Exodus 30.18-21)
8 Bezalel made a large bowl and a stand out of bronze from the mirrors of the women who helped at the entrance to the sacred tent.
The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 27.9-19)
9-17Around the sacred tent Bezalel built a courtyard 44 meters long on the south and north and 22 meters wide on the east and west. He used 20 bronze posts on bronze stands for the south and north and 10 for the west. Then he hung a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods. He placed three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hung a curtain 6.67 meters wide on each set of posts.
18-19For the entrance to the courtyard, Bezalel made a curtain nine meters long, which he hung on four bronze posts that were set on bronze stands. This curtain was 2.25 meters high, the same height as the one for the rest of the courtyard, and was made of fine linen embroidered and woven with blue, purple, and red wool. He hung the curtain on the four posts, using silver hooks and rods. 20The pegs for the tent and for the curtain around the tent were made of bronze.
The Sacred Tent
21-23Bezalel had worked closely with Oholiab, who was an expert at designing and engraving, and at embroidering blue, purple, and red wool. The two of them completed the work that the Lord had commanded to be done.
Moses put Aaron's son Ithamar in charge of the Levites who kept record of the metals used for the sacred tent. 24According to the official weights, the amount of gold given was a ton, 25 and the silver that was collected when the people were counted came to 3.4 tons. 26 Everyone who was counted paid the required amount, and there was a total of 603,550 men who were 20 years old or older.
27Thirty-four kilograms of the silver were used to make each of the 100 stands for the sacred tent and the curtain. 28The remaining 30 kilograms of silver were used for the hooks and rods and for covering the tops of the posts.
29Two thousand four hundred and twenty-five kilograms of bronze were given. 30And it was used to make the stands for the entrance to the tent, the altar and its grating, the equipment for the altar, 31the stands for the posts that surrounded the courtyard, including those at the entrance to the courtyard, and the pegs for the tent and the courtyard.
translation_text:
Wɔyɛ Ɔhyew Afɔremuka no
(Eksodɔs 27.1-8)
1 Na ɔde ɔkanto yɛɛ ɔhyew afɔremuka no, ne tenten basafa abien ne fa ne ne tɛtrɛtɛ basafa abien ne fa, ɛyɛ ahinanan, na ne sorokɔ yɛ basafa biako ne fa. 2Na ɔyɛɛ ne mmɛn, ne twɔtwɔw anan no so, emu ara na ne mmɛn no tuatua, na ɔde kɔbere duraa ho. 3Na ɔyɛɛ afɔremuka no ho nneɛma nyinaa, nseaa ne sesaw ade ne nkora, adinam ne nsramma kukuwa no; ɛho nneɛma nyinaa, ɔde kɔbere na ɛyɛe. 4Na ɔnwenee afɔremuka no ho kɔbere ntontan a wɔanwene no sɛ ɔtan, ne bamma no ase fi fam kodu mfinimfini. 5Na oguu nkaa anan tuatuaa kɔbere ntontan no ntwea anan no so, sɛ ɛnyɛ mpoma no hyehyɛbea. 6Na ɔde ɔkanto sinsen mpoma, na ɔde kɔbere duraduraa ho. 7Na ɔde mpoma no wurawuraa nkaa no mu afɔremuka no nkyɛn nkyɛn, na wɔde asoa. Ɔde ntaaboo na ɛyɛe, na emu da ɔkwan.
Wɔyɛ ɔkanto ne adiwo
8 Na ɔde kɔbere yɛɛ asankasɔn no, na ne ntaase nso yɛ kɔbere a onya fii mmea a wɔba bɛsom, ahyiae ntamadan no ano, no kɔbere nhwehwɛ mu.
9 Na ɔyɛɛ adiwo no: nifa fam a ɛkyerɛ nifa adiwo mmɔhɔɔ a wɔde asaawa fitaa a wɔafira anwene, basafa aduonum, 10ne n'adum aduonu ne ne kɔbere nnyinaso aduonu, adum no nkoropɛe ne ne mmeae yɛ dwetɛ; 11ne benkum fam mmɔhɔɔ no, basafa aduonum, n'adum aduonu ne ne kɔbere nnyinaso aduonu, adum no nkoropɛe ne ne mmeae yɛ dwetɛ; 12ne atɔe fam mmɔhɔɔ no basafa aduonum anum, n'adum du ne ne nnyinaso du, adum no nkɔtɔkorɔ ne ne mmeae yɛ dwetɛ; 13ne anim fam a ɛkyerɛ apuei de, basafa aduonum anum: 14ɔfa ha mmɔhɔɔ basafa ason ne fa, n'adum abiɛsa ne ne nnyinaso abiɛsa; 15ne ɔfa biako no de nso adiwo no abobow ano ɔfa ha ne ha mmɔhɔɔ basafa ason ne fa, n'adum abiɛsa ne ne nnyinaso abiɛsa. 16Adiwo no mmɔhɔɔ a etwa ho hyia nyinaa, asaawa fitaa a wɔafira na wɔde yɛe, 17na adum no yɛ kɔbere, adum no nkoropɛe ne ne mmeae yɛ dwetɛ, ne ti nnuraho yɛ dwetɛ; adiwo no adum nyinaa dwetɛ mmeae na ɛbeabea ho; 18na adiwo no abobow ano nkataano no yɛ adenwene adwuma a wɔde bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa a wɔafira ayɛ, na ne tenten si basafa du, na ne sorokɔ wɔ ne trɛw mu si basafa abien ne fa, te sɛ adiwo no ho mmɔhɔɔ no; 19na n'adum anan ne ne kɔbere nnyinaso anan, ne nkoropɛe yɛ dwetɛ, na ne ti nnuraho ne ne mmeae nso yɛ dwetɛ. 20Na tenabea no ne adiwo no ho mmofunnua a etwa ho hyia no nyinaa yɛ kɔbere.
Ɔman no ayɛyɛde no anobu
21 Eyi ne tenabea no, adanse tenabea no ho nneɛma anobu, sɛnea wɔnam Mose anom asɛm so maa ɔsɔfo Aaron ba Itamar buu ano maa Lewifo som no. 22 Na Hur ba Uri ba Besalel a ofi Yuda abusuakuw mu no yɛɛ nea AWURDE hyɛɛ Mose no nyinaa; 23na nea ɔka ne ho ne Ahisamak ba Oholiab a ofi Dan abusuakuw mu a ɔyɛ sika ne dua dwumfo ne ɔnwemfo a ɔde bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa di ntama mu adwinni.
24 Sika a wɔde yɛɛ adwuma no nyinaa, kronkronbea no ho nnwuma nyinaa, ɔtow sika no, ano si dwetikɛse aduonu akron ne nnwetɛbona ahansɔn aduasa, sɛnea kronkronbea dwetɛbona no te. 25Na asafo no mu nnipa a wɔkan wɔn no dwetɛ ano si dwetikɛse ɔha ne nnwetɛbona apem ahansɔn aduɔsɔn anum, sɛnea kronkronbea dwetɛbona no te: 26wɔn a wɔkan wɔn fraa dodow no mu a wɔadi mfirihyia aduonu anaa nea ɛboro saa a wosi mpem ahansia ne mpensa ne ahanum aduonum no mu biara yii beka biako a ɛyɛ dwetɛbona fa, sɛnea kronkronbea dwetɛbona no te. 27Na wɔde dwetɛ dwetikɛse ha no guu kronkronbea no nnyinaso ne ntwamu mmɔhɔɔ no nnyinaso no, nnyinaso ha no yɛ dwetikɛse ha, dwetikɛse biako yɛ nnyinaso biako. 28Na nnwetɛbona apem ahansɔn aduɔsɔn anum no, ɔde yɛɛ adum no nkoropɛe, na ɔde bi duraduraa ne ti ho, na ɔde bi beabeaa ho. 29Na ɔtow kɔbere no ano si dwetikɛse aduɔsɔn ne nnwetɛbona mpennu ahannan. 30Na ɛno na ɔde yɛɛ ahyiae ntamadan no ano nnyinaso, ne kɔbere afɔremuka ne ɛho kɔbere ntontan ne afɔremuka no ho nneɛma nyinaa, 31ne adiwo no nnyinaso a etwa ho hyia, ne adiwo no abobow ano nnyinaso, ne tenabea no ho mmofunnua nyinaa, ne adiwo no mmofunnua a etwa ho hyia nyinaa.

english_text:
Making the Priestly Clothes
(Exodus 28.1-14)
1Beautiful priestly clothes were made of blue, purple, and red wool for Aaron to wear when he performed his duties in the holy place. This was done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
2-3The entire priestly vest was made of fine linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool. Thin sheets of gold were hammered out and cut into threads that were skillfully woven into the vest. 4-5It had two shoulder straps to support it and a sash that fastened around the waist. 6Onyx stones were placed in gold settings, and each one was engraved with the name of one of Israel's sons. 7Then these were attached to the shoulder straps of the vest, so the Lord would never forget his people. Everything was done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Breastpiece
(Exodus 28.15-30)
8The breastpiece was made with the same materials and designs as the priestly vest. 9It was 22 centimeters square and folded double 10with four rows of three precious stones: A carnelian, a chrysolite, and an emerald were in the first row; 11a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond were in the second row; 12a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst were in the third row; 13and a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper were in the fourth row. They were mounted in a delicate gold setting, 14and on each of them was engraved the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
15-18Two gold rings were attached to the upper front corners of the breastpiece and fastened with two braided gold chains to gold settings on the shoulder straps. 19Two other gold rings were attached to the lower inside corners next to the vest, 20and two more near the bottom of the shoulder straps right above the sash. 21To keep the breastpiece in place, a blue cord was used to tie the two lower rings on the breastpiece to those on the vest. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Clothes for the Priests
(Exodus 28.31-43)
22The priestly robe was made of blue wool 23with an opening in the center for the head. The material around the collar was bound so as to keep it from wearing out. 24-26Along the hem of the robe were woven pomegranates of blue, purple, and red wool with a bell of pure gold between each of them. This robe was to be worn by Aaron when he performed his duties.
27-29Everything that Aaron and his sons wore was made of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, including their robes and turbans, their fancy caps and underwear, and even their sashes that were embroidered with needlework.
30The words “Dedicated to the Lord” were engraved on a narrow strip of pure gold, 31which was fastened to Aaron's turban. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Work Is Completed
(Exodus 35.10-19)
32So the people of Israel finished making everything the Lord had told Moses to make. 33Then they brought it all to Moses: the sacred tent and its equipment, including the hooks, the framework and crossbars, and its posts and stands; 34the covering of tanned ram skins and fine leather; the inside curtain; 35the sacred chest with its carrying poles and the place of mercy; 36the table with all that goes on it, including the sacred bread; 37the lampstand of pure gold, together with its equipment and oil; 38the gold-covered incense altar; the ordination oil and the sweet-smelling incense; the curtain for the entrance to the tent; 39the bronze altar for sacrifices with its bronze grating, its carrying poles, and its equipment; the large bronze bowl with its stand; 40the curtain with its posts and cords, and its pegs and stands that go around the courtyard; everything needed for the sacred tent; 41and the finely woven priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons.
42-43When Moses saw that the people had done everything exactly as the Lord had commanded, he gave them his blessing.
translation_text:
Ɔsom ntaade no yɛ
(Eksodɔs 28.1-14)
1 Na bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi no, wɔde yɛɛ ɔsom ntade a wɔde bɛsom kronkronbea hɔ, na wɔyɛɛ Aaron ntade kronkron no, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no.
2Na ɔde sika ne bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa a wɔafira nwenee asɔfotade no. 3Na wɔboroo sika tratraa twitwaa no nteanteaa sɛ wɔde rebɛsesa bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa no mu adi no adwinni. 4Wɔyɛɛ ɛho mmati a wɔde toa; na wɔkaa ano abien no toae. 5Na asɔfotade no nkyekyeremu a ɛwɔ so no, efi mu ara te sɛ n'adwinni no ara, sika ne bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa a wɔafira, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no. 6Na wɔyɛɛ apopobibiri abo a esisi sika nnwinne mu a wɔakurukyerɛw so nsɔanode nkurukyerɛwee, sɛnea Israel mma din te. 7Na ɔde fam asɔfotade no mmati so sɛ ɛnyɛ Israelfo no nkae abo, sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Mose no.
Adɛbo no yɛ
(Eksodɔs 28.15-30)
8Na ɔde adwinni nwenee adɛbo no sɛ asɔfotade no adwinni no te, sika bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa a wɔafira; 9ɛyɛ ahinanan, wobukaw adɛbo no to so, ne tenten yɛ nsama na ne trɛw yɛ nsama, na wobukaw to so. 10Na wɔde abo kyerɛpɛn anan sisii mu; kyerɛpɛn a edi kan no yɛ bogyanam bo, akrate bo ne ahabammono bo; 11na kyerɛpɛn a ɛto so abien yɛ nsrama bo, hoa bo ne bɔwerɛ bo; 12na kyerɛpɛn a ɛto so abiɛsa yɛ akutuhono bo, mfrafrae bo ne beredum bo; 13na kyerɛpɛn a ɛto so anan yɛ sikabereɛbo, apopobibiribo ne ahwehwɛbo; ne nsisimu no wɔyɛɛ ho sika nnwinne hyiae. 14Na abo no ano du Israel mma no din ano, dumien, sɛ wɔn din te; ɛyɛ nsɔanode nkurukyerɛwee, sɛnea din no te mmiako mmiako, sɛ mmusuakuw dumien no te. 15Na wɔde sika amapa yɛɛ adɛbo no so ntweaban a wɔawɔw no mmɛsa sɛ nhama. 16Na wɔyɛɛ sika nnwinne abien ne sika nkaa abien, na wɔde nkaa abien no hyehyɛɛ adɛbo no ntwea abien so. 17Na wɔde sika mmɛsa abien no toatoaa nkaa abien a ɛwowɔ adɛbo no ntwea so no mu. 18Na wɔde mmɛsa abien no ano abien a aka no toatoaa nnwinne abien no mu, na wɔde hyehyɛɛ asɔfotade no mmati abien no so, anim fam. 19Na wɔyɛɛ sika nkaa abien de hyehyɛɛ adɛbo no ntwea abien no so, wɔ ano a ɛwɔ emu fam kyerɛ asɔfotade no. 20Na wɔyɛɛ sika nkaa abien bio de hyehyɛɛ asɔfotade no afaafa abien no so anim fam wɔ ase a ɛbɛn ne ntoae, nguguso no nkyekyeremu no so. 21Na wɔde bibiri nhama kyekyeree adɛbo nkaa no susoo nguguso no nkaa no mu sɛ ɛmfam asɔfotade no nkyekyeremu no atifi, na adɛbo no antwitwiw amfi asɔfotade no so, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no.
Asɔfotade afoforɔ no yɛ
(Eksodɔs 28.31-43)
22 Na ɔyɛɛ asɔfotade no ase batakari no, wɔde birisi na ɛnwenee ne nyinaa. 23Na batakari no tokuru da ne mfinimfini te sɛ nkatabo mu tokuru, wɔde ntamabena ban tokuru no ano hyiae, na ansuane. 24Na wɔde bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi a wɔafira yɛɛ ateaa aba wɔ batakari no mmuano so. 25Na wɔyɛɛ sika amapa nnɔnnɔmma, na wɔde nnɔnnɔmma no sensɛn ateaa aba no ntam ntam, batakari no mmuano no so de twaa ho hyiae, ateaa aba no ntam ntam: 26adɔmma ne ateaa aba, adɔmma ne ateaa aba didi so ara batakari no mmuano so hyia, na wɔde asom, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no.
27 Na wɔde nwera fɛfɛ a wɔanwene yɛɛ ntade yuu no maa Aaron ne ne mma, 28ne nwera abotiten, ne nwera ahokeka abotiri, ne nwera twakoto a wɔde asaawa fitaa a wɔafira ayɛ, 29ne adenwene abɔmu a wɔde asaawa fitaa a wɔafira ne bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi yɛe, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no.
30 Na wɔboroo sika amapa tratraa de yɛɛ abɔanim kronkron no, na wɔkyerɛw so nkyerɛwee sɛ nsɔanode so nkurukyerɛwee sɛ: Kronkron ma AWURADE. 31Na wɔde bibiri hama kyekyere fam abotiten no so, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no.
Adwuma no wie
(Eksodɔs 35.10-19)
32Na wɔyɛɛ ahyiae ntamadan no ho adwuma nyinaa wiei, na Israelfo yɛe sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no nyinaa; saa ara na wɔyɛe. 33Na wɔde tenabea no brɛɛ Mose: ntamadan no ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa, ne nkɔtɔkoro, ne nsisiho ntaaboo, ne mmeamu ne ne nsisimu adum ne ne nnyinaso; 34ne adwennini nhoma a wɔahyɛ no kɔkɔɔ nkataso ne sukraman nhoma nkataso, ne ntwamu mmɔhɔɔ no; 35adanse adaka ne ne mpoma ne mpata agua no; 36ɔpon no ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa ne kyerɛ abodoo no; 37kaneadua kronkron no, n'akanea a wɔasiesie sisi so ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa ne kanea no ngo; 38ne sika afɔremuka ne ɔsra ngo ne ɔhyew aduhuam ne ntamadan no ano nkataano no; 39kɔbere afɔremuka no ne ɛho kɔbere ntontan no, ne mpoma ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa; asankasɔn no ne ne ntaase; 40adiwo no mmɔhɔɔ, n'adum ne ne nnyinaso ne adiwo no abobow ano nkataano, ne ntampehama ne ne mmofunnua, ne ahyiae ntamadan no tenabea no som ho nneɛma nyinaa; 41ɔsom ntade a wɔde som kronkronbea hɔ ne ɔsɔfo Aaron ntade kronkron ne ne mma ntade a wɔde bedi asɔfo no. 42Sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no nyinaa, saa ara na Israelfo yɛɛ adwuma no nyinaa. 43Na Mose hwɛɛ adwuma no nyinaa, na hwɛ, wɔayɛ no sɛnea AWURADE hyɛe no, saa pɛ na wɔyɛe. Na Mose hyiraa wɔn.

english_text:
The Lord's Tent Is Set Up
1The Lord said to Moses:
2Set up my tent on the first day of the year 3and put the chest with the Ten Commandments behind the inside curtain. 4Bring in the table and set on it those things that are made for it. Also bring in the lampstand and attach the lamps to it. 5Then place the gold altar of incense in front of the sacred chest and hang a curtain at the entrance to the tent. 6Set the altar for burning sacrifices in front of the entrance to my tent. 7Put the large bronze bowl between the tent and the altar and fill the bowl with water. 8Surround the tent and the altar with the wall of curtains and hang the curtain that was made for the entrance.
9Use the sacred olive oil to dedicate to me the tent and everything in it. 10Do the same thing with the altar for offering sacrifices and its equipment 11and with the bowl and its stand. 12Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent and tell them to wash themselves. 13Dress Aaron in the priestly clothes, then use the sacred olive oil to ordain him and dedicate him to me as my priest. 14Put the priestly robes on Aaron's sons 15and ordain them in the same way, so they and their descendants will always be my priests.
16Moses followed the Lord's instructions. 17And on the first day of the first month of the second year, the sacred tent was set up. 18The posts, stands, and framework were put in place, 19then the two layers of coverings were hung over them. 20The stones with the Ten Commandments written on them were stored in the sacred chest, the place of mercy was put on top of it, and the carrying poles were attached. 21The chest was brought into the tent and set behind the curtain in the most holy place. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
22The table for the sacred bread was put along the north wall of the holy place, 23after which the bread was set on the table. 24The lampstand was put along the south wall, 25then the lamps were attached to it there in the presence of the Lord. 26The gold incense altar was set up in front of the curtain, 27and sweet-smelling incense was burned on it. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
28The curtain was hung at the entrance to the sacred tent. 29Then the altar for offering sacrifices was put in front of the tent, and animal sacrifices and gifts of grain were offered there. 30The large bronze bowl was placed between the altar and the entrance to the tent. It was filled with water, 31then Moses and Aaron, together with Aaron's sons, washed their hands and feet. 32In fact, they washed each time before entering the tent or offering sacrifices at the altar. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
33Finally, Moses had the curtains hung around the courtyard and at the entrance.
The Glory of the Lord
34 Suddenly the sacred tent was covered by a thick cloud and filled with the glory of the Lord. 35And so, Moses could not enter the tent. 36Whenever the cloud moved from the tent, the people would break camp and follow; 37then they would set up camp and stay there, until it moved again. 38No matter where the people traveled, the Lord was with them. Each day his cloud was over the tent, and each night a fire could be seen in the cloud.
translation_text:
Wotu Tenabea no hyɛ AWURADE nsa
1 Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 2Ɔsram a edi kan no da a edi kan no na si ahyiae ntamadan no tenabea no. 3Na fa adanse adaka no si mu, na fa ntwamu mmɔhɔɔ no kata adaka no ani. 4Na fa ɔpon no kɔ mu, na siesie nea wɔde sisi so no; na fa kaneadua no kɔ mu, na fa n'akanea sisi so. 5Na fa sika aduhuamhyew muka no kosi adanse adaka no anim; na fa tenabea no ano nkataano no sɛn hɔ. 6Na fa ɔhyew afɔremuka no si ahyiae ntamadan tenabea no ano. 7Na fa asankasɔn no si ahyiae ntamadan no ne afɔremuka no ntam, na fa nsu gu mu. 8Na sisi adiwo no hyia, na fa adiwo no abobow ano nkataano no sɛn hɔ. 9Na fa ɔsra ngo no sra tenabea no ne emu ade nyinaa, na yɛ ɛno ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa kronkron na ɛnyɛ akronkronne. 10Na sra ɔhyew afɔremuka no ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa ngo, na yɛ afɔremuka no kronkron, na afɔremuka no nyɛ akronkronne mu adekronkron. 11Na sra asankasɔn ne ne ntaase no ngo, na yɛ no kronkron. 12Na fa Aaron ne ne mma no bra ahyiae ntamadan no ano, na fa nsu guare wɔn.
13Na fa ntade kronkron no hyɛ Aaron, na sra no ngo yɛ no kronkron, na onni me sɔfo. 14Na fa ne mma nso bra, na hyehyɛ wɔn ntade, 15na sra wɔn ngo sɛnea wosraa wɔn agya no, na wonni me asɔfo, na wɔn sra no nyɛ wɔn daa asɔfodi, wɔn awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu. 16Na Mose yɛe sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ no no nyinaa, saa ara na ɔyɛe.
17Na afe a ɛto so abien no sram a edi kan no da a edi kan no, wosii tenabea no. 18Na Mose sii tenabea no, na ɔhyehyɛɛ ne nnyinaso na ogyinagyinaa ne ntaaboo no, na ɔde ne mmeamu no beabeaa mu, na ogyinagyinaa ne nsisimu adum. 19Na ɔyeree ntamadan no kataa tenabea no so, na ɔde ntamadan no nkataso no kataa so, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no. 20Na ɔfaa Adanse no de hyɛɛ adaka no mu, na ɔde mpoma wurawuraa adaka no ho, na ɔde mpata agua no sii adaka no so; 21na ɔde adaka no kɔɔ tenabea no mu, na osii ntwamu mmɔhɔɔ no, na ɔde kataa adanse adaka no ano, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no. 22Na ɔde ɔpon no sii ahyiae ntamadan no mu, tenabea no nkyɛn mu a ɛkyerɛ benkum fam, wɔ ntwamu mmɔhɔɔ no akyi; 23na osiesiee ɛso abodoo AWURADE anim, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no. 24Na ɔde kaneadua no sii ahyiae ntamadan no mu, ɔpon no ntentenso wɔ tenabea no nkyɛn mu a ɛkyerɛ nifa fam; 25na ɔde akanea no sisii so AWURADE anim, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no. 26Na ɔde sika afɔremuka no sii ahyiae ntamadan no mu, ntwamu mmɔhɔɔ no anim; 27na ɔhyew so aduhuam, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no. 28Na ɔde nkataano no sɛn tenabea no ano; 29na ɔde ɔhyew afɔremuka no sii ahyiae ntamadan tenabea no ano, na ɔbɔɔ so ɔhyew afɔre ne aduan afɔre, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no. 30Na ɔde asankasɔn no sii ahyiae ntamadan no ne afɔremuka no ntam, na ɔde nsu guu mu sɛ wɔmfa nhohoro wɔn ho. 31Na Mose ne Aaron ne ne mma no de hohoroo wɔn nsa ne wɔn nan ho; 32sɛ wɔkɔ ahyiae ntamadan no mu anaasɛ wɔrebɛbɛn afɔremuka no ho a, wɔhohoroo wɔn ho, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no. 33Na osii adiwo no de twaa tenabea no ne afɔremuka no ho hyiae, na ɔde adiwo no abobow ano mmɔhɔɔ no sɛn hɔ. Na Mose wiee adwuma no.
Omununkum bɛkata tenabea no so
34 Ɛnna omununkum no bɛkataa ahyiae ntamadan no so, na AWURADE anuonyam bɛhyɛɛ tenabea no ma. 35Na Mose antumi anhyɛn ahyiae ntamadan no mu, efisɛ omununkum no te so, na AWURADE anuonyam ahyɛ tenabea no ma. 36 Na Israelfo akwantu no nyinaa mu, omununkum no ma ne ho so fi tenabea no so a, na wɔkɔ wɔn anim; 37na sɛ omununkum no amma ne ho so a, ɛnne wontu ara kosi da a ɛma ne ho so. 38Efisɛ wɔn akwantu no nyinaa mu na AWURADE mununkum no wɔ tenabea no so awia, na ogya wɔ mu anadwo, Israel fi no nyinaa anim.

english_text:
1-3The Lord spoke to Moses from the sacred tent and gave him instructions for the community of Israel to follow when they offered sacrifices.
Sacrifices To Please the Lord
The Lord said:
Sacrifices to please me must be completely burned on the bronze altar.
Bulls or rams or goats are the animals to be used for these sacrifices. If the animal is a bull, it must not have anything wrong with it. Lead it to the entrance of the sacred tent, and I will let you know if it is acceptable to me. 4Lay your hand on its head, and I will accept the animal as a sacrifice for taking away your sins.
5After the bull is killed in my presence, some priests from Aaron's family will offer its blood to me by splattering it against the four sides of the altar.
6Skin the bull and cut it up, 7while the priests pile wood on the altar fire to make it start blazing. 8-9Wash the bull's insides and hind legs, so the priests can lay them on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. A priest will then send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
10If you sacrifice a ram or a goat, it must not have anything wrong with it. 11Lead the animal to the north side of the altar, where it is to be killed in my presence. Then some of the priests will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
12-13Cut up the animal and wash its insides and hind legs. A priest will put these parts on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. Then he will send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
14If you offer a bird for this kind of sacrifice, it must be a dove or a pigeon. 15A priest will take the bird to the bronze altar, where he will wring its neck and put its head on the fire. Then he will drain out its blood on one side of the altar, 16remove the bird's craw with what is in it, and throw them on the ash heap at the east side of the altar. 17Finally, he will take the bird by its wings, tear it partially open, and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_text:
Ɔhyew afɔrebɔde
1Na AWURADE frɛɛ Mose, na ofi ahyiae ntamadan no mu kasa kyerɛɛ no sɛ: 2Kasa kyerɛ Israelfo, na ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Sɛ mo mu bi de ayɛyɛde rebrɛ AWURADE a, afieboa a ofi anantwi ne nguan mu na momfa nyɛ mo ayɛyɛde mmra.
3 Sɛ n'ayɛyɛde no yɛ ɔhyew afɔre a efi anantwi mu a, ɔmfa onini a odi mu mmra; ahyiae ntamadan no ano na ɔmfa no mmra, na wasɔ AWURADE ani. 4 Na ɔmfa ne nsa nto ɔhyew afɔre no atifi, na ɛnsɔ ani mma no na ɛmpata mma no. 5Na onkum nantwi ba no, AWURADE anim, na Aaron mma, asɔfo no, mfa mogya no mmra, na wɔmfa mpete afɔremuka a ɛwɔ ahyiae ntamadan no ano no so nhyia. 6Na ongua ɔhyew afɔre no nhoma, na ontwitwa no asinasin. 7Na ɔsɔfo Aaron mma no nsiesie mmabaa wɔ afɔremuka no so na wɔnsɔ ano. 8Na Aaron mma, asɔfo no, mfa asinasin no, botiri no ne srade no ngu afɔremuka gya no so. 9 Na ɔnhohoro n'ayamde ne ne nnyawa ho wɔ nsu mu; na ɔsɔfo no nhyew ne nyinaa afɔremuka no so, na ɛnyɛ ɔhyew afɔre, ogya afɔre a eyi hua huamhuam ma AWURADE.
10Na sɛ n'ayɛyɛde no fi nguan mu, nguanten anaa mmirekyi mu, na ɔde rekɔbɔ ɔhyew afɔre a, onini a odi mu na ɔmfa mmra. 11Na onkum no afɔremuka no nkyɛn mu atifi fam, AWURADE anim, na Aaron mma, asɔfo no, mfa ne mogya mpete afɔremuka no so nhyia. 12Na ontwitwa n'asinasin no mu, ɛne ne ti ne ne srade nyinaa, na ɔsɔfo no nsiesie ngu afɔremuka no so gya no so. 13Na ayamde ne nnyawa no, ɔmfa nsu nhohoro ho; na ɔsɔfo no mfa ne nyinaa mmra mmɛhyew afɔremuka no so; ɛyɛ ɔhyew afɔre, ogya afɔre a eyi hua huamhuam ma AWURADE.
14Na sɛ n'ayɛyɛde no fi ntakraboa mu na ɔde rebɛbɔ ɔhyew afɔre ama AWURADE a, ɔmfa nturukuku anaa mmorɔnoma mma nyɛ n'ayɛyɛde mmra. 15Na ɔsɔfo no mfa mmra afɔremuka no ho, na ɔntew ne ti, na ɔnhyew afɔremuka no so, na wonkyi ne mogya ngu afɔremuka no ho. 16Na onyi ne mene ase ne nea ɛwɔ mu ntow nkyene afɔremuka no nkyɛn apuei fam, nea nso gu hɔ. 17Na onsuan ne mu, ne ntaban ho, nanso ɔnntew mu, na ɔsɔfo no nhyew wɔ afɔremuka no so, wɔ ogya no so, ɛyɛ ɔhyew afɔre, ogya afɔre a eyi hua huamhuam ma AWURADE.

english_text:
Sacrifices To Give Thanks to the Lord
The Lord said:
1When you offer sacrifices to give thanks to me, you must use only your finest flour. Put it in a dish, sprinkle olive oil and incense on the flour, 2and take it to the priests from Aaron's family. One of them will scoop up the incense together with a handful of the flour and oil. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay this part on the bronze altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 3The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
4If you bake bread in an oven for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour, but without any yeast. You may make the flour into a loaf mixed with olive oil, or you may make it into thin wafers and brush them with oil.
5If you cook bread in a shallow pan for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour. Mix it with olive oil, but do not use any yeast. 6Then break the bread into small pieces and sprinkle them with oil. 7If you cook your bread in a pan with a lid on it, you must also use the finest flour mixed with oil.
8You may prepare sacrifices to give thanks in any of these three ways. Bring your sacrifice to a priest, and he will take it to the bronze altar. 9Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay part of it on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 10The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
11Yeast and honey must never be burned on the altar, so don't ever mix either of these in a grain sacrifice. 12You may offer either of them separately, when you present the first part of your harvest to me, but they must never be burned on the altar.
13Salt is offered when you make an agreement with me, so sprinkle salt on these sacrifices.
14Freshly cut grain, either roasted or coarsely ground, must be used when you offer the first part of your grain harvest. 15You must mix in some olive oil and put incense on top, because this is a grain sacrifice. 16A priest will sprinkle all of the incense and some of the grain and oil on the altar and send them up in smoke to show that the whole offering belongs to me.
translation_text:
Aduan afɔrebɔ
1Na sɛ obi de aduan afɔre ayɛyɛde rebrɛ AWURADE a, n'ayɛyɛde no nyɛ asikresam, na ongu so ngo, na ɔmfa ohuamfufu nto so. 2Na ɔmfa mmrɛ Aaron mma no, asɔfo no, na ɔsɔfo no mfa asikresam ne ngo no nsa mama, ne ohuamfufu no nyinaa, na ɔnhyew wɔ afɔremuka no so sɛ nkae ade. Ɛyɛ ogya afɔre a eyi hua huamhuam ma AWURADE. 3Na aduan afɔre no mu nea ɛbɛka no nyɛ Aaron ne ne mma dea. AWURADE gya mu akronkronne mu ade kronkron ne no.
4Na sɛ wode aduan afɔre ayɛyɛde a wɔato no fononoo mu reba a, fa asikresam apiti a wɔde ngo afɔtɔw tetare ne apiti fam a wɔagu so ngo bra. 5Na sɛ w'ayɛyɛde no yɛ aduan afɔre a wɔakyew no dade so a, ma ɛnyɛ asikresam apiti a wɔde ngo afɔtɔw; 6bubu mu asinasin, na hwie ngo gu so; aduan afɔre ne no.
7Na sɛ w'ayɛyɛde no yɛ kutu mu aduan afɔre a, fa asikresam ne ngo yɛ. 8Na fa aduan afɔre a wɔde nneɛma yi ayɛ no brɛ AWURADE; na wɔde brɛ ɔsɔfo no a, ɔmfa mmra afɔremuka no ho. 9Na ɔsɔfo no nyi ayɛyɛde no so nkae ade no, na ɔnhyew wɔ afɔremuka no so, ogya afɔre a eyi hua huamhuam ma AWURADE ne no. 10Na aduan afɔre no nkae nyɛ Aaron ne ne mma dea; akronkronne mu adekronkron a efi AWURADE gya afɔre mu ne no.
11 Aduan afɔre a mode bɛbrɛ AWURADE no nyinaa, mommfa mmɔkaw nnyɛ; na monnhyew mmɔkaw biara ne ɛwo biara sɛ ogya afɔre mma AWURADE. 12 Momfa nneɛma yi mmrɛ AWURADE sɛ aba a edi kan mu afɔrebɔde, nanso wɔmmfa bi mmma afɔremuka no so sɛ emmeyi hua huamhuam. 13 Na w'aduan afɔre ayɛyɛde nyinaa, to mu nkyene, na mma wo Nyankopɔn apam nkyene mmpa w'aduan afɔre mu; fa nkyene ka w'ayɛyɛde nyinaa ho.
14 Na sɛ wode aba a edi kan ayɛyɛde rebrɛ AWURADE a, fa aburow mmɛtem a wɔato no ogya mu atutu apa ho yɛ w'aba a edi kan mu ayɛyɛde; 15na fa ngo gu so, na fa ohuamfufu to so: aduan afɔre ne no. 16Na ɔsɔfo no nhyew aburow mfuamfua a wɔapa ho no bi ne ngo no bi ne ohuamfufu no nyinaa sɛ nkae ade: ɛyɛ ogya afɔre a wɔbɔ ma AWURADE.

english_text:
Sacrifices To Ask the Lord's Blessing
The Lord said:
1When you offer sacrifices to ask my blessing, you may offer either a bull or a cow, but there must be nothing wrong with the animal. 2Lead it to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay your hand on its head, and have it killed there. A priest from Aaron's family will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
3Offer all of the fat on the animal's insides, 4as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 5Some of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me, together with the sacrifice that is offered to please me.
6Instead of a bull or a cow, you may offer any sheep or goat that has nothing wrong with it. 7If you offer a sheep, you must present it to me at the entrance to the sacred tent. 8Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
9Offer the fat on the tail, the tailbone, and the insides, 10as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 11One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering for me.
12If you offer a goat, you must also present it to me 13at the entrance to the sacred tent. Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
14Offer all of the fat on the animal's insides, 15as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 16One of the priests will put these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering with a smell that pleases me.
All fat belongs to me. 17So you and your descendants must never eat any fat or any blood, not even in the privacy of your own homes. This law will never change.
translation_text:
Asomdwoe afɔrebɔ
1Na sɛ obi ayɛyɛde yɛ asomdwoe afɔre, na anantwi no bi na ɔde reba a, onini oo, ɔbere oo, nea odi mu na ɔmfa no mmra AWURADE anim. 2Na ɔmfa ne nsa nto n'ayɛyɛde no atifi, na onkum no, ahyiae ntamadan no ano, na Aaron mma no, asɔfo no, mfa mogya no mpete afɔremuka no so nhyia. 3Na onyi asomdwoe afɔre no bi mmra mmɛyɛ AWURADE gya afɔre: srade a ɛkata ayamde no so no ne ayamde no ho srade nyinaa, 4ne asaabo abien no ne srade a ɛwɔ ho, sisia mu no, ne mmerɛbo so ntontan no; omfi asaabo ho nyi. 5Na Aaron mma no nhyew, afɔremuka no so, mpae ɔhyew afɔre a egu ogya no so no, na ɛnyɛ ogya afɔre a eyi hua huamhuam ma AWURADE.
6Na sɛ n'ayɛyɛde a ɔde rebɛbɔ asomdwoe afɔre ama AWURADE no yɛ nguan no bi a, onini oo, ɔbere oo, nea odi mu na ɔmfa mmra. 7Sɛ n'ayɛyɛde no yɛ oguammaa na ɔde reba a, ɔmfa mmra AWURADE anim; 8na ɔmfa ne nsa nto n'ayɛyɛde no atifi, na onkum no ahyiae ntamadan no ano, na Aaron mma no mfa ne mogya mpete afɔremuka no so nhyia. 9Na onyi asomdwoe afɔre no bi mmra mmɛbɔ ogya afɔre mma AWURADE: ne srade ne ne sradedua mu a ontwa no pidua so pa ara ne srade a ɛkata ayamde no so ne ayamde no ho srade nyinaa, 10ne asaabo abien no ne srade a ɛwɔ ho, sisia mu no, ne mmerɛbo so ntontan no; omfi asaabo ho nyi. 11Na ɔsɔfo no nhyew wɔ afɔremuka no so: ɛyɛ aduan afɔre a wɔbɔ no gya so ma AWURADE.
12Na sɛ n'ayɛyɛde no yɛ abirekyi a, ɔmfa mmra AWURADE anim; 13na ɔmfa ne nsa nto n'atifi, na onkum no, ahyiae ntamadan no ano, na Aaron mma no mfa ne mogya mpete afɔremuka no so nhyia. 14Na onyi bi mmra mmɛyɛ n'ayɛyɛde, AWURADE gya afɔre: srade a ɛkata ayamde so no ne ayamde ho srade nyinaa; 15ne asaabo abien no, ne srade a ɛwɔ ho, sisia mu no, ne mmerɛbo so ntontan no; omfi asaabo ho nyi. 16Na ɔsɔfo no nhyew wɔ afɔremuka no so, ɛyɛ ogya afɔreduan a eyi hua huamhuam; srade no nyinaa yɛ AWURADE dea. 17 Ɛnyɛ daa ahyɛde, mo awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu ne mo tenabea nyinaa sɛ munnni srade anaa mogya biara.

english_text:
Sacrifices for Sin
(Leviticus 6.24-30)
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to the community of Israel:
Offer a sacrifice to ask forgiveness when you sin by accidentally doing something I have told you not to do.
When the High Priest Sins
The Lord said:
3When the high priest sins, he makes everyone else guilty too. And so, he must sacrifice a young bull that has nothing wrong with it. 4The priest will lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay his hand on its head, and kill it there. 5He will take a bowl of the blood inside the tent, 6dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain. 7Then, in my presence, he will smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent.
8-10The priest will remove the fat from the bull, just as he does when he sacrifices a bull to ask my blessing. This includes the fat on the insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. He will then send it all up in smoke.
11-12The skin and flesh of the bull, together with its legs, insides, and the food still in its stomach, are to be taken outside the camp and burned on a wood fire near the ash heap.
When the Whole Nation Sins
The Lord said:
13When the nation of Israel disobeys me without meaning to, the whole nation is still guilty. 14Once you realize what has happened, you must sacrifice a young bull to ask my forgiveness. Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, 15where your tribal leaders will lay their hands on its head, before having it killed in my presence.
16The priest will take a bowl of the animal's blood inside the sacred tent, 17dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain. 18Then, in my presence, he must smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent. 19-21After this, the priest will remove the fat from the bull and send it up in smoke on the altar. Finally, he will burn its remains outside the camp, just as he did with the other bull. By this sacrifice the sin of the whole nation will be forgiven.
When a Tribal Leader Sins
The Lord God said:
22Any tribal leader who disobeys me without knowing it is still guilty. 23As soon as the leader realizes what has happened, he must sacrifice a goat that has nothing wrong with it. 24This is a sacrifice for sin. So he will lay his hand on the animal's head, before having it killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar. 25The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar. 26Then he must send all of the fat up in smoke, just as he does when a sacrifice is offered to ask my blessing. By this sacrifice the leader's sin will be forgiven.
When Ordinary People Sin
The Lord said:
27 When any of you ordinary people disobey me without meaning to, you are still guilty. 28As soon as you realize what you have done, you must sacrifice a female goat that has nothing wrong with it. 29Lead the goat to the north side of the bronze altar and lay your hand on its head, before having it killed. 30Then a priest will dip a finger in the blood; he will smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar. 31After this, the priest will remove all of the fat, just as he does when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. The priest will then send the fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. This animal is sacrificed so that I will forgive you ordinary people when you sin.
32If you offer a lamb instead of a goat as a sacrifice for sin, it must be a female that has nothing wrong with it. 33Lead the lamb to the altar and lay your hand on its head, before having it killed. 34The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar. 35After this, all of the fat must be removed, just as when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. Then the priest will send it up in smoke to me, together with a food offering, and your sin will be forgiven.
translation_text:
Bɔne ho afɔre
1Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 2Kasa kyerɛ Israelfo sɛ: Sɛ obi anhyɛ da na ɔyɛ nneɛma a AWURADE ahyɛ sɛ wɔnnyɛ no mu biara no, na ɔkɔyɛ emu biara a, 3sɛ nso ɛyɛ ɔsɔfo a wɔasra no (ɔsɔfopanyin) yɛ bɔne ma ɔman no di so a, ɛnne ne bɔne a ɔyɛe nti ma ɔmfa nantwi ba onini a odi mu mmrɛ AWURADE mmɛbɔ bɔne ho afɔre. 4Na ɔmfa nantwinini no mmra ahyiae ntamadan no ano, na ɔmfa ne nsa nto n'atifi, na onkum no, AWURADE anim. 5Na ɔsɔfo a wɔasra no no mfa nantwi no mogya no bi nkɔ ahyiae ntamadan no mu, 6 na ɔsɔfo no mfa ne nsatea mmɔ mogya no mu, na ɔmpete mogya no bi mpɛn asɔn, AWURADE anim, kronkronbea ntwamu mmɔhɔɔ no anim. 7 Na ɔsɔfo no mfa mogya no bi nkeka aduhuamhyew muka a ɛwɔ AWURADE anim, ahyiae ntamadan mu no mmɛn ho, na onhwie nantwi no mogya nyinaa ngu ɔhyew afɔremuka a ɛwɔ ahyiae ntamadan ano no ase. 8Na onyi bɔne ho afɔre nantwi no srade nyinaa mfi ne ho: srade a ɛkata ayamde no so ne ayamde no ho srade nyinaa, 9ne asaabo abien no ne srade a ɛwɔ so, sisia mu no, ne mmerɛbo so ntontan no; omfi asaabo ho nyi, 10sɛnea woyi fi asomdwoe afɔre nantwi ho no; na ɔsɔfo no nhyew wɔ ɔhyew afɔremuka no so. 11 Na ɔmfa nantwinini no nhoma ne ne nam nyinaa ne ne ti ne ne nnyawa ne n'ayamde ne ne n'agyanan no, 12 nantwinini mu no nyinaa, mfi nkɔ nsra no akyi, nea ɛhɔ tew, nea wohwie nso gu, na ɔmfa ogya nhyew wɔ mmabaa so; nea wohwie nso gu na wɔnhyew.
Ɔman mu no
13 Na sɛ Israel asafo nyinaa fom, na asɛm no ahintaw ɔman no, na wɔyɛ nneɛma a AWURADE ahyɛ sɛ wɔnnyɛ no mu bi, na wodi so, 14 na wohu bɔne a wɔayɛ de afom no a, ɛnne asafo no mfa nantwi ba onini mmra mmɛbɔ bɔne ho afɔre, na wɔmfa no mmra ahyiae ntamadan no ano. 15Na asafo no mu mpanyimfo mfa wɔn nsa ngu nantwinini no atifi, na wonkum nantwi no, AWURADE anim. 16Na ɔsɔfo a wɔasra no no mfa nantwinini no mogya no bi nhyɛn ahyiae ntamadan no mu, 17na ɔsɔfo no mfa ne nsatea mmɔ mogya no mu mfa mpete mpɛn asɔn, AWURADE anim, ntwamu mmɔhɔɔ no anim, 18na ɔmfa mogya no bi nkeka afɔremuka a esi AWURADE anim, ahyiae ntamadan no mu no mmɛn ho, na onhwie mogya no nyinaa ngu ɔhyew afɔremuka a esi ahyiae ntamadan ano no ase. 19Na onyi ne srade nyinaa mfi so, na ɔnhyew wɔ ɔhyew afɔremuka no so. 20Na sɛnea ɔyɛɛ bɔne ho afɔre nantwinini no, saa ara na ɔnyɛ eyi nso; na ɔsɔfo no mpata mma wɔn, na wɔde bɛkyɛ wɔn. 21 Na ɔmfa nantwinini no mfi nkɔ nsra no akyi, na ɔnhyew no sɛnea wɔhyew kan nantwinini no, asafo no bɔne ho afɔre ne no.
Ɔman no mu atitiriw
22Sɛ otitiriw bi anhyɛ da na ɔyɛ nneɛma a AWURADE ne Nyankopɔn ahyɛ sɛ wɔnnyɛ no nyinaa mu ade biako, na odi so, na sɛ wɔma ohu ne bɔne a wayɛ no a, 23ɛnne ɔmfa n'ayɛyɛde a ɛyɛ ɔpapo a odi mu mmra; 24na ɔmfa ne nsa nto ɔpapo no atifi, na onkum no nea wokum ɔhyew afɔre no wɔ AWURADE anim: bɔne ho afɔre nen. 25Na ɔsɔfo no mfa ne nsatea mfa bɔne ho afɔre no mogya no bi nkeka ɔhyew afɔremuka no mmɛn ho, na onhwie ne mogya no ngu ɔhyew afɔremuka no ase. 26Na ɔnhyew ne srade nyinaa wɔ ɔhyew afɔremuka no so sɛ asomdwoe afɔre srade no; na ɔsɔfo no mpata mma no, ne bɔne no ho, na wɔde bɛkyɛ no.
Ɔmanfo no
27Na sɛ asase no so nkurɔfo no mu biara anhyɛ da na ɔyɛ nneɛma a AWURADE ahyɛ sɛ wɔnnyɛ no mu ade biako, na odi so, na sɛ wɔma ohu ne bɔne a wayɛ a, 28ɛnne, ne bɔne a wayɛ no nti, ɔmfa n'ayɛyɛde, abirekyibere a odi mu mmra mmɛma; 29na ɔmfa ne nsa nto bɔne ho afɔre no atifi, na onkum bɔne ho afɔre no, nea wokum ɔhyew afɔre hɔ. 30Na ɔsɔfo no mfa ne nsatea nka mogya no bi nkeka ɔhyew afɔremuka no mmɛn ho, na onhwie ne mogya nyinaa ngu ɔhyew afɔremuka no ase. 31 Na onyi ɛho srade sɛnea woyi asomdwoe afɔre de no, na ɔsɔfo no nhyew wɔ ɔhyew afɔremuka no so, na enyi hua huamhuam mma AWURADE; na ɔsɔfo no mpata mma no, na wɔde bɛkyɛ no.
32Na sɛ ɔde oguammaa bɛyɛ n'ayɛyɛde aba abɛbɔ bɔne ho afɔre a, ɔmfa ɔbere a odi mu mmra; 33na ɔmfa ne nsa nto bɔne ho afɔre no atifi, na onkum no nyɛ bɔne ho afɔre, nea wokum ɔhyew afɔre hɔ. 34Na ɔsɔfo no mfa ne nsatea nka bɔne ho afɔre no mogya no bi nkeka ɔhyew afɔremuka no mmɛn ho, na onhwie mogya no nyinaa ngu afɔremuka no ase. 35Na onyi ne srade nyinaa, sɛnea woyi asomdwoe afɔre guammaa ho srade no, na ɔsɔfo no nhyew wɔ afɔremuka no so, sɛnea AWURADE gya afɔrebɔ te no; na ɔsɔfo no mpata mma no, ne bɔne a wayɛ no ho, na wɔde bɛkyɛ no.

english_text:
The Lord said:
1If you refuse to testify in court about something you saw or know has happened, you have sinned and can be punished.
2You are guilty and unfit to worship me, if you accidentally touch the dead body of any kind of unclean animal.
3You are guilty if you find out that you have accidentally touched anything unclean that comes from a human body.
4You are guilty the moment you realize that you have made a hasty promise to do something good or bad.
5As soon as you discover that you have committed any of these sins, you must confess what you have done. 6Then you must bring a female sheep or goat to me as the price for your sin. A priest will sacrifice the animal, and you will be forgiven.
7If you are poor and cannot afford to bring an animal, you may bring two doves or two pigeons. One of these will be a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness, and the other will be a sacrifice to please me.
8Give both birds to the priest, who will offer one as a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness. He will wring its neck without tearing off its head, 9splatter some of its blood on one side of the bronze altar, and drain out the rest at the foot of the altar. 10Then he will follow the proper rules for offering the other bird as a sacrifice to please me.
You will be forgiven when the priest offers these sacrifices as the price for your sin.
11If you are so poor that you cannot afford doves or pigeons, you may bring one kilogram of your finest flour. This is a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness, so don't sprinkle olive oil or sweet-smelling incense on it. 12Give the flour to a priest, who will scoop up a handful and send it up in smoke together with the other offerings. This is a reminder that all of the flour belongs to me. 13By offering this sacrifice, the priest pays the price for any of these sins you may have committed. The priest gets to keep the rest of the flour, just as he does with grain sacrifices.
Sacrifices To Make Things Right
(Leviticus 7.1-10)
14-15The Lord told Moses what the people must do to make things right when they find out they have cheated the Lord without meaning to:
If this happens, you must either sacrifice a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay the price of a ram with the official money used by the priests. 16In addition, you must pay what you owe plus a fine of 20 percent. Then the priest will offer the ram as a sacrifice to make things right, and you will be forgiven.
17-19If you break any of my commands without meaning to, you are still guilty, and you can be punished. When you realize what you have done, you must either bring to the priest a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay him for one. The priest will then offer it as a sacrifice to make things right, and you will be forgiven.
translation_text:
Bɔne ahorow ho afɔrebɔ
1 Na sɛ obi yɛ bɔne sɛ wato ntanka bi na ɔne ɛho dansefo, sɛ ohui oo, ɔtee oo, na wanka a, ɔbɛsoa ne mmusu; 2 anaasɛ sɛ obi ka afide biara, sɛ aboa bi a ne ho ntew funu, anaa afieboa bi a ne ho ntew funu, anaa aboaa bi a ne ho ntew funu, na onnim mpo a, ne ho agu fi, na odi so; 3anaasɛ sɛ ɔka onipa ho fi bi, na sɛ afide a ama onii ko ho agu fi no te dɛn ara, na onnim mpo a, sɛ akyi no ohu a, odi so.
4Sɛ asɛnhunu fi onipa anom anaasɛ ɔka ntam sɛ ɔbɛyɛ bɔne anaa papa bi, na onnim mpo a, sɛ akyi no n'ani ba ne ho so a, odi ade yi mu biara ho so; 5na afei, sɛ odi ade yi mu biara ho so a, ɔnka nea wayɛ mu bɔne no, 6na ne bɔne a wayɛ no nti, ɔmfa n'asodi ho afɔre mmrɛ AWURADE, nguan mu ɔbere, oguanten anaa abirekyi, na ɛnyɛ bɔne ho afɔre, na ɔsɔfo no mpata mma no wɔ ne bɔne no ho.
7Na sɛ ne nsa anso oguan so a, ɔmfa nturukuku abien anaa mmorɔnoma mma abien mmrɛ AWURADE mmɛyɛ bɔne a wayɛ no mu asodi ho afɔre; biako nyɛ bɔne ho afɔre, na biako nyɛ ɔhyew afɔre. 8 Na ɔmfa mmrɛ ɔsɔfo no, na ɔmfa nea ɛyɛ bɔne ho afɔre no kan, na onkyim ne ti, nanso ɔnntew mmfi so; 9na ɔmfa bɔne ho afɔre no mogya no bi mpete afɔremuka no ho, na mogya no nkae no, ɔmfa ngu ɔhyew afɔremuka no ase: bɔne ho afɔre ne no. 10 Na nea ɔto so abien no, ɔmfa no mmɔ ɔhyew afɔre, sɛnea ne yɛbea te. Na ɔsɔfo no mpata mma no wɔ ne bɔne a wayɛ no ho, na wɔde bɛkyɛ no. 11 Na sɛ ne nsa anso nturukuku abien anaa mmorɔnoma mma abien so a, nea ɔmfa nyɛ ne bɔne a ɔyɛe ho ayɛyɛde ne asikresam olonka abupɛn du mu biako, na ɛnyɛ bɔne ho afɔre; ɔmmfa ngo nngu so, na ɔmmfa ohuamfufu nnto so, efisɛ ɛyɛ bɔne ho afɔre. 12Na ɔmfa mmrɛ ɔsɔfo no, na ɔsɔfo no mfa mu nsa ma nyɛ nkae ade, na ɔnhyew wɔ afɔremuka no so, sɛnea AWURADE gya afɔrebɔ te no; bɔne ho afɔre ne no. 13 Na ɔsɔfo no mpata mma no, ne bɔne a wayɛ nneɛma yi biara mu no ho, na wɔde befiri no; na nkae no nyɛ ɔsɔfo no de, sɛ aduan afɔre.
Asodi ho afɔre
14Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 15Sɛ obi anhyɛ da na ɔyɛ bɔne a ɛyɛ kusumdi AWURADE akronkronne ho a, ɛnne n'asodi afɔre a ɔmfa mmrɛ AWURADE ne odwennini a odi mu, sɛnea wobɛbɔ ne bo, dwetɛ nnwetɛbona mu, sɛnea kronkronbea dwetɛbona te; na ɛnyɛ asodi ho afɔre. 16 Na nea wayɛ ho bɔne, akronkronne mu no, onsi ananmu, na ɔmfa mu abupɛn anum mu biako mpae so, na ɔmfa mmrɛ ɔsɔfo no, na ɔsɔfo no mfa asodi ho afɔre dwennini no mpata mma no, na wɔde bɛkyɛ no. 17Na sɛ obi yɛ bɔne wɔ nneɛma a AWURADE ahyɛ sɛ wɔnnyɛ no mu ade biako a, sɛ wanhu mpo a, odi so na ɔso ne mmusu; 18na ɔmfa odwennini a odi mu mmrɛ ɔsɔfo no, sɛnea wɔbɛbɔ ne bo, na ɛnyɛ asodi ho afɔre; na ɔsɔfo no mpata mma no, ɔfom a wafom na wanhu no ho, na wɔde bɛkyɛ no. 19 Asodi ho afɔre ne no; AWURADE ho so na wadi.

english_text:
Other Sins That Need Sacrifices or Payments
(Numbers 5.5-10)
1-3 The Lord told Moses what the people must do when they commit other sins against the Lord:
You have sinned if you rob or cheat someone, if you keep back money or valuables left in your care, or if you find something and claim not to have it.
4When this happens, you must return what doesn't belong to you 5and pay the owner a fine of 20 percent. 6-7In addition, you must either bring to the priest a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay him for one. The priest will then offer it as a sacrifice to make things right, and you will be forgiven for what you did wrong.
Daily Sacrifices
(Exodus 29.38-43; Numbers 28.1-8)
8-9The Lord told Moses to tell Aaron and his sons how to offer the daily sacrifices that are sent up in smoke to please the Lord:
You must put the animal for the sacrifice on the altar in the evening and let it stay there all night. But make sure the fire keeps burning. 10The next morning you will dress in your priestly clothes, including your linen underwear. Then clean away the ashes left by the sacrifices and pile them beside the altar. 11Change into your everyday clothes, take the ashes outside the camp, and pile them in the special place.
12The fire must never go out, so put wood on it each morning. After this, you are to lay an animal on the altar next to the fat that you sacrifice to ask my blessing. Then send it all up in smoke to me.
13The altar fire must always be kept burning—it must never go out.
Sacrifices To Give Thanks to the Lord
The Lord said:
14When someone offers a sacrifice to give thanks to me, the priests from Aaron's family must bring it to the front of the bronze altar, 15where one of them will scoop up a handful of the flour and oil, together with all the incense on it. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, he will lay all of this on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 16-17The rest of it is to be baked without yeast and eaten by the priests in the sacred courtyard of the sacred tent. This bread is very holy, just like the sacrifices for sin or the sacrifices for making things right, and I have given this part to the priests from what is offered to me on the altar.
18Only the men in Aaron's family are allowed to eat this bread, and they must go through a ceremony to be made holy before touching it. This law will never change.
When Priests Are Ordained
19The Lord spoke to Moses 20and told him what sacrifices the priests must offer on the morning and evening of the day they are ordained:
It is the same as the regular morning and evening sacrifices—half a kilogram of flour 21mixed with olive oil and cooked in a shallow pan. The bread must then be crumbled into small pieces and sent up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 22-23Each of Aaron's descendants who is ordained as a priest must perform this ceremony and make sure that the bread is completely burned on the altar. None of it may be eaten!
Sacrifices for Sin
(Leviticus 4.1,2)
24The Lord told Moses 25how the priests from Aaron's family were to offer the sacrifice for sin:
This sacrifice is very sacred, and the animal must be killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar. 26The priest who offers this sacrifice must eat it in the sacred courtyard of the sacred tent, 27and anyone or anything that touches the meat will be holy. If any of the animal's blood is splattered on the clothes of the priest, they must be washed in a holy place. 28If the meat was cooked in a clay pot, the pot must be destroyed, but if it was cooked in a bronze pot, the pot must be scrubbed and rinsed with water.
29This sacrifice is very holy, and only the priests may have any part of it. 30None of the meat may be eaten from the sacrifices for sin that require blood to be brought into the sacred tent. These sacrifices must be completely burned.
translation_text:
Ɔhyew afɔrebɔ ho mmara
1Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 2Sɛ obi yɛ bɔne di AWURADE kusum sɛ ɔsan ne yɔnko ade bi a ɔde ama no asie anaasɛ ɔde ahyɛ ne nsa, anaasɛ ɔbɔ korɔn, anaasɛ odi ne yɔnko amim, 3anaasɛ wahu biribi a ayera, na ɔsan, na ɔka ntanhunu, sɛ onipa yɛ eyinom biara mu bɔne, 4 na sɛ ɛba sɛ wayɛ bɔne na odi so saa a, ɔmfa ade a owiae, anaa ade a odii mu amim, anaa ade a wɔde maa no asie, anaa ade a ɛyerae a ohui, 5 anaa ade biara a ɔkaa ho ntanhunu no nsan mmra, ɔmfa ne nyinaa mmra, na ɔmfa abupɛn anum mu biako mpae so mma ɔdede, n'asodi ho afɔrebɔ da no ara; 6 na ɔmfa n'asodi ho afɔre a ɔde rebrɛ AWURADE no mmrɛ ɔsɔfo no, nguan mu dwennini a odi mu, sɛnea wɔbɛbɔ ne bo, na ɛnyɛ asodi ho afɔre. 7Na ɔsɔfo no mpata mma no wɔ AWURADE anim, na wɔde ade biara a wayɛ a odi ho so no bɛkyɛ no.
Ɔhyew afɔre ho mmara
8Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 9 Hyɛ Aaron ne ne mma no sɛ: Eyi ne ɔhyew afɔre ho mmara, ɔhyew afɔre no ntena asammorofi, afɔremuka no so anadwo mu nyinaa nkosi anɔpa, na wɔmma afɔremuka no so gya no nnɛw wɔ so. 10 Na ɔsɔfo no nhyɛ ne nwera atade, na ɔnhyɛ ne nwera twakoto nkata ne ho, na ɔnsesaw nso a ɔhyew afɔre gya no hyew gyawee afɔremuka no so no ngu afɔremuka no nkyɛn. 11 Na onyi ne ntade no, na ɔnhyɛ ntade foforo, na ɔmfa nso no mfi nkɔ nsra no akyi nkogu nea ɛhɔ tew. 12Na wɔmma afɔremuka so gya no nnɛw, ennnum ara da, na ɔsɔfo no nsɔ mmabaa wɔ so daa anɔpa, na onsiesie ɔhyew afɔre no wɔ so, na ɔnhyew so asomdwoe afɔre ho srade no. 13Ogya nnɛw afɔremuka no so daa, ennnum da.
14 Na eyi ne aduan afɔre ho mmara: Aaron mma no mfa mmra AWURADE anim wɔ afɔremuka no anim. 15Na ɔmfa aduan afɔre no asikresam no nsa ma, ne ngo no bi ne aduan afɔre no so huamfufu nyinaa, na ɔnhyew wɔ afɔremuka no so, na enyi hua huamhuam nyɛ nkae ade mma AWURADE. 16Na nkae no, Aaron ne ne mma no nni no apiti, wonni no nea ɛhɔ yɛ kronkron, ahyiae ntamadan no adiwo na wonni. 17Wɔmmfa mmɔkaw mmfra nnto; wɔn kyɛfa a mede mama wɔn wɔ me gya afɔre mu ne no; ɛyɛ akronkronne mu ade kronkron, sɛ bɔne ho afɔre ne asodi ho afɔre. 18Aaron mma mu mmarima nyinaa nni; ɛnyɛ AWURADE gya afɔre horow ho daa ahyɛde, mo awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu; obiara a ɔka no nyɛ kronkron.
19Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 20 Eyi ne Aaron ne ne mma ayɛyɛde a wɔmfa mmrɛ AWURADE, ɛda a wɔsra no ngo no, asikresam olonka abupɛn du mu biako nyɛ daa ayɛyɛde, anɔpa de fa na anwummere de fa. 21Wɔmfa ngo nkyew wɔ dadesanka mu; yɛ no nkyewa bra; yɛ no sɛ aduan afɔre a wɔatoto abubu mu asinasin bra, na enyi hua huamhuam mma AWURADE. 22Na ɔsɔfo a wɔbɛsra no ngo asi n'ananmu wɔ ne mma mu no na ɔnyɛ; ɛyɛ AWURADE daa ahyɛde; wɔnhyew no mu. 23Na ɔsɔfo no aduan afɔre nyinaa wɔnhyew no mu; wonnni bi.
Bɔne afɔre ho mmara
24Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: 25 Kasa kyerɛ Aaron ne ne mma no sɛ Eyi ne bɔne ho afɔre ho mmara: Nea wokum ɔhyew afɔre aboa no, ɛhɔ ara na wonkum bɔne ho afɔre de no, AWURADE anim; akronkronne mu adekronkron ne no. 26Ɔsɔfo a ɔbɔ bɔne ho afɔre no na onni; nea ɛhɔ yɛ kronkron na wonni wɔ ahyiae ntamadan no adiwo. 27Obiara a ɔka nam no nyɛ kronkron; na nea mogya no bi apete n'atade mu no nhoro nea ɛpetee mu no wɔ nea ɛhɔ yɛ kronkron. 28Na ahina a wɔnoae wɔ mu no, wɔmmɔ, na sɛ kɔbere sɛn mu na wɔnoae a, wontwiw mu na wɔmfa nsu nhohoro mu. 29Mmarima a wofi asɔfo abusua kuw mu nyinaa nni bi; ɛyɛ akronkronne mu adekronkron. 30Na bɔne ho afɔre a wɔde ne mogya no bi ba ahyiae ntamadan mu bɛpata wɔ kronkronbea hɔ nyinaa, wonnni; wɔmfa ogya nhyew.

english_text:
Sacrifices To Make Things Right
(Leviticus 5.14-19)
The Lord said:
1The sacrifice to make things right is very sacred. 2The animal must be killed in the same place where the sacrifice to please me is killed, and the animal's blood must be splattered against the four sides of the bronze altar. 3Offer all of the animal's fat, including the fat on its tail and on its insides, 4as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 5One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke to me. 6This sacrifice for making things right is very holy. Only the priests may eat it, and they must eat it in a holy place.
7The ceremony for this sacrifice and the one for sin are the same, and the meat may be eaten only by the priest who performs this ceremony of forgiveness.
8In fact, the priest who offers a sacrifice to please me may keep the skin of the animal, 9just as he may eat the bread from a sacrifice to give thanks to me. 10All other grain sacrifices—with or without olive oil in them—are to be divided equally among the priests of Aaron's family.
Sacrifices To Ask the Lord's Blessing
The Lord said:
11Here are the instructions for offering a sacrifice to ask my blessing: 12If you offer it to give thanks, you must offer some bread together with it. Use the finest flour to make three kinds of bread without yeast—two in the form of loaves mixed with olive oil and one in the form of thin wafers brushed with oil. 13You must also make some bread with yeast. 14Give me one loaf or wafer from each of these four kinds of bread, after which they will belong to the priest who splattered the blood against the bronze altar.
15When you offer an animal to ask a blessing from me or to thank me, the meat belongs to you, but it must be eaten the same day. 16It is different with the sacrifices you offer when you make me a promise or voluntarily give me something. The meat from those sacrifices may be kept and eaten the next day, 17-18but any that is left over must be destroyed. If you eat any of it after the second day, your sacrifice will be useless and unacceptable, and you will be both disgusting and guilty.
19Don't eat any of the meat that has touched something unclean. Instead, burn it. The rest of the meat may be eaten by anyone who is clean and acceptable to me. 20-21But don't eat any of this meat if you have become unclean by touching something unclean from a human or an animal or from any other creature. If you do, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
22The Lord told Moses 23to say to the people:
Don't eat the fat of cattle, sheep, or goats. 24If one of your animals dies or is killed by some wild animal, you may do anything with its fat except eat it. 25If you eat the fat of an animal that can be used as a sacrifice to me, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel. 26 And no matter where you live, you must not eat the blood of any bird or animal, 27or you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
28The Lord also told Moses 29-30to say to the people of Israel:
If you want to offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, you must bring the part to be burned and lay it on the bronze altar. But you must first lift up the choice ribs with their fat to show that the offering is dedicated to me. 31A priest from Aaron's family will then send the fat up in smoke, but the ribs belong to the priests. 32-33The upper joint of the right hind leg is for the priest who offers the blood and the fat of the animal. 34I have decided that the people of Israel must always give the choice ribs and the upper joint of the right hind leg to Aaron's descendants 35who have been ordained as priests to serve me. 36This law will never change. I am the Lord!
37These are the ceremonies for sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessing or his forgiveness, as well as the ceremonies for those sacrifices that demand a payment and for the sacrifices that are offered when priests are ordained. 38While Moses and the people of Israel were in the desert at Mount Sinai, the Lord commanded them to start offering these sacrifices.
translation_text:
Asodi afɔrebɔ ho mmara
1 Na eyi ne asodi ho afɔre ho mmara; ɛyɛ akronkronne mu ade kronkron. 2 Nea wokum ɔhyew afɔre aboa no, ɛhɔ ara na wonkum asodi ho afɔre no nso; na onhwie ne mogya mpete afɔremuka no so nhyia. 3Na onyi ne srade nyinaa mmra: ne sradedua, ne srade a ɛkata ayamde ho no, 4 ne asaabo abien, ne srade a ɛwɔ ho, sisia mu no, ne mmerɛbo so ntontan, omfi asaabo ho nyi; 5Na ɔsɔfo no nhyew ne nyinaa afɔremuka no so nyɛ AWURADE gya afɔre: asodi ho afɔre ne no. 6Mmarima a wofi asɔfo abusuakuw mu nyinaa nni; nea ɛhɔ yɛ kronkron na wonni; ɛyɛ akronkronne mu ade kronkron. 7Sɛ bɔne ho afɔre te no, sɛ asodi ho afɔre nso te ne no, mmara koro na ɛda ho; ɔsɔfo a ɔde pata no, ɛnyɛ ne dea. 8 Na ɔsɔfo a ɔbɔ ɔhyew afɔre ma obi no, ɔhyew afɔre a ɔbɔe no nhoma nyɛ ɔsɔfo no dea. 9 Na aduan afɔre a wɔto fononoo mu nyinaa, ne nea wosiesie no kutu mu ne kyew dade so nyinaa, ɔsɔfo a ɔde ba no na ɛnyɛ ne dea. 10Na aduan afɔre a wɔagu so ngo anaa nea ɛyɛ wosee nyɛ Aaron mma nyinaa de, obiara nnya sɛnea ne yɔnko nya.
Asomdwoe afɔre
11 Na eyi ne asomdwoe afɔre a wɔbɔ ma AWURADE no ho mmara. 12 Sɛ wɔyɛ no aseda afɔre de ba a, aseda afɔre a ɔde ba no nyɛ apiti tetare a wɔde ngo afɔtɔw, ne apiti fam a wɔde ngo agu so ne asikresam tetare a wɔde ngo afɔtɔw akyew. 13Mmɔkaw abodoo tetare na ɔmfa nka n'ayɛyɛde ne n'asomdwoe aseda afɔre no ho mmra. 14Na ɔmfa ayɛyɛde no mu biara biako mmra, na wɔmma so mma AWURADE, ɔsɔfo a ɔde asomdwoe afɔre mogya petee no na ɛnyɛ ne dea. 15 Na n'asomdwoe aseda afɔre no nam no, wonni no da a wɔde bae no ara, wonnnyaw bi nnkosi adekyee. 16Na sɛ n'ayɛyɛde no yɛ bɔhyɛ anaa ayamye ayɛyɛde a, wonni no da a ɔbɔ n'afɔre no, na sɛ ade kye bi so a, wonni ara; 17na afɔre no nam a ɛbɛka akosi da a ɛto so abiɛsa no, wɔmfa ogya nhyew. 18Na sɛ obi di n'asomdwoe afɔre nam no bi da a ɛto so abiɛsa no a, ɛrensɔ ani, na wɔremmu mma nea ɔde bae no, ɛyɛ akyide, na ɔkra a obedi bi no bɛsoa ne mmusu. 19Na nam a aka biribi a ɛho ntew no, wonnni; wɔmfa ogya nhyew. Na nam no de, obiara a ne ho tew nni bi. 20Na ɔkra a obedi asomdwoe afɔre a ɛyɛ AWURADE dea no nam no bi na n'afide da no so no, wobetwa saa ɔkra no afi ne man mu akyene. 21Na ɔkra bi a ɔbɛka afide biara, onipa ho afide bi oo, aboa a ne ho ntew oo, akyide biara a ɛho ntew oo, na obedi AWURADE asomdwoe afɔre nam no bi no, wobetwa saa ɔkra no afi ne man mu akyene.
Mogya ne srade ho akyiwade
22Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ 23 Kasa kyerɛ Israelfo sɛ Nantwi ne oguanten ne abirekyi srade biara, munnni. 24 Na aboa funu srade ne nea wɔatetew no srade, wɔmfa nyɛ adwuma biara, na odi na munnni. 25Na obiara a obedi afieboa a wɔde bi bɛbɔ AWURADE gya afɔre srade no, wobetwa ɔkra a odi no afi ne man mu akyene. 26 Na mogya biara nso, anomaa de oo, atɔteboa de oo, munnni, mo tenabea biara mu; 27ɔkra biara a obedi mogya biara no, wobetwa saa ɔkra no afi ne man mu akyene.
28Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ 29Kasa kyerɛ Israelfo sɛ Nea ɔbɛbɔ n'asomdwoe afɔre ama AWURADE no, ɔmfa n'asomdwoe afɔre no mu ayɛyɛde mmrɛ AWURADE. 30 N'ankasa ne nsa na ɔmfa nso AWURADE gya afɔre no mu mmra, srade ne ɔyan na ɔmfa mmra; ɔyan no, wonhim nyɛ ohim afɔre AWURADE anim. 31Na ɔsɔfo no nhyew srade no, afɔremuka no so, na ɔyan no nyɛ Aaron ne ne mma dea. 32 Na ɔsrɛ nifa no, momfa nyɛ mo asomdwoe afɔre mu soma afɔrebɔde mma ɔsɔfo no. 33Aaron mma mu nea ɔde asomdwoe afɔre mogya ne srade ba no, ɔno na ɔsrɛ nifa no nyɛ ne kyɛfa. 34Na ohim yan ne ɛsoma srɛ no na mafa, Israelfo asomdwoe afɔre no mu, na mede mama ɔsɔfo Aaron ne ne mma sɛ wɔn daa kyɛfa a efi Israelfo nsam.
35Eyi ne Aaron kyɛfa ne ne mma kyɛfa a efi AWURADE gya afɔre mu, ɛda a wɔde wɔn bae sɛ wommedi AWURADE asɔfo, 36na AWURADE hyɛe sɛ wɔmfa mma wɔn, ɛda a wɔsraa wɔn ngo fii Israelfo mu, sɛ ɛnyɛ wɔn daa kyɛfa, wɔn awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu no. 37 Eyi ne mmara a ɛda hɔ ma ɔhyew afɔre ne aduan afɔre ne bɔne ho afɔre ne asodi ho afɔre ne nsamhyɛ afɔre ne asomdwoe afɔre 38a AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose, Sinai bepɔw so, ɛda a ɔhyɛɛ Israelfo sɛ wɔmfa wɔn ayɛyɛde mmrɛ AWURADE, Sinai sare so no.

english_text:
The Ceremony for Ordaining Priests
(Exodus 29.1-37)
1The Lord said to Moses:
2Send for Aaron and his sons, as well as their priestly clothes, the oil for ordination, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and a basket of bread made without yeast. 3Then bring the whole community of Israel together at the entrance to the sacred tent.
4Moses obeyed the Lord, and when everyone had come together, 5he said, “We are here to follow the Lord's instructions.”
6After Moses told Aaron and his sons to step forward, he told them to wash themselves. 7He put the priestly shirt and robe on Aaron and wrapped the sash around his waist. Then he put the sacred vest on Aaron and fastened it with the finely woven belt. 8Next, he put on Aaron the sacred breastpiece that was used in finding out what the Lord wanted his people to do. 9He placed the turban on Aaron's head, and on the front of the turban was the narrow strip of thin gold as a sign of his dedication to the Lord.
10Moses then dedicated the sacred tent and everything in it to the Lord by sprinkling them with some of the oil for ordination. 11He sprinkled the bronze altar seven times, and he sprinkled its equipment, as well as the large bronze bowl and its base. 12He also poured some of the oil on Aaron's head to dedicate him to the Lord. 13Next, Moses dressed Aaron's sons in their shirts, then tied sashes around them and put special caps on them, just as the Lord had commanded.
14Moses led out the bull that was to be sacrificed for sin, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head. 15After it was killed, Moses dipped a finger in the blood and smeared some of it on each of the four corners of the bronze altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the altar. This purified the altar and made it a fit place for offering the sacrifice for sin. 16Moses then took the fat on the bull's insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and sent them up in smoke on the altar fire. 17Finally, he took the skin and the flesh of the bull, together with the food still in its stomach, and burned them outside the camp, just as the Lord had commanded.
18Moses led out the ram for the sacrifice to please the Lord. After Aaron and his sons had laid their hands on its head, 19Moses killed the ram and splattered its blood against the four sides of the altar. 20-21Moses had the animal cut up, and he washed its insides and hind legs. Then he laid the head, the fat, and the rest of the ram on the altar and sent them up in smoke with a smell that pleased the Lord. All this was done just as the Lord had commanded.
22Moses led out the ram for the ceremony of ordination. Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head, 23and it was killed. Moses smeared some of its blood on Aaron's right earlobe, some on his right thumb, and some on the big toe of his right foot. 24Moses did the same thing for Aaron's sons, before splattering the rest of the blood against the four sides of the altar. 25He took the animal's fat tail, the fat on its insides, and the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and the right hind leg. 26Then he took from a basket some of each of the three kinds of bread that had been made without yeast and had been dedicated to the Lord.
